9.DDetailed specification

This section specifies how C03, the joint reservation authority, turns a booking intent into a held and then committed bundle of vehicle, seat, cargo, bay, charge and work-slot capacity: the inputs it relies on, the order in which constraints are applied, how the timing of one vehicle, one bay and one charging session is coordinated, how reservation states change and what each state holds, and how amendments replace an allocation without ever leaving a booking uncovered. It elaborates the constraint propagation sequence (D09.1), the atomic replacement sequence (D09.2) and the transition table (D09.3), and the C03 functional view in Appendix B (C03).

9.D.1 Purpose and scope

Feasibility in this service is joint: a passenger trip is only deliverable if the vehicle can reach the pickup, the seats and accessible space are free on every segment, any inserted cargo fits, the vehicle can be turned around, cleaned and inspected, it holds enough energy for the trip and the next one, and the bay and charge port it needs are free when it needs them. C03 is the single place where these conditions are checked together and where capacity is allocated, so that no other component can promise capacity that C03 has not reserved.

In scope: the C03 decomposition into candidate generation, hard constraint evaluation, energy envelope, ranking and the D2 transaction; resource timing and the departure guard; reservation states; amendment by atomic replacement. Out of scope: the booking saga and cancellation as seen from C02 (P11), the energy scheduler inside C05 (P12), hub and replenishment capacity planning (P25–P26), and the detailed sharing rules (P29–P30), which this chapter applies but does not define.

9.D.2 Actors and responsibilities

ActorResponsibility
C02 BookingSends plan requests, holds, commit intents and amendments over I03; persists COMMIT_PENDING and the intent before committing; finalises D1 by compare-and-set (BKG-024, BKG-046)
Candidate generatorExpands an F01 intent into F02 candidates: vehicles and sites that can serve the location, compatible pools and tour insertions, site and work-slot joins (BKG-002)
Hard constraint evaluatorAccepts or rejects each candidate on ODD, seats, payload, cargo space, per-segment capacity, every accepted passenger limit and delivery / energy limits; emits a feasible bundle or a binding reason (BKG-003, BKG-006)
C05 energy envelopeSupplies the site's kW limit, charging efficiency, arrival / next-trip / reserve energy terms and its capabilityRev and age (BKG-007)
Feasible-plan rankingOrders feasible bundles by weighted empty km, wait, cost and risk; retains normalised terms and the reason (BKG-009)
D2 transactionAllocates the selected bundle under ordered locks with exclusive and pooled capacity checks; commits the outbox atomically (BKG-016, BKG-017)
C04 / vehicle, C05 / EMSReport execution and clearance; old physical capacity is released only on their clearance (BKG-039)

9.D.3 Preconditions and inputs

Demand / policy
Passenger and cargo time windows; party, access needs, mass and volume; allowed detour, handling and consent; the policy version and snapshot time under which the request is evaluated (BKG-001). The policy version is recorded on the bundle so that a later review can re-evaluate the decision under the same rules.
Resource snapshot
Intervals and revisions read from D2 for every resource a candidate touches, plus Resource / Capability records whose availability is supported by current evidence (PLT-036).
Energy capability
Read from C05 for a site, window and minimum energy; returned with limits, capabilityRev and age. Its revision is independent of the resource snapshot's revisions (BKG-008).
Freshness
Capability and vehicle / site evidence older than its freshness budget is not used; the affected capacity is blocked (PLT-024). The budgets are a G2 decision (TBD-006).

9.D.4 Behaviour

Main flow — feasibility and hold (D09.1):

  1. C02 sends the plan request with terms and windows over I03.
  2. C03 reads the D2 resource revisions and, in parallel, the C05 energy capability for the candidate sites and windows.
  3. The candidate generator produces F02 candidates. For a shared ride or cargo insertion it proposes insertion positions in existing tours rather than only new tours.
  4. The hard constraint evaluator checks every candidate. For an insertion, it recomputes the pickup, arrival and detour of every passenger already on the tour and keeps each accepted limit binding (BKG-005). Seats, accessible space, payload and cargo volume are checked on each segment, not on the tour as a whole (BKG-004).
  5. Energy feasibility is checked against the C05 envelope and the departure guard (9.D.6).
  6. If no candidate survives, C03 returns REJECTED with the binding reason and an alternative where one exists (BKG-022).
  7. Surviving bundles are ranked; the selected plan carries its resource revision set.
  8. The D2 transaction locks the resources in order, checks that their revisions match the snapshot, runs exclusive and pooled capacity checks, and commits an expiring HELD bundle with its outbox entry (BKG-020).
  9. C03 returns the hold with its expiry; C02 presents the offer with that expiry.

Main flow — commit. On acceptance, C02 rejects expired or changed input, otherwise persists COMMIT_PENDING, the intent and the outbox in D1 and sends the commit (BKG-024). C03 promotes the hold; where an external energy reservation is needed it is requested from C05 with outcome accept, reject or unknown (BKG-041). Only an accepted outcome with valid capacity permits the local commit; the bundle becomes CONFIRMED only when verified (BKG-027, BKG-043).

Alternative flow — amendment by atomic replacement (D09.2):

  1. An amendment on a CONFIRMED booking carries new terms; the old allocation stays in force (BKG-035).
  2. C03 plans and holds the new bundle as in the main flow, with shared seats checked as summed capacity per segment including the new bundle (BKG-018).
  3. On acceptance, CommitBundle names both the new and the old bundle and the expected resource revisions; new capacity is held before the old is retired (BKG-036).
  4. If the old allocation has not started, the swap is committed. If the mission has started or its state is unknown, the old occupancy is retained until physical clearance (BKG-037, BKG-038).
  5. Old physical capacity is released only after vehicle / EMS clearance; failed compensation stays owned and reconciled (BKG-039, BKG-045).

Exception flows.

  1. Revision mismatch at hold or commit. A resource revision changed after the snapshot; the transaction fails without effect and the request is re-planned on a fresh snapshot. The user is shown refreshed terms before any further acceptance (SVC-040).
  2. Hold expiry. A HELD bundle that is not accepted before its expiry moves to EXPIRED and its capacity is released (BKG-023).
  3. Outcome unknown. A commit whose outcome cannot be confirmed moves to RECONCILING; the original intent is queried; occupancy stays blocked and the quote TTL does not release it (BKG-025, BKG-026).
  4. Energy rejected or conflicting. Compensation releases old or undoes new capacity as required (BKG-044).
  5. Stale energy capability. The candidate is treated as energy-infeasible with the staleness as binding reason, rather than assumed feasible.

9.D.5 Constraint model

Constraints are split into two classes with different treatment:

  • Hard constraints decide feasibility: ODD; seats, accessible space, payload and cargo volume per segment; every accepted passenger limit (pickup, arrival, detour); delivery windows; handling; consent; energy; resource availability with current evidence. A candidate either satisfies all of them or is rejected with the first binding reason found. Hard constraints are never traded against each other or against cost.
  • Ranking terms order feasible bundles: empty km, wait, cost and risk, normalised so that they are comparable, then weighted. The weights are not set in this document (TBD-032). The normalised terms and the reason for the selection are retained so that an operator can explain why one bundle was chosen over another (SVC-043).

Ranking never relaxes a hard constraint, and ranking never allocates: only the D2 transaction creates an allocation (BKG-010). The separation means that a change of weights can change which feasible plan is chosen, but can never make an infeasible plan acceptable.

Per-segment checking matters for shared rides and cargo: a tour may have a free seat on average while one segment is full. Checking each segment, and summing pooled demand on that segment, prevents an insertion that is feasible on paper from overloading the vehicle between two stops. Loading bays, staff and hub capacity are separate resources reserved in their own right, not implied by the vehicle reservation (BKG-014).

9.D.6 Resource timing and departure guard

The 2.2 timeline coordinates four resources for one vehicle cycle: the vehicle itself, a parking bay, a service bay with its charge port, and service work (clean / inspect). Each reservation is a half-open interval on its resource (PLT-035), so one reservation can end at the instant the next begins without overlap. Exclusive resources (a bay, a charge port) admit no overlapping intervals; pooled resources (seats, staff) admit overlap up to their capacity.

Precedence binds the intervals together: the vehicle cannot leave until every required task — charge to target, cleaning, inspection — has finished; tasks may overlap only where an overlap has been approved (BKG-011). Reposition, wait / charge, passenger trip and turnaround are counted as one vehicle cycle, with empty travel, boarding, cargo dwell and energy counted once (BKG-015).

The electrical branch of the departure guard is the inequality stated in 2.2 (BKG-012). In words: departure energy is arrival energy plus the energy delivered during the charging intervals (AC power times interval length times charging efficiency) minus auxiliary consumption; it must cover the next trip plus the reserve and cannot exceed the usable maximum. Power is in kW, interval lengths in hours and energy in kWh, with conversion losses counted once (ASM-018). The charging power available in each interval comes from the C05 envelope, so a derated site lengthens the charge interval or makes the departure infeasible; it never silently lowers the reserve.

9.D.7 Rules and invariants

  1. R9.1 Only the D2 transaction creates an allocation; one transaction per bundle resource set (BKG-010, BKG-016).
  2. R9.2 All accepted passenger limits remain binding after any insertion (BKG-005).
  3. R9.3 Capacity is checked on every segment; shared seats are summed per segment (BKG-004, BKG-018).
  4. R9.4 The resource snapshot and the energy capability are separate versioned inputs (BKG-008).
  5. R9.5 A hold expires; a PENDING commit does not expire on quote TTL (BKG-023, BKG-025).
  6. R9.6 CONFIRMED requires a verified bundle; IN_SERVICE requires observed execution; COMPLETED requires an observed end with verified actuals (BKG-027, BKG-028).
  7. R9.7 Replacement holds new before retiring old; swaps apply only to unstarted allocations (BKG-036, BKG-037).
  8. R9.8 Started or unknown missions retain occupancy until physical clearance (BKG-038).
  9. R9.9 Shared rides and cargo require segment capacity, a route revision and distinct booking outcomes per passenger and shipment (BKG-013).
  10. R9.10 No distributed atomic commit with EMS or providers is assumed (BKG-019).

9.D.8 Data and state

The reservation states of 2.3 describe what capacity a request holds at each point:

StateCapacity heldLeaves byTime behaviour
REQUESTEDNoneFeasible → HELD; infeasible → REJECTED—
HELDExpiring hold, with resourceRevAccept → COMMIT_PENDING; expiry → EXPIREDExpires at expiresAt

The bundle carries its own revision, expiry, policy version and input snapshot reference, the intent and idempotency key, and its result; intervals carry their reservation revision and allocation state (P10 3.1). A replacement bundle references the bundle it replaces, so the history of an amended booking is a chain of bundles rather than an overwritten one. Cancellation is coordinated through D1 and follows P11.

9.D.9 Interfaces used

  • I03 — C02 → C03: plan, hold, promote, commit / swap, cancel; guarded outcomes COMMITTED / HELD / REJECTED / PENDING.
  • I05 via C05 — capability reads and energy reservations, with accept / reject / unknown outcomes.
  • I04 — C03 → C04: mission commands for confirmed bundles, gated by the D1 permit.
  • C09 — AllocationCommitted from the D2 outbox.

9.D.10 Failure handling and recovery

FailureEffect on capacityRecovery
Concurrent allocation on the same resourceSecond transaction fails its revision checkRe-plan on a fresh snapshot; refresh terms
Lost commit responseOccupancy blocked in COMMIT_PENDINGQuery by intent; idempotency key prevents a second allocation (P24 T-R04)
EMS outcome unknownOccupancy blockedQuery the same planId until resolved or escalated (BKG-042)

Stale vehicle / site stateAffected capacity blockedUnblocked when fresh evidence arrives (P24 T-R01)

9.D.11 Security, privacy and audit

All keys carry the tenant scope, and resource references are validated within it, so one operator's bundle cannot lock another operator's resource (PLT-030). Consent is a hard constraint input: a candidate that needs a signal outside the consent scope is infeasible. Each decision is reconstructable from the bundle's policy version, input snapshot reference, the retained ranking reason and the binding reasons of rejected candidates, which is what the operator workspace needs to explain an infeasibility (SVC-043).

9.D.12 Observability and operations

  • Distribution of binding reasons for rejected requests, by zone and time, to show which constraint limits service.
  • Holds created, expired and promoted, to show offer-to-acceptance behaviour without counting expired holds as demand served.
  • Bundles in COMMIT_PENDING and RECONCILING with their age and owner, and capacity blocked by unknown outcomes or stale evidence.
  • Departure-guard failures by site, separating energy shortage from task precedence.

9.D.13 Verification approach

  • Transition tests — every transition of D09.3 and every forbidden transition (for example, HELD directly to CONFIRMED) is exercised.
  • Concurrency tests — competing holds on the same exclusive resource and on the same pooled segment produce at most capacity, never an overrun.
  • Boundary tests — back-to-back half-open intervals are accepted; any overlap on an exclusive resource is rejected.
  • Insertion tests — inserting a passenger or shipment that would breach an existing passenger's limit on any segment is rejected with that limit as reason.
  • Replacement tests — amendment of an unstarted, started and unknown allocation shows hold-before-retire, swap, and retained occupancy respectively.
  • Energy tests — departure-guard cases at the reserve and at the usable maximum, and with derated or stale capability.
  • Fault tests — lost responses and replayed intents give no duplicate allocation (P24 T-R04); G3 verifies seat / payload limits per segment and route revisions (SVC-068).

9.D.14 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Filter then rank, rather than a single weighted objective. Folding constraints into a penalty would let a large saving outweigh a broken passenger limit. Filtering on hard constraints first keeps accepted limits binding by construction, and makes the ranking weights a commercial choice rather than a safety one.

Hold before commit. Offering without holding risks confirming capacity that has been sold to someone else in the meantime. A short-lived hold makes the offer honest; the expiry bounds how long unused capacity is withheld.

Hold new before retiring old. Releasing first and re-planning second can leave a confirmed passenger with nothing if the new plan fails. Holding both briefly costs capacity but ensures that a failed amendment leaves the existing booking intact.

Blocking under uncertainty. Releasing PENDING capacity on quote TTL would allow double allocation if the commit did succeed. Keeping it blocked until reconciled trades utilisation for correctness.

Ordered locks. Locking a bundle's resources in one deterministic order prevents two concurrent bundles from each holding part of the other's set and waiting indefinitely.

9.D.15 Open points

  • Ranking weights for empty km / wait / cost / risk (TBD-032).
  • Freshness budgets (TBD-006); query budget for unresolved commands (TBD-027).
  • ODD conditions in the G2 constraint register (TBD-011).
  • Shared-ride thresholds and operating authority (TBD-029); cargo eligibility (TBD-047).
  • Cancel / replan of in-flight work depends on vehicle support (TBD-042).

Replay must use separate projections and idempotent effect handlers.
Times
occurredAt and receivedAt are both carried; correlationId links the event to the originating intent.

Source: P10 3.2; P08 1.1; P08 1.2

10.DDetailed specification

This section specifies the domain model and message contracts as a data design: what each entity represents and when it is created, how keys and cardinalities form one unbroken chain from an accepted journey to resource use and settlement, which revision guards each entity relies on for concurrency control, how uniqueness turns retries into idempotent operations, and how commands, results and events are interpreted by their producers and consumers. It elaborates the ownership view (D10.1), the CommitBundle exchange (D10.2) and the inbox decision logic (D10.3); the field dictionary is in the interface control appendix (Appendix D).

10.D.1 Purpose and scope

The model exists so that any question about a journey — what was offered, what the user accepted, which capacity was reserved, which vehicle executed which command, how much energy was planned and delivered, and what was billed — can be answered by following keys, without inference across stores. It also gives every writer the guards it needs to reject stale or duplicated changes in a system where delivery is at least once and external outcomes can be unknown.

In scope: the entities of 3.1, their keys, foreign keys, cardinalities, revision fields and invariants; the I03 CommitBundle command and result; the event envelope used by all domains. Out of scope: storage technology, physical schemas and field types, which are not stated; the complete API schemas, which remain open (TBD-040). The payloads in 3.2 are conceptual examples, not complete schemas (ASM-005).

10.D.2 Entities and their lifecycle

EntityRepresentsCreated whenChanges by
PlanReferenceA consented reference to a user's external plan (calendar or partner event instance)C01 receives a plan from a channel under a consentNew sourceRevision from the source; consent expiry or withdrawal
BookingThe user's journey commitment: terms, rider, pickup window, destination, current bundleC02 normalises an intent (with or without a PlanReference)Compare-and-set on expectedBookingRev; each accepted change raises bookingRev
ResourceBundleOne coherent set of reserved capacity for a bookingC03 holds a feasible planState changes under bundleRev; amendment creates a new bundle that replaces the old
ResourceIntervalUse of one resource over a half-open time interval by one bundleD2 transaction for the bundlereservationRev and allocationState
Resource / CapabilityA vehicle, bay, charger or staff resource with its capacity and constraintsNot stated in this documentNew capabilityRev and status with observedAt
ActivitySaga / WorkOrderA provider activity or service task (cleaning / inspection / handover) linked to a bookingC02 places an activity hold or schedules workconditionsRev, acceptedTermsRev, state, owner, dueAt
Mission / CommandA command to a vehicle with its delivery and execution stateC04 releases a mission for a confirmed bundlemissionRev; status updates ordered by statusSeq
EnergyPlanA revision of the energy plan for a bundle at a siteC05 plans power intervals for a bundleNew planRev; acceptedRev when the site accepts; executionEvidence
UsageFact / LedgerVerified metered usage and the ledger entries derived from itC07 validates actuals under a contractRevCorrection entries referencing correctionOf; never overwritten

PlanReference, Booking, ResourceBundle, ResourceInterval, Mission / Command, EnergyPlan and UsageFact / Ledger each have exactly one writing component (PLT-009). Resource / Capability has no single writing component named in this document; availability is used only when backed by current evidence (PLT-036).

10.D.3 Keys, cardinalities and the trace chain

Every primary key starts with tenantId, and every foreign key includes it (PLT-030, ASM-009). A reference is valid only if the referenced row exists in the same tenant; this is validated by the writer, not assumed from the caller.

  1. PlanReference 0..1 : N Booking. A booking may come from a shared plan or directly from app input; a plan may lead to several bookings (for example, outbound and return).
  2. Booking 1 : N ResourceBundle. A booking has one current bundle (currentBundleId) and a history of bundles linked through replacesBundleId, so amendments are a chain, not an overwrite.
  3. Booking 1 : N ActivitySaga / WorkOrder. Activities and service tasks reference the booking and, where relevant, the bundle.
  4. ResourceBundle 1 : N ResourceInterval; ResourceInterval N : 1 Resource. The bundle's capacity is the set of its intervals; each interval occupies one resource.
  5. ResourceBundle 1 : N Mission / Command, EnergyPlan revisions, UsageFact / Ledger. Execution, energy and settlement all refer back to the bundle, so actual use and cost are attributable to the reservation that caused them.

This chain is the data basis of the journey key chain in the traceability contract (SVC-016): intentId appears on Booking and ResourceBundle, bookingRev on Booking, and the bundle links to the mission. It also supports counting one shared vehicle mission carrying several intents (SVC-012).

10.D.4 Revisions and concurrency control

Each revision field has one meaning and one guard; they are not interchangeable.

bookingRev
Revision of the Booking, owned by D1. Every update is a compare-and-set on expectedBookingRev; a mismatch means another change won and the caller must re-read (PLT-033).
termsRev / acceptedTermsRev
Revision of the offered terms and the revision the user accepted. A commit carries acceptedTermsRev so that a change of terms after acceptance cannot be committed silently.
bundleRev
Revision of the bundle in D2; returned in the result and used as aggregateRevision of AllocationCommitted.
reservationRev
Revision of each resource's reservations; expectedResourceRevs in CommitBundle lists these for the ordered resource set (PLT-040).
capabilityRev
Revision of a resource's or site's capability, including the EMS capability used for energy feasibility; carried separately from resource revisions (BKG-008).
missionRev / statusSeq
Revision of a mission and the sequence of its status reports; old or repeated status cannot overwrite newer state.
planRev / acceptedRev
Revision of an EnergyPlan and the revision accepted by the site; acceptance of a plan revision is not delivered energy (PLT-038, ASM-019).
sourceRevision / sourceRev
Revision as stated by an external source (plan provider, meter); used to detect replays and late corrections from the source.
contractRev / billRev
Contract version applied to usage and revision of the issued bill; a correction raises billRev and leaves the earlier bill traceable.
conditionsRev
Revision of activity conditions on an ActivitySaga; an ETA change re-enters the saga with a new revision (BKG-062).

Optimistic concurrency is used throughout: no writer holds a lock across a user interaction. D2 additionally takes ordered locks inside its own transaction for the duration of the capacity check and commit (BKG-017).

10.D.5 Uniqueness and idempotency

ConstraintProtects againstBehaviour on repeat
PlanReference unique within tenant on provider / account / event / instanceDuplicate plans from calendar resync or repeated deliveryRepeat maps to the existing reference; a new sourceRevision updates it (PLT-031)
ResourceBundle unique on tenant / intent / keyDuplicate allocation from retried commitsSame key + same payload returns the stored result; same key + different payload is rejected with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (PLT-034, PLT-042)
Same commandId: one immutable payloadHashA changed command sent under an old IDChanged payload under the same ID is rejected (PLT-037)
eventId in each consumer's inboxDuplicate effects from at-least-once deliveryDuplicate has no second effect (PLT-015)
Unique earning IDs in settlementDuplicate paymentEach earning carries a unique earning ID; payment and payroll jobs are idempotent (ENE-042, PLT-007)

A retry is always sent with the original key or ID. Generating a new key for a retry would turn an idempotent repeat into a second, independent request and defeat the constraint.

10.D.6 Behaviour

Main flow — CommitBundle (D10.2):

  1. C02 persists COMMIT_PENDING, the intent and the outbox in D1 (BKG-024).
  2. C02 sends CommitBundle with tenantId, intentId, bookingId, expectedBookingRev, newBundleId, oldBundleId, expectedResourceRevs, acceptedTermsRev, capabilityRev and idempotencyKey (PLT-041).
  3. C03 looks up tenant / intent / key. A stored result with an identical payload is returned unchanged; a different payload is rejected with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.
  4. C03 validates every reference within the tenant scope.
  5. C03 takes ordered locks on the resource set and compares current reservation revisions with expectedResourceRevs.
  6. C03 runs exclusive and pooled capacity checks and commits D2 with its outbox.
  7. C03 returns the result: state COMMITTED, bundleId, bundleRev, intentIdForD1, committedAt and externalReleaseJobs (PLT-045).
  8. C02 finalises D1 by compare-and-set and schedules the external release jobs listed in the result.
  9. AllocationCommitted is published with aggregateId = bundleId, aggregateRevision = bundleRev and correlationId = intentId (PLT-020).

Alternative outcomes. HELD, REJECTED and PENDING are returned explicitly with reasonCode and retryability (PLT-043). HELD means capacity is held but not committed; REJECTED is a definite refusal; PENDING means an external effect is unresolved and occupancy stays blocked. The caller retries only where retryability permits, and always with the same intent and key.

Main flow — event consumption (D10.3):

  1. The consumer receives an envelope and checks eventId against its inbox; a known eventId is acknowledged with no effect.
  2. It compares aggregateRevision with the last applied revision for aggregateId.
  3. The next revision is applied and the eventId recorded in the inbox in the same local change.
  4. A gap causes the consumer to fetch the missing revisions before applying.
  5. An event that still cannot be applied is quarantined and an alert raised (PLT-016, PLT-018).

Exception flows.

  1. Lost result. C02 does not receive the CommitBundle result. It does not treat this as a rejection (PLT-044); it re-sends with the same idempotencyKey or queries the original intent. The reservation moves to RECONCILING while the outcome is unknown (BKG-026).
  2. Booking revision conflict at finalise. The D1 compare-and-set fails because the booking changed (for example, a cancel was recorded). C02 re-reads and resolves against the committed allocation; cancellation and permit issuance serialise in D1 (BKG-051).

10.D.7 Rules and invariants

  1. R10.1 Keys and foreign keys include tenantId; references are validated within that scope (PLT-030).
  2. R10.2 D1 owns bookingRev; every Booking update is a compare-and-set (PLT-010, PLT-033).
  3. R10.3 Atomic guarantees cover D2 only; no transaction spans D1 and D2 (PLT-013).
  4. R10.4 Exclusive intervals do not overlap; pooled intervals sum to no more than capacity (PLT-035).
  5. R10.5 An unknown outcome is never a rejection (PLT-044).
  6. R10.6 An EnergyPlan acceptance is not delivered energy (PLT-038).
  7. R10.7 Actuals are never destructively overwritten; corrections reference the corrected entry (PLT-039).
  8. R10.8 Every event carries the full envelope, and correlationId links it to the originating intent (PLT-019, PLT-020).
  9. R10.9 PlanReference stores start and end as UTC with an IANA zone (PLT-032).

10.D.8 Message contract semantics

I03 CommitBundle. intentId names the business intent (here an amendment) and is the unit of idempotency together with idempotencyKey. bookingId with expectedBookingRev states which booking revision the commit was prepared against. newBundleId and oldBundleId express the replacement: the bundle to be committed and the bundle it retires. expectedResourceRevs lists the reservation revisions of the resources in the bundle's ordered resource set, in that order. acceptedTermsRev binds the commit to the terms the user accepted, and capabilityRev to the energy capability used for feasibility.

I03 Result. state is the explicit outcome. bundleId and bundleRev identify the committed allocation. intentIdForD1 is the intent that C02 must finalise in D1, so that the result can be applied even if C02 lost its in-memory context. committedAt is a UTC instant. externalReleaseJobs lists the jobs that release external holds tied to the retired allocation; they run after clearance (BKG-039) and are intended to be idempotent, so that they can be retried.

Event envelope. eventId identifies the event for deduplication; type and schemaVersion tell the consumer how to read the payload; tenantId scopes it; aggregateId and aggregateRevision order it per aggregate; occurredAt is when the change happened at the owner and receivedAt when it was received, both UTC instants, so that freshness and delay can be judged separately; correlationId ties it to the intent that caused it.

10.D.9 Time handling

  • All instants are stored in UTC. Where a local calendar meaning matters (a user's plan), the IANA zone is stored with it so that the local time can be reconstructed across zone rule changes.
  • Intervals are half-open: an interval includes its start and excludes its end, so adjacent reservations do not collide.
  • Observation time (observedAt) is kept distinct from receipt time (receivedAt); availability decisions use the age of the observation, not of its receipt.
  • Validity is explicit: holds and plans carry expiresAt, consents carry expiresAt, commands carry validUntil.

10.D.10 Schema evolution

Every event carries schemaVersion so that consumers can process old and new versions side by side during a change. Revision fields and idempotency keys are part of the contract and are not removed in later versions, because consumers rely on them for ordering and deduplication. The complete schemas, required fields and evolution policy are open (TBD-040).

10.D.11 Failure handling and recovery

FailureDetected byHandling
Retried commandtenant / intent / keyStored result returned; no second allocation
Conflicting retrySame key, different payloadIDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; caller investigates, does not re-key
Stale expectationexpectedBookingRev or expectedResourceRevs mismatchNo effect; re-read and re-plan
Cross-tenant referenceReference validationRejected; nothing written
Duplicate eventInboxNo second effect
Missing eventRevision gapFetch gap, then apply
Unappliable eventApply failure after fetchQuarantine; alert
Wrong actualValidation or later evidenceCorrection entry with correctionOf; new billRev

10.D.12 Security, privacy and audit

Tenant scope in every key makes cross-tenant access a validation failure rather than an access-control afterthought. PlanReference holds a consent reference with purpose and expiry, so personal plan data is used only under its recorded purpose (SVC-001); bookings created from it survive a calendar resync or deletion (BKG-064). The model is append-oriented where audit matters: bundle chains, command journals with immutable payload hashes, plan revisions and correction entries mean that the state at any past point can be reconstructed and every change attributed to its writer and intent.

10.D.13 Verification approach

  • Constraint tests — each uniqueness and interval constraint rejects a violating write (PLT-031, PLT-034, PLT-035).
  • Idempotency tests — the same CommitBundle repeated returns one result; a changed payload under the same key returns IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; a lost result followed by retry leaves one allocation (P24 T-R04).
  • Concurrency tests — two commits with the same expectedBookingRev: exactly one succeeds.
  • Envelope tests — duplicated, reordered and missing events yield one application per revision, a gap fetch, or quarantine.
  • Trace tests — from a UsageFact, the bundle, booking, intent and PlanReference are reachable within the same tenant.
  • Ledger tests — a correction leaves the original entry intact and traceable.

10.D.14 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Tenant in every key. A tenant column checked only by queries is easy to omit. Making it part of every key and foreign key turns isolation into a property of the data.

Revisions rather than timestamps for ordering. Clocks across components and vehicles drift; per-aggregate revisions give a total order per aggregate without relying on clock agreement, while observedAt and receivedAt are kept for freshness.

Bundle chain rather than in-place update. Updating a bundle in place would lose the allocation being replaced while the replacement is still uncertain. A new bundle that references the old keeps both until the swap is finalised.

Explicit outcomes including PENDING. A binary success / failure contract forces callers to guess when an external effect is unresolved. An explicit PENDING with retryability lets the caller block capacity and reconcile instead.

10.D.15 Open points

  • Complete API schemas and required fields (TBD-040); protocols (TBD-003).
  • Contribution weights and versioned deductions under contractRev (TBD-034).
  • Clock bounds and retention parameters (TBD-007); freshness budgets (TBD-006).

11.DDetailed specification

This section specifies the booking saga that turns a customer acceptance into an authoritative dispatch permit: how C02 and D1 own intent and cancellation, how C03 and D2 hold and promote capacity with local atomic changes only, how the external energy effect at C05 / site EMS is requested, resolved or compensated without a distributed commit, and how cancellation and permit issuance are serialised so that no mission is released on an unverified or cancelled booking. It covers the main flow, the reject and unknown branches, cancellation before and after permit issuance, the invariants that hold across all of them, and the evidence used to verify them.

11.D.1 Purpose and scope

The saga in P11 4.1 is the single path by which a quoted journey becomes movement. It exists because three owners with independent stores take part in one customer commitment: C02 owns the booking in D1, C03 owns route, segment, bay and charge capacity in D2, and C05 owns energy plans in D4 on behalf of a site EMS that is outside the platform. None of these stores can be committed atomically with another (PLT-013), so the design replaces a distributed transaction with durable intent, local atomic steps, idempotent external requests and explicit reconciliation.

In scope: quote and amend, the expiring hold, acceptance and intent persistence, hold promotion, the energy reservation and its three outcomes, the local commit or compensation, D1 finalisation, the dispatch-permit gate, and cancellation at any phase. Out of scope and specified elsewhere: candidate generation and constraint evaluation (P09 2.1), the D2 transaction and CommitBundle contract (P10 3.2), mission command delivery and execution (P13 6.1), energy scheduling (P12 5.1) and centre fencing of in-flight work (P20 13.1). Activity holds at external providers follow the same pattern on I06 (P23 16.1) and are not repeated here.

11.D.2 Actors and responsibilities

Actor / containerOwnsResponsibility in the sagaMust not
Client / rider (via C01)Request and acceptanceRequests a quote or amendment with a request identity, accepts a specific terms revision, may cancel at any time.Receive a confirmation before D1 is finalised.
C02 Booking / D1Booking intent, cancellation, bookingRev, saga state, dispatch permit (BKG-040)Validates acceptance against the offer, persists intent with its outbox, drives the commit, records cancellation, finalises by CAS and issues or withholds the permit (Appendix B C02).Write D2 or D4; confirm on an unverified commit (CAP-005).
C03 Planner / D2Holds, bundles, intervals and their revisionsReads resource and energy inputs, creates the expiring HELD bundle, promotes it to PENDING, requests the energy effect, and commits the swap or compensates (Appendix B C03).Release PENDING occupancy on quote TTL; release old physical capacity before clearance.
C05 / Site EMSEnergy capability and plan journal (D4)Answers capability reads with limits, capabilityRev and age; accepts, rejects or leaves unknown a ReserveEnergy request; answers status queries on the same planId (Appendix B C05).Treat a repeated request with the same key as new work.
C04 FleetMission release and in-flight cancel / replanObtains the current D1 permit before releasing a mission; turns a late cancellation into cancel / replan of the in-flight mission (Appendix B C04).Release a mission without a current permit (DSP-001).
C06 OperationsOwned exceptionsReceives unresolved reconciliations and failed compensations as owned cases with owner, deadline and backup (CAP-048).Close a case as a way of releasing capacity.

11.D.3 Preconditions and inputs

  • The request has passed C01 identity, tenant, consent and schema checks (PLT-001), and every key used below carries tenantId (PLT-030).
  • C03 holds a resource snapshot from D2 (intervals and their revisions) and an energy capability from C05 (limits, capabilityRev and age). These are two versioned inputs with independent revisions, never one shared revision (BKG-008); energy feasibility uses the C05 energy envelope including freshness (BKG-007). The freshness limit for capability data is a platform parameter (TBD-006, decided at G2).
  • For an amendment, D1 holds the current booking with its bookingRev and current bundle; the old allocation stays in force until the replacement is finalised (BKG-035).
  • Postcondition of a successful saga: D1 shows CONFIRMED by CAS with no pending cancel, D2 holds the committed bundle, D4 holds the accepted energy plan revision, and a current dispatch permit is available to C04. Postcondition of any other outcome: no current permit exists, and every capacity that may still be physically used remains occupied and owned.

11.D.4 Behaviour

Main flow (quote → hold → accept → commit → permit). Step numbers refer to the sequence in P11 4.1.

  1. The client sends Quote/amend with a request identity (01). C02 forwards Plan(terms, windows) to C03 (02).
  2. C03 reads the resource revisions from D2 and the energy capability for the site, window and minimum energy from C05 in parallel (03–06). The two reads are independent; neither is assumed to be consistent with the other at a common instant.
  3. C03 opens one D2 transaction over the ordered resource set: it validates the revision set under ordered locks, runs exclusive and pooled-capacity checks including summed seat capacity per segment, and on success writes an expiring HELD bundle together with its outbox entry (07–08) (BKG-017, BKG-018, BKG-020).
  4. C03 returns the offer with the hold expiry; C02 returns terms and expiresAt to the client (09–10).
  5. The client accepts a specific terms revision (11). C02 rejects the acceptance if the hold has expired or any input it was based on has changed; otherwise D1 persists COMMIT_PENDING, the intent and the outbox entry in one local commit before anything is sent (BKG-024, PLT-011).
  6. C02 sends Commit(intent, key) (12). C03 promotes the hold (13); D2 answers PENDING or reject (14). From this point the occupancy is blocked and is not governed by the quote TTL (BKG-025).
  7. C03 requests the external effect as ReserveEnergy(planId, rev, key) (15) and records one of three outcomes: accept, reject or unknown (16) (BKG-041).
  8. On accept with valid capacity, C03 performs CommitSwap(intent) in D2 (18) and receives a durable outcome (19) (BKG-043); release of the old allocation is scheduled as release work, executed only after clearance (20).
  9. C03 returns Outcome(intent) to C02 (21). D1 finalises the booking by CAS on the expected booking revision (BKG-046).
  10. If D1 is CONFIRMED and no cancel is pending, C02 issues a current dispatch permit (26) and reports the customer outcome (25) (BKG-047, DSP-002). C04 obtains this permit before it releases the mission (BKG-048).

Alternative flows.

  1. Infeasible request. At step 3 the transaction does not create a hold; C03 returns the binding reason with an alternative, and no occupancy is created (BKG-022).
  2. Hold expires before acceptance. The HELD bundle moves to EXPIRED and the unused hold is released (BKG-023). A later acceptance of the same terms is rejected at step 5 and the client is re-quoted.
  3. Amendment. The amended request carries new terms; the replacement holds new capacity before the old is retired, the swap applies only to unstarted allocations, and started or unknown missions keep their occupancy (BKG-036, BKG-037, BKG-038). The CommitBundle command names both the new and the old bundle (I03).
  4. Energy reject or conflict (D11.2). C03 starts compensation: it undoes the new allocation and releases what is no longer needed, then returns the outcome; D1 records the rejection with reason and alternative and no permit is issued (BKG-044).

Exception flows.

  1. Unknown energy outcome (D11.2). D1 moves to RECONCILING; PENDING occupancy stays blocked; C03, through C05, queries the same planId until the outcome is accept or reject, or the case is escalated (17) (BKG-042, ENE-017, ENE-018). The permit stays blocked throughout (DSP-004). A new request under a new identity is never issued in place of the query.
  2. Cancellation before permit issuance. At any phase, Cancel(intent, rev) (22) makes D1 record cancelRequested against the intent (BKG-050). Because cancel and permit issuance serialise in D1 (BKG-051, DSP-003), a permit can no longer be issued. C02 sends Reconcile / cancel to C03 (23), which resolves any outstanding external outcome first and then compensates; the persisted result (24) is finalised in D1 by CAS.
  3. Cancellation after permit issuance (D11.1). The cancellation becomes cancel / replan of the in-flight mission through C04 and is reported to the customer without a promise of zero movement (BKG-052, DSP-005). Cancel / replan is used only where the vehicle supports it (TBD-042); otherwise C04 waits or escalates with capacity held. Old physical capacity is released only after vehicle / EMS clearance (BKG-039, DSP-006).
  4. Compensation fails. A release or undo that does not complete stays owned and reconciled until its outcome is known; it is raised to C06 as an owned case (BKG-045, DSP-007).

11.D.5 Rules and invariants

R11.1
Only D2 offers atomic guarantees. No step assumes a commit that spans D1, D2, D4 or a site EMS (BKG-019, PLT-013).
R11.2
Every state change that must cause a message is committed together with its outbox entry; nothing is sent from volatile state (PLT-011).
R11.3
Unknown is not rejection. An unknown external outcome keeps occupancy blocked and the permit withheld until the original request identity is resolved (BKG-042, DSP-004).
R11.4
PENDING occupancy is released only by an explicit outcome (accept followed by commit, or reject followed by compensation), never by a timer such as the quote TTL (BKG-025).
R11.5
Only an accepted energy outcome with valid capacity permits CommitSwap (BKG-043).
R11.6
A dispatch permit is a gate derived from D1, not a booking state: it exists only while D1 is CONFIRMED and no cancel is pending (BKG-047).
R11.7
cancelRequested and permit issuance are serialised on the same D1 record; whichever is committed first determines the branch, and the other observes it (BKG-051).
R11.8
Physical capacity is released on physical evidence: old capacity after vehicle / EMS clearance; started or unknown missions keep occupancy (BKG-038, BKG-039).
R11.9
Every compensation has an owner until its outcome is known; failure moves it into an owned case, never into silence (BKG-045).
R11.10
A repeated request with the same idempotency key and the same payload returns the original result; the same key with a different payload is rejected with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (PLT-042).

11.D.6 Data and state

The saga keeps two state machines in two stores and links them by intent. D2 carries the allocation lifecycle of the bundle (REQUESTED → HELD / REJECTED; HELD → COMMIT_PENDING / EXPIRED; COMMIT_PENDING → CONFIRMED / RECONCILING; see D09.3), with PENDING as the occupancy of a promoted hold. D1 carries the booking finalisation of D11.3: COMMIT_PENDING with durable intent and outbox, CONFIRMED with a verified bundle, RECONCILING while the original intent is queried, and REJECTED with reason and alternative. cancelRequested is a recorded fact against the intent, not a separate state, so it can coexist with any phase.

ItemStore / ownerRole in the saga
intentId, bookingId, bookingRev, expectedBookingRevD1 / C02Identity of the customer commitment; CAS guard for finalisation.
termsRev, acceptedTermsRev, expiresAtD1 / C02Binds the acceptance to one offer and its hold expiry; a mismatch rejects at step 5.
holdId, expiresAt, bundleId, bundleRev, idempotencyKeyD2 / C03Hold and bundle identity; unique on tenant / intent / key (PLT-034).
expectedResourceRevs, newBundleId, oldBundleIdI03 CommitBundleOrdered resource set and the replacement pair used by CommitSwap (PLT-041).
planId, rev, key; capabilityRev, ageD4 / C05Identity of the energy effect; the same planId is used for every query.
externalReleaseJobs, reasonCode, retryabilityI03 ResultRelease work that waits for clearance; reason and retry class of a non-committed outcome.
cancelRequestedD1 / C02Recorded against the intent at any phase; blocks permit issuance.

BookingChanged and AllocationCommitted are published from the owners' outboxes through C09 and consumed through idempotent inboxes (PLT-014, PLT-015); consumers order by aggregate revision, so a delayed event cannot overwrite a newer booking state.

11.D.7 Interfaces used

  • I03 C02 → C03: Plan, Hold, Commit / PromoteHold, CommitSwap, Reconcile / cancel; results COMMITTED / HELD / REJECTED / PENDING with reason and retryability.
  • I05 C03 / C05 ↔ site EMS: Read capability, ReserveEnergy, query by planId; outcomes accept / reject / unknown.
  • I04 C04 → vehicle: mission release under a current permit; cancel / replan of in-flight work after issuance.
  • C09 event backbone: transactional outbox, at-least-once delivery, idempotent inbox.

Transport protocols for I03, I04 and I05 are a G2 decision (TBD-003); the saga relies only on the properties stated here: idempotent requests, explicit outcomes and query by original identity.

11.D.8 Failure handling and recovery

FailureDetected byResponseCapacity / permit
Commit message lost between C02 and C03No outcome for the intentOutbox redelivers with the same key; C03 returns the original resultHeld / blocked; no permit
ReserveEnergy response lost or ambiguousOutcome unknownRECONCILING; query the same planId; escalate to an owned case if unresolvedPENDING stays blocked; no permit
Energy reject or conflictExplicit rejectCompensate (undo new / release old as required); REJECTED with alternativeOnly capacity not physically in use is released
Stale capability at plan timeAge beyond the freshness budget (TBD-006)Re-read before hold; reject acceptance on changed inputNo hold on stale input
CAS conflict at D1 finalisationRevision mismatchRe-read D1; re-evaluate cancel and outcome; retry finalisationNo permit until finalised
Compensation failsRelease / undo not confirmedKeep owned; open C06 case with owner, deadline and backupCapacity stays occupied
Late cancel on an executing missionPermit already issuedCancel / replan if supported, else wait or escalateOld capacity after clearance only

After a regional restore the order is RESTORE → RECONCILE → ENABLE DISPATCH (D08.2, PLT-027): outstanding intents are resolved against their original identities before any new permit is issued, so a restored COMMIT_PENDING record never becomes a permit by default. Retry and query cadence are platform parameters (TBD-007).

11.D.9 Security, privacy and audit

All keys, foreign keys and idempotency scopes include the tenant; references are validated within that scope before any hold is created (PLT-030). The dispatch permit is the only authorisation C04 accepts for mission release, which keeps the authority to move a vehicle for a booking with the owner of the booking. Every transition is reconstructable from D1 and D2 revisions, the outbox, and the event envelope correlationId that links each event to its originating intent; the customer outcome reported at step 25 is derived from the persisted D1 state, never from an in-memory result. The saga carries no rider personal data beyond the booking references already held in D1.

11.D.10 Observability and operations

  • Per intent: current D1 state, D2 occupancy, last energy outcome, pending cancel, and the age of the oldest unresolved external effect.
  • Aggregate signals: count of RECONCILING intents and their age, PENDING occupancy blocked by unknown outcomes, failed compensations by owner, CAS conflicts, outbox and inbox lag (C09 lag and poison-event alerts).
  • Escalation: an unresolved query or compensation becomes an owned case; the operator sees the intent, the external identity being queried and the capacity it blocks. Operator actions release only cleared capacity (BKG-033).

11.D.11 Verification approach

  1. Branch tests over the outcome table of D11.2: accept, reject / conflict and unknown, each checked against D2 occupancy, D1 result and permit.
  2. Interleaving tests of Cancel against finalisation and permit issuance on the same intent, asserting that a permit never coexists with a recorded cancelRequested (D11.3).
  3. Duplicate and replay tests: repeated Commit and ReserveEnergy with the same key; same key with a changed payload rejected.
  4. Timer tests: quote TTL elapsing while PENDING must not release occupancy; HELD expiry must release only unused holds.
  5. Late-cancel tests through C04 (D11.1) and the unknown-outcome fault injection of T-R04 (P24 17.1), checking that capacity is held until clearance.
  6. Inspection that no component claims atomicity outside D2 (BKG-019).

11.D.12 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Saga over distributed commit. A two-phase commit across D1, D2 and a site EMS would require the EMS to participate as a resource manager, which an external, locally protected installation cannot be required to do; it would also couple booking availability to the slowest participant. The saga accepts that external effects can be ambiguous and makes ambiguity a first-class state with a defined owner and a query path.

Separate versioned inputs. Treating resource snapshot and energy capability as one revision would imply a consistent cut across two owners that does not exist. Keeping them separate lets each be validated against its own revision at commit time.

Block on unknown rather than release. Releasing on a timer would maximise utilisation but could double-allocate a bay or charge window that is in fact committed at the site. Holding capacity costs utilisation; the design prefers that to a physical conflict.

Permit as a gate, not a state. Making the permit a derived predicate on D1 keeps one source of truth for whether a mission may be released and allows cancellation to be serialised against it on the same record.

Honest late cancellation. Once a mission is released, the vehicle may already be moving; reporting a cancellation as zero movement would be false. The design reports cancel / replan and releases capacity on clearance.

11.D.13 Open points

  • Freshness budget for capability data and the latency budget of the saga (TBD-006, TBD-005, G2).
  • Retry and query parameters for unresolved external effects (TBD-007).
  • Per-vehicle support for cancel / replan of in-flight work (TBD-042).
  • Protocols for I03, I04 and I05 (TBD-003) and complete API schemas (TBD-040).
  • EMS capability and access agreements per site (TBD-035).

The mobility schedule imposes departure-energy constraints. C05 allocates feasible power, reconciles equipment response and sends shortages back to C03. C07 settles measured contributions.

12.DDetailed specification

This section specifies the two energy paths of P12: the control path, in which C05 turns mobility departure-energy constraints, site capability and market commitments into journalled I05 plan revisions and feeds shortages back to C03; and the measurement path, in which observed delivery arrives on I08 and C07 settles household and site contributions under a versioned contract. It defines the scheduler's constraint set in words, the plan-journal guard, the feedback rules, the contribution formula and its allocation rules, the settlement pipeline, the failure behaviour and the verification evidence for each.

12.D.1 Purpose and scope

The service depends on energy that it does not own: household bays with PV, SOFC and storage, corporate sites with building and company-fleet demand, and an optional district CEMS / GTFC supply. Each site has its own protection, limits and owners. The purpose of this chapter is to let the mobility schedule impose firm departure-energy requirements on those sites without taking over their control, and to pay each contributor for what was measured, not for what was planned.

In scope: C05 scheduling and rolling replanning; the I05 plan journal and execution guard; equipment feedback and derating; the I08 measured-actuals path; C07 settlement and the household contribution formula. Out of scope: the booking-time energy reservation (P11 4.1), departure-readiness and replenishment queues (P26 19.2), and plant protection, which remains local to site equipment (ENE-021). Fuel / H2 control is outside the electrical scope of I05 (ENE-020, TBD-036). The optional optimisation capability of C05 is gated separately from the MVP (TBD-022).

12.D.2 Actors and responsibilities

Actor / containerResponsibilityBoundary
C03 Joint reservation authoritySupplies mobility constraints per bundle and replans when C05 returns a shortage.Never relaxes a hard constraint to absorb a shortage.
C05 Energy / EMS adaptersSchedules energy, validates limits, journals and sends plan revisions, reconciles equipment response, owns D4 (Appendix B C05).Sends setpoints and plans; does not operate plant protection.
Site EMS / charger (home, corporate, district)Accepts, rejects or executes a plan revision within local protection and outage behaviour.Local protection overrides any plan.
Market / aggregatorHolds sale schedules, balancing and reserved-capacity commitments.Eligibility and access gates apply (TBD-035).
Meters / I08 adaptersDeliver measured actuals with unit, quality, source revision and contract revision.Measurements are the only basis for settlement.
C07 Usage / settlementValidates actuals, applies the contract, allocates, reconciles, issues bill revisions and corrections, runs payment and payroll jobs; owns D6 (Appendix B C07).Never destructively overwrites actuals.
Equipment workstream (Org)Validates the equipment limits that C05 uses (ENE-022).Limits are inputs to C05, not C05 assumptions.

12.D.3 Inputs to the scheduler

C05 takes three classes of input, each versioned and each with its own owner (ENE-003, ENE-004):

Mobility constraints (C03)
bundleId, arrival and departure, E_arrival, E_next_trip and E_reserve, bay / work / charge intervals, priority and the accepted service promise. These are firm: they are the reason the plan exists.
Forecast and capability
Building demand and PV forecast, SOFC / GTFC availability and limits, grid, storage and site connection caps, each carrying capabilityRev, observedAt and quality. Age is evaluated against the freshness budget (TBD-006).
Market / aggregator commitments
Sale schedule and realised results, balancing kW with duration and baseline, reserved capacity and response limits, eligibility and access gates. Commitments already made are recorded in D4 (ENE-006).

12.D.4 Behaviour

Control loop (rolling replanning).

  1. On a new or changed mobility constraint, a capability revision, a commitment change or equipment feedback, C05 starts a replanning cycle (ENE-001).
  2. C05 reserves firm demand first: the departure-energy requirement of every accepted bundle is placed before any flexible or market use (ENE-002).
  3. C05 solves for the remaining flexibility under the AC bus balance and the storage, SOC, energy and ramp bounds (12.D.5), with the configured energy and delay cost as objective (TBD-033).
  4. If no feasible schedule meets every firm constraint, C05 returns the shortage to C03 for replanning (ENE-005); C03 revises the mission or offer under its own hard constraints.
  5. If feasible, C05 produces a plan revision keyed by planId and planRev and hands it to the I05 plan journal.

I05 plan journal and execution guard (D12.1).

  1. C05 validates current limits against the capabilityRev the plan was built on and its validity window (ENE-014). A stale or changed capability sends the plan back to step 1 of the control loop.
  2. C05 persists the plan command (planId, planRev, bundleId, capabilityRev, validUntil, powerIntervals[]) in D4 before sending it (ENE-013, ENE-015).
  3. C05 sends setpoints to the site EMS / charger and records the response as ACK, reject or unknown (ENE-016).
  4. On unknown, C05 queries the status of the same planId until the outcome is resolved or escalated, and does not resend under a new identity (ENE-017).
  5. On ACK, C05 records acceptedRev and publishes EnergyUpdated through C09. The ACK confirms the plan revision only; it is not delivered energy (ENE-019).
  6. On reject, C05 replans; if the reject removes energy a bundle depends on, the shortage goes to C03.

Measurement and feedback path.

  1. Site equipment reports observed power, energy, meter quality and site alarms. C05 revises feasibility from these observations, including site derating (ENE-023).
  2. Stale capability or meter data blocks the affected capacity and triggers replanning (ENE-024); the vehicle is released for its next departure only when the departure-energy predicate holds on observed values (ENE-026, P26).
  3. Meters deliver actuals on I08 with meterPointId, interval, sourceRev, quantity, unit and contractRev (ENE-037) to C07.

Settlement pipeline (D12.2; ENE-039).

  1. Validate actuals. Check unit, interval, quality and source revision. Entries with missing data stay provisional (ENE-041).
  2. Apply contractRev. Price the validated quantities under the contract revision in force for the interval (ENE-038).
  3. Allocate payer / credit. Compute each contribution by the formula of 12.D.6 and assign payerRef.
  4. Reconcile. Confirm that net pools, credits and assigned costs do not overlap and that pools exclude prior credits and costs (ENE-048, ENE-049).
  5. Issue billRev. Write verified usage and ledger entries to D6 and publish UsageVerified.
  6. Correction entries. Later changes are new entries linked by correctionOf to the corrected record (ENE-040).

12.D.5 Rules and invariants: control path

R12.1
The schedule satisfies P_import + P_gen,net + P_dis,AC = P_load,AC + P_EV,AC + P_ch,AC + P_export at every interval (ENE-007).
R12.2
Every P term is net kW at one AC boundary (ENE-008). Terms measured on another side of a converter are brought to that boundary before they enter the balance.
R12.3
Conversion losses are accounted once, in the storage-energy update, and not again in the bus balance (ENE-009).
R12.4
SOC, energy and ramp are bounded; import and export are never simultaneous; storage charge and discharge are never simultaneous (ENE-010, ENE-011, ENE-012).
R12.5
Firm demand is reserved before flexibility is optimised; a shortage is returned to C03, never absorbed by relaxing a firm constraint (ENE-002, ENE-005).
R12.6
No plan command is sent without a prior journal entry and a current-limit validation (ENE-014, ENE-015).
R12.7
A plan ACK is not delivered energy; only observed measurement changes departure readiness or settlement (ENE-019).
R12.8
I05 is limited to electrical scope; plant protection remains local (ENE-020, ENE-021).

12.D.6 Contribution accounting

For household i, the contribution is Rᵢ = Σₐ qᵢₐpₐ + Σₜ Eᵢₜpᵢₜ + Σₘ αᵢₘSₘ + Σₛ βᵢₛUᵢₛ − Cᵢ (ENE-044). Each term has a distinct basis and must not be counted in another term:

TermMeaningRule
Σₐ qᵢₐpₐSpace and equipment: rented duration and agreed tasks of item a, at its priceCleaning and similar tasks count only when separately agreed.
Σₜ EᵢₜpᵢₜService electricity supplied in interval t, at its priceExcludes home self-use (ENE-045).
Σₘ αᵢₘSₘShare of net distributable adjustment pool mwᵢₘ ≥ 0; αᵢₘ = wᵢₘ / Σⱼwⱼₘ only when Σw > 0 (ENE-046).
Σₛ βᵢₛUᵢₛSharing revenue from use sSettled as separate eligible revenue (ENE-051).
CᵢAssigned costsApplied as versioned deductions (ENE-050).
R12.9
A pool whose total weight is zero is left unallocated for review rather than divided (ENE-047).
R12.10
Net pools exclude prior credits and costs; net pools, credits and assigned costs stay non-overlapping (ENE-048, ENE-049).
R12.11
Availability kW and delivered kWh are distinct quantities and are never substituted for each other (ENE-052).
R12.12
Each earning carries a unique earning ID; payment and payroll jobs are idempotent (ENE-042, ENE-043).
R12.13
Actuals are never overwritten; corrections are linked entries (ENE-040).

The weights wᵢₘ and deductions Cᵢ belong to the versioned contract (TBD-034); the formula fixes the structure, not the values.

12.D.7 Data and state

The control path and the measurement path write different records that share bundleId, so that every kWh can be traced to an accepted journey without merging plan and measurement (D12.3). EnergyPlan in D4 is keyed by tenantId, planId and planRev, references bundleId and siteId, and records capabilityRev, powerIntervals[], departureMinKWh, expiresAt, acceptedRev and executionEvidence; one bundle has many plan revisions over its life. UsageFact / Ledger in D6 is keyed by tenantId with usageId or ledgerEntryId, references bundleId and contractRev, and records meterPointId, interval, qty, unit, quality, sourceRev, payerRef, correctionOf?, billRev and currency.

A plan revision moves through journalled, sent and ACK / reject / unknown; acceptedRev records the latest revision the site accepted. A settlement entry is provisional until its actuals validate and is superseded only through a correction entry. Neither record carries the other's meaning: executionEvidence on a plan does not settle anything, and a settled quantity does not change a plan.

12.D.8 Interfaces used

  • I05 C05 ↔ site EMS: capacity, setpoints and derating; plan journal and execution guard; equipment feedback.
  • I08 meters / actuals → C07: units, quality and correction links.
  • I03 and the C03 constraint input: mobility constraints in, shortages back.
  • C09: EnergyUpdated from C05 and UsageVerified from C07 through transactional outboxes.

12.D.9 Failure handling and recovery

ConditionResponseEffect on mobility
Infeasible scheduleReturn shortage to C03C03 replans; firm promises are not silently broken
Stale capability or meter dataBlock affected capacity; replanAffected assignments held
I05 response unknownQuery the same planId; escalate if unresolvedDependent capacity stays blocked
I05 rejectReplan; shortage to C03 if firm demand is affectedMission or offer revised
Site derating, outage or alarmRevise feasibility from observationDeparture readiness re-evaluated (P26)
Missing or low-quality actualsEntry stays provisionalNone; settlement delayed
Late or corrected actualsCorrection entry linked by correctionOf; new billRevNone
Zero total weight in a poolLeave unallocated for reviewNone
Duplicate payment job runUnique earning ID makes the second run a no-opNone

12.D.10 Security, privacy and audit

Household sites expose load, generation and presence patterns; meter data and site identity are tenant-scoped and accessed only for scheduling and settlement. Every settled amount is reproducible from D6: the actuals with their sourceRev, the contractRev applied, the allocation weights of that contract, and the chain of correction entries. Because every entry names the contractRev it was settled under, a dispute is answered by recomputing that billRev from the same inputs rather than from the current contract. C05 actions on site equipment are limited to plans and setpoints within the electrical scope; local protection is not operated from the platform (ENE-021).

12.D.11 Observability and operations

  • Control path: plan revisions by outcome (ACK / reject / unknown), age of unresolved plans, shortages returned to C03, derating and alarm events per site, capability age per site.
  • Measurement path: provisional entries and their age, correction entries per billRev, pools left unallocated for review, reserve violations and unmet trips reported even when daily energy balances (ENE-036).
  • Daily inspection on corporate sites is carried out by the staffed site; household cleaning is a separately agreed task and is settled only when agreed.

12.D.12 Verification approach

  1. Analysis of the scheduler formulation against R12.1–R12.5: balance at one boundary, single loss accounting, bounds and mutual exclusions (ENE-007–ENE-012).
  2. Plan-journal tests (D12.1): no send without journal; stale capability rejected; unknown answered by query on the same planId; ACK not counted as delivery.
  3. Site stress tests of P26 19.3: concurrent arrivals, one resource unavailable, reduced power, delayed fuel delivery (ENE-035).
  4. Settlement analysis and tests (D12.2): formula terms disjoint, zero-weight pool unallocated, provisional entries, correction chains, duplicate job runs.

12.D.13 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Hierarchical control. C05 plans and the site executes and protects. Direct platform control of site equipment would place protection behind a network dependency and would require each site owner to cede control; a plan-and-acknowledge contract keeps responsibility where the equipment is.

Rolling replanning. Forecasts, arrivals and site conditions change continuously; a single day-ahead plan would be invalid before execution. Rolling replanning with versioned inputs accepts change as normal and makes each plan traceable to the inputs it used.

Measurement-based settlement. Settling on plans would pay for energy that may not have been delivered and would let an ACK stand in for a meter. Settling on validated actuals under a versioned contract makes payments auditable and corrections explicit.

Explicit formula terms. Separating space, service electricity, adjustment pools, sharing revenue and costs prevents double counting, which is the most likely error when one household is both a site host and a participant in shared revenue.

12.D.14 Open points

  • Scheduler objective and its configured costs (TBD-033).
  • Contribution weights and versioned deductions (TBD-034).
  • Market / aggregator eligibility and EMS access agreements (TBD-035).
  • Fuel / H2 capability on I05 and a fuel-to-energy model (TBD-036); district CEMS / GTFC limits (TBD-037).
  • Node power, energy and footprint limits (TBD-014); freshness budgets (TBD-006); I05 and I08 protocols (TBD-003).

UNKNOWN is a knowledge state, not a vehicle state. Expiry blocks a new command but never stops status reconciliation.

Vehicle/ADS owns driving and fallback. Read-only queries and emergency escalation remain available with stale data. Case closure follows P18; motion requests use P22 action-specific guards. Rejected/unknown effects stay reconciled.

D13.1State machineI04 command delivery, vehicle execution and observer knowledge

Delivery acknowledgment and vehicle execution are separate state dimensions on one commandId. UNKNOWN belongs to the observer (C04 journal), not to the vehicle, and never substitutes for a delivery or execution state.

Source: P13 §6.1 (this chapter); P10 §3.1; P22 §15.2

D13.2State machineC06 case lifecycle with lease, escalation and reopen

The case is owned by one qualified seat under a single action lease. A lease that expires or is not acknowledged returns the case to assignment with a backup owner; material new evidence reopens a resolved or closed case.

13.DDetailed specification

This section specifies the remote mission protocol of P13 6.1: how C04 persists and delivers an I04 command, how delivery, vehicle execution and observer knowledge are kept as separate dimensions on one command identity, how an uncertain outcome is held, queried and escalated, how C06 owns the resulting case under a single action lease, how a remote action is authorised and observed, and when availability may be revised. It defines the flows, the state rules, the evidence each transition needs, failure recovery and the verification approach.

13.D.1 Purpose and scope

A remote system cannot know what a vehicle did from the fact that it sent a command. A message can be delivered and not accepted, accepted and not executed, executed and not reported, or reported late with stale state. The protocol therefore treats every command as a durable, identified request whose effect is established only by evidence from the vehicle, and treats the absence of that evidence as a state of knowledge that must be owned until it is resolved.

In scope: mission release on I04 after the dispatch permit, the D3 command and status journal, the unknown-outcome loop, C06 vehicle cases in D5, owner leases and escalation, the authorisation of a scoped remote action and the release decision that revises availability. Specified elsewhere: the dispatch permit (P11 4.1), the remote channels and vehicle trust zone (P14 7.1), release predicates (P18), remote-assistance advice (P19), centre fencing (P20 13.1), seat staffing and handover (P21 14.1) and action-specific guards (P22 15.1). The vehicle and ADS own driving and fallback throughout; nothing in this protocol substitutes for them.

13.D.2 Actors and responsibilities

ActorResponsibilityStore
C04 FleetReleases missions under a current permit, persists and sends commands, validates vehicle messages, records delivery and execution, marks UNKNOWN, queries original identities, opens cases, projects availability (Appendix B C04).D3 command and status journal
Adapter / journal (vehicle edge)Deduplicates by command identity, enforces expiry, reports receipt, acceptance and execution separately (OPS-008).Durable edge journal
Vehicle / ADSAccepts or rejects each command onboard, executes or aborts, retains DDT and fallback (DSP-035, OPS-017).Onboard
C06 CaseOwns vehicle cases, assigns a qualified seat under a single action lease, escalates, authorises scoped actions, decides release (Appendix B C06).D5 vehicle cases / owner leases
Remote operator / backup ownerAcknowledges the current case revision, gathers evidence, proposes actions within role and qualification.—
C03Holds the affected vehicle capacity while a command is UNKNOWN and reassesses availability only after release (DSP-019).D2

13.D.3 Preconditions

  • C04 holds the current D1 permit for the mission (DSP-001).
  • The vehicle is reachable under the current authority epoch and has installed the fence of the active centre (P20 13.1); without a fence ACK no new action is taken.
  • Each command carries tenantId, commandId, bundleId, vehicleId, missionRev, routeRef, validUntil and payloadHash; one commandId has exactly one immutable payloadHash (DSP-010, PLT-037, I04).

13.D.4 Behaviour

Main flow: mission delivery and outcome (steps 01–05 of P13 6.1).

  1. C04 forms Mission(id, validTo) for the permitted bundle.
  2. C04 persists the command in D3 (PERSISTED) before sending it (DSP-008), then sends it to the edge adapter (SENT).
  3. The adapter returns Receipt(cmdId) (RECEIVED). Receipt proves delivery only (DSP-013).
  4. The vehicle validates the command onboard and accepts or rejects it with a reason.
  5. C04 journals the outcome in D3 (DSP-009) and keeps the delivery and execution dimensions separate (OPS-001).

Exception flow: uncertain outcome (steps 06–09).

  1. If acceptance is unknown, a fault occurs or telemetry is stale, C04 marks the command UNKNOWN as observer knowledge, keeps its identity and makes C03 block reuse of the affected capacity (OPS-002, DSP-017, DSP-019).
  2. C04 sends Query(cmdId) for the original identity and never re-issues the effect under a new identity (DSP-020).
  3. For each answer, C04 verifies observedAt, seq and clock quality; old or repeated state is not accepted as proof of recovery (OPS-003, DSP-021).
  4. The query loop runs while the query budget remains (TBD-027). If the outcome becomes known, the journal is updated and the flow continues from step 5 of the main flow.

Case flow (steps 10–14).

  1. When the outcome remains unknown, C04 opens a C06 case with OpenCase(command, last observation, severity, deadline) (DSP-022). The case enters OPEN.
  2. C06 assigns one qualified seat with Assign(lease, dueAt); the lease is held in D5 (OPS-011). The case enters ASSIGNED.
  3. The owner acknowledges the current revision with ACK(caseRev) before acting. The case enters ACK.
  4. The owner submits an action with evidence. The case enters ACTIVE.

Alternative flow: lease expiry, missing ACK or urgent deadline (D13.3).

  1. C06 detects that the lease expired, the ACK is missing or the deadline is urgent.
  2. C06 escalates and issues a new lease to a backup owner; ownership is reassigned, not abandoned (OPS-012).
  3. Any action still carrying the old lease is rejected as stale.
  4. The handover passes the acceptance of pending commands, passenger status, field ETA and the next deadline; the backup owner acknowledges the current caseRev before acting.

Guarded action and execution (steps 15–22).

  1. For a motion-enabling action, C06 checks role, caseRev, authority fence, current evidence and expected state before authorising a scoped action (DSP-037, OPS-076); the action class and its guards are those of P22 15.1.
  2. C04 persists and sends the resulting command exactly as in the main flow; a receipt is recorded as receipt only.
  3. On acceptance, C04 observes execution as Executing(seq, time) and correlates it with independent evidence (DSP-014). Completion or abort with correlated evidence yields a verified result and the case moves to RESOLVED. Receipt or acceptance alone never resolves a case (OPS-005).
  4. On rejection or an unknown outcome, the case stays open and C06 reconciles by state query or initiates an approved fallback; missing terminal evidence stays unresolved (OPS-009, DSP-023).

Release (steps 24–25).

  1. With fresh state and accepted release authority, C06 makes a release decision and closes the case with its evidence (OPS-014).
  2. C04 revises availability with physical completion evidence attached (DSP-031). Closure itself never changes ADS mode, never automatically clears an operational hold and never by itself releases capacity (OPS-015, DSP-033); the release predicates of P18 govern.
  3. If material new evidence arrives after RESOLVED or CLOSED, the case reopens (OPS-013).

13.D.5 Rules and invariants

R13.1
Persist before send. No command leaves C04 without a D3 entry (DSP-008).
R13.2
One identity, one payload. The same commandId with a changed payload is rejected; a replayed commandId produces no duplicate effect at the edge (DSP-011).
R13.3
Delivery, execution and observer knowledge are separate. RECEIVED is not ACCEPTED, ACCEPTED is not EXECUTING, and UNKNOWN is never a vehicle state (DSP-012, DSP-018).
R13.4
Unknown holds capacity. While a command is UNKNOWN, the affected vehicle capacity is held and its reuse blocked (DSP-019).
R13.5
Expiry stops new acceptance, not reconciliation. An expired command cannot be accepted, and its status is still queried until known (DSP-015, OPS-006).
R13.6
Evidence must be fresh and ordered. A query result is accepted only after observedAt, seq and clock quality pass; old or repeated state cannot prove recovery (DSP-021).
R13.7
One owner per case. Every open case has one qualified owner under one action lease, a deadline and a backup (OPS-011, CAP-048).
R13.8
Stale lease, stale action. An action carrying an expired lease or an outdated caseRev is rejected (OPS-012).
R13.9
Resolution requires observed execution correlated with evidence (OPS-005).
R13.10
Read-only queries and emergency escalation remain available when vehicle data is stale (DSP-024).
R13.11
No remote command overrides ADS constraints; safety checks remain onboard (DSP-034).

13.D.6 Data and state

The command record in D3 (Mission / Command, key tenantId and commandId) carries deliveryState, executionState, statusSeq, observedAt and receivedAt; each outcome state is recorded as a CommandAuditEvent with its reason (P22 15.2). The three dimensions of D13.1 are evaluated together:

DimensionValuesSource of truthCan resolve a case?
Delivery (deliveryState)PERSISTED → SENT → RECEIVEDC04 journal and adapter receiptNo
Execution (executionState)ACCEPTED → EXECUTING → COMPLETED / ABORTED; REJECTED and EXPIRED with reasonVehicle report with statusSeq and observedAtOnly COMPLETED / ABORTED with correlated evidence
Observer knowledgeUNKNOWNC04 judgement on missing, faulty or stale evidenceNo; it opens or keeps a case

The vehicle case in D5 follows OPEN → ASSIGNED → ACK → ACTIVE → RESOLVED → CLOSED (D13.2, OPS-010). caseRev identifies the revision of the case; ACK and action requests carry the revision they were based on, so a decision taken on an older view of the case is detectable. The handover record holds vehicle, mission, case revision, lease epoch, reason, advice type, expiry and expected outcome. Case changes are published as CaseChanged through C09.

13.D.7 Interfaces used

  • I04 mission, receipt and execution; Query(cmdId); telemetry for freshness.
  • I07 OpenCase, Assign, ACK, Escalate / new lease, Action + evidence, scoped authorisation, release decision.
  • C09 MissionObserved from C04 and CaseChanged from C06 through transactional outboxes.
  • D1 permit from C02 (P11 4.1); capacity hold and reassessment in C03.

13.D.8 Failure handling and recovery

FailureDetectionResponse
Send fails before receiptNo receipt for a SENT commandQuery(cmdId) on the original identity; any re-delivery uses the same commandId and payload, which the edge deduplicates
Response lost after acceptanceReceipt without outcome; stale telemetryUNKNOWN; hold capacity; Query(cmdId)
Stale or repeated statusobservedAt, seq or clock quality check failsDiscard as proof; keep UNKNOWN; continue querying

Contradicting evidence after closureMaterial new evidenceReopen the case
