13.D.9 Security, privacy and audit

Remote actions are authenticated, scoped and expiring and carry the current lease, capability and scene (DSP-036). The operator's role and qualification, the authority epoch and the case revision are part of every request, so each effect can be attributed to an accountable person acting on a known view of the case. Service AI may draft or summarise, but cannot authorise motion or bypass a command guard (DSP-038). The D3 journal and D5 case history together reconstruct who asked for what, on which evidence, what the vehicle reported and when; raw events and evidence gaps are preserved rather than smoothed (DSP-016).

13.D.10 Observability and operations

  • Per command: delivery and execution state, UNKNOWN age, last verified observation and its quality.
  • Per case: state, owner, lease expiry, dueAt, caseRev, linked commands and capacity held.
  • Aggregates: commands in UNKNOWN, cases past dueAt, escalations to backup owners, reopened cases, stale-action rejections.
  • The operator workspace shows per-signal age and validity; disabled actions show their reason; replay disables actions (P21).

13.D.11 Verification approach

  1. State-machine tests of D13.1: every allowed transition, and the absence of any path from RECEIVED or UNKNOWN to a resolved case.
  2. Fault injection T-R04 (P24 17.1): lost responses, duplicate delivery and expiry during execution, asserting query by original ID, no duplicate effect and held capacity.
  3. Freshness test T-R01: old or repeated status must not be accepted as recovery.
  4. Lease tests of D13.3: expiry, missing ACK and urgent deadline produce a backup owner and reject the stale action.
  5. Case lifecycle tests of D13.2: closure without fresh state is refused; closure does not release capacity; new evidence reopens.
  6. Guard tests T-R03 and T-R06 for scoped, motion-enabling actions under the current fence.

13.D.12 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Separate dimensions over a single status. A single status field would force a choice between "sent" and "running" when the truth is "delivered, outcome not known". Splitting delivery, execution and knowledge prevents an optimistic default from releasing capacity that the vehicle may still be using.

Query by original identity over resend. Resending under a new identity can double an effect if the first command did execute. Querying the original identity, with edge deduplication, makes retries safe.

Owned cases over alerts. An alert can be ignored; a case with one owner, a lease and a deadline cannot silently lapse. Leases make ownership explicit and allow a clean handover when a seat is overloaded or unavailable.

Evidence-gated release. Releasing on closure or on reconnect would couple a bookkeeping event to physical availability. Requiring fresh state, release authority and physical completion evidence keeps capacity tied to what the vehicle has actually done.

13.D.13 Open points

  • Query budget for unresolved commands (TBD-027).
  • Remote response deadline and its components (TBD-010); freshness and clock parameters (TBD-006, TBD-007).
  • Response class, seat coverage and escalation parameters (TBD-008); ADS-owner fence, action capability and journal parameters (TBD-009).
  • Remote assistance in the MVP is separately gated (TBD-023); complete action schemas (TBD-040).

7.2Operational roles and failure containment

Remote assistance and remote driving

RA supplies contextual advice that the ADS can reject after re-evaluating the scene and ODD. Real-time remote DDT is outside this baseline. Adding remote driving requires a distinct operating envelope, control arbitration, communications safety analysis and operator / approval evidence.

Operational and legal responsibility

Map system roles to the permitted operation, designated supervisor and field-response organisation. Passenger support cannot override door interlocks or authorise motion. Vehicle-specific link-loss and fallback behaviour remains local and does not depend on a remote reply.

  1. Active authority

    • Replicated evidence + backlog
    • Vehicle fence ACK gates new actions
  2. Standby promotion
    • Acquire higher authority epoch
    • Require vehicle fence ACK (P20)
    • Reconcile prior effects before action
  3. Degraded service
    • Hold affected assignments
    • Preserve priority safety traffic
    • Escalate without hiding uncertainty

Acceptance: independently partition telemetry, media, primary centre and workstation. Old-epoch requests reject after the vehicle installs its fence. Test durable deduplication and unknown outcomes. Reconnect and case closure require the release predicate on P18 before availability can change.

14.DDetailed specification

This section specifies the remote architecture of P14 as a control-authority contract. It states which decisions stay onboard with the Level 4 ADS and which belong to the centre, defines each remote channel with its own evidence, health and loss behaviour, describes the remote-monitoring, contextual-assistance and passenger-support flows, and sets out how centre failure, standby promotion and degraded service are contained so that no change of centre, link or case state can by itself move a vehicle or restore its availability (RM-01, RM-02).

14.D.1 Purpose and scope

The service operates driverless vehicles whose automated driving system performs the entire dynamic driving task and its fallback inside an approved ODD. The remote centre adds monitoring, contextual assistance, passenger support, case ownership and fleet decisions. The architectural risk is that a remote function, by design or by failure, acquires authority it cannot safely exercise over a network: issuing a manoeuvre the vehicle has not validated, presenting stale media as live, or restoring a vehicle to service because a link came back. This chapter draws the boundary that prevents this.

In scope: the vehicle trust zone and its onboard functions, the remote channels and their consumers, the C04 vehicle adapter and C06 case policy as seen from the vehicle, operational roles and responsibility mapping, and the authority states of the centre per vehicle. Specified elsewhere: the mission and case protocol (P13 6.1), roadside observations (P15, P16), signal families and alarm detection (P17), release predicates (P18), assistance advice (P19), fencing detail (P20 13.1) and action guards (P22). Real-time remote DDT is outside this baseline (OPS-018, TBD-024).

14.D.2 Authority allocation

DecisionAuthorityRemote role
OEDR (detect and respond to road events); tactical and operational drivingADS / local safety authorityNone; observed through telemetry
DDT fallback, MRM and the achieved MRCADSObserves achieved-state evidence; zero speed alone is not MRC (OPS-040)

The ADS retains DDT and DDT fallback authority, safety checks remain onboard and no cloud function overrides ADS constraints (OPS-017, DSP-034).

14.D.3 Components and responsibilities

ADS / local safety authority
Perception, localisation and motion control; initiates the local fallback response; re-evaluates scene and ODD before acting on any advice (Appendix B vehicle trust zone).
Edge adapter / durable journal
Publishes vehicle state, ODD and diagnostics; holds command identity, expiry and deduplication; separates receipt, acceptance and execution; prioritises uplink and buffers events; stores the accepted authority epoch (OPS-008).
Media / passenger interface
Exterior views with calibration IDs, scene and frame capture timestamps, optional approved cabin channels, passenger SOS and accessible voice, and media-health evidence independent of the telemetry channel.
C04 vehicle adapter / I04
Validates schema, identity, unit and seq; projects state with observation quality; journals effects and unknowns; preserves raw events and gaps; queries original IDs after lost responses; never defaults missing state to healthy (OPS-021, Appendix B C04).
C06 cases / I07 policy
Correlates vehicle and I09 roadside evidence while preserving source quality and conflicts; assigns a qualified seat under a single action lease; bounds RA advice; gates release on fresh vehicle evidence; prevents service AI from authorising motion (OPS-089, Appendix B C06).
Operator / PaaS consumers
See focus scene, history and evidence age. C03 holds affected vehicle capacity, C02 revises journey and passenger offer, C05 revises feasible energy and site slots. No consumer re-enters a vehicle on reconnect or releases it because a case closed (DSP-032, DSP-033).

14.D.4 Channel specification

The channel table in D14.1 lists source, payload, consumer and loss behaviour. The following rules apply across all channels:

  1. Each channel reports its own health and age. Loss of one channel is explicit uncertainty on that channel; it is never inferred from another channel and never defaulted to healthy (OPS-020, DSP-027).
  2. The telemetry / alarm channel carries reliable events with heartbeat and seq. C04 projects state with gaps, clock quality, age and validity (DSP-026); link loss marks remote state UNKNOWN.
  3. The command / result channel carries only authenticated, scoped, expiring actions bound to the current lease, capability and scene, and returns the onboard accept / reject with the observed result (OPS-022).
  4. The evidence / media channel carries adaptive video and keyframe evidence with capture timestamps. No stale frame is rendered as live, and replay mode disables live actions (OPS-023).
  5. Passenger SOS and voice carry independent quality flags and follow local policy plus escalation; they are a support path, not a control path.
  6. Roadside I09 evidence enters through C10 validation outside the vehicle trust zone and reaches C06 as monitoring evidence only; unknown coverage is never a clear road (P15).

Freshness limits per signal are set by the platform (TBD-006); this chapter fixes only that every consumer evaluates age against them.

14.D.5 Behaviour

Remote monitoring.

  1. The edge adapter publishes telemetry and alarms with heartbeat and seq; media publishes frames with capture timestamps.
  2. C04 validates each message (DSP-025) and projects state with observation quality; C06 detects and triages per signal family (P17 10.1).
  3. The operator workspace shows the focus scene, history and the age of each piece of evidence; a missing signal appears as uncertainty, not as normal.

Contextual assistance (RA).

  1. The vehicle raises an assistance request with its scene revision; C06 opens or updates a case and assigns a qualified seat.
  2. The operator gathers evidence and proposes bounded advice; C06 applies the action-specific guards of P22.
  3. C04 delivers the guarded advice as an authenticated, scoped, expiring action. The ADS re-evaluates scene and ODD and may reject it; acceptance is reported onboard with the observed result.
  4. Advice never widens the ODD, never implies a mode transition and never creates a direct actuator path (P19).

Passenger support. Passenger SOS or voice is routed to passenger support with its own channel health. Support may inform, reassure and dispatch field response; it cannot override door interlocks, authorise motion or give an unsafe exit instruction (OPS-024).

Link loss. The vehicle applies its own vehicle-specific link-loss and fallback behaviour without waiting for a remote reply (OPS-019). The centre marks remote state UNKNOWN, holds affected capacity and keeps case ownership (OPS-026). Read-only queries and emergency escalation remain available.

Centre failure and standby promotion (D14.2).

  1. On loss of the primary centre, affected assignments and capacity are held; existing vehicle effects are treated as unresolved.
  2. The standby is promoted only through quorum-backed authority under a higher authority epoch, with a signed grant and the journal (OPS-027); it recovers cases and commands from the durable journal.
  3. For each reachable vehicle, the centre verifies identity and boot epoch and installs the fence; the vehicle stores the epoch durably and acknowledges with PersistedFenceACK(epoch) (OPS-028).
  4. Without that ACK, the centre takes no new action on the vehicle; after it, the vehicle rejects old-epoch requests while prior accepted effects still reconcile (OPS-029).
  5. The centre queries each unresolved commandId under the new epoch and reconciles prior effects before any new action (OPS-030).
  6. Unreachable vehicles stay in degraded service: no new motion-enabling action; field and emergency escalation remain available (OPS-031).

Degraded service and reconnect. The centre holds affected assignments, preserves priority safety traffic and escalates without hiding uncertainty. Reconnection does not re-enter the vehicle into service; availability changes only when the release predicate of P18 holds (OPS-036, DSP-032).

14.D.6 Rules and invariants

R14.1
The ADS holds DDT and fallback authority; no remote function overrides an ADS constraint (OPS-017).
R14.2
Every remote action is accepted or rejected onboard; the centre learns its effect only from the observed result (DSP-035).
R14.3
Channels are independent evidence sources; health is never inferred across channels (OPS-020).
R14.4
Live is a property of evidence age, not of the display; stale frames are not live and replay disables actions (OPS-023).
R14.5
Monitoring, assistance and passenger support use separate permissions and evidence paths; I07 permissions differ by case type (I07).
R14.6
Service AI drafts or summarises within task scope and cannot authorise ADS movement (OPS-089).
R14.7
A centre gains action rights per vehicle only after that vehicle's fence ACK; new cloud ownership does not instantly revoke an unreachable vehicle's old authority (P20 13.1).
R14.8
Centre ownership loss blocks new dispatch and does not erase an accepted physical effect (OPS-033).
R14.9
A vehicle without fence / dedup capability is excluded from automated centre handover (OPS-034, TBD-041).
R14.10
Neither reconnect nor case closure changes availability; only the P18 release predicate does (OPS-015, DSP-032).

14.D.7 Data and state

The vehicle trust zone is identified by device identity, boot epoch and capability revision; these qualify every message and every fence. The centre keeps, per vehicle, one of the authority states of D14.3: Active authority (durable cases and command journal, replicated evidence and backlog, fence ACK gates new actions), Standby promotion (higher epoch acquired, fence ACK awaited, prior effects being reconciled) and Degraded service (assignments held, safety traffic preserved, escalation open). A vehicle that reboots without recoverable authority or journal evidence blocks new action until resynchronised (OPS-032). A new mission after a centre change carries id, epoch and expiry (OPS-035).

14.D.8 Interfaces used

  • I04: telemetry / alarm, command / result and evidence / media channels; Status(boot, seq); InstallFence and PersistedFenceACK.
  • I07: case resolution and guarded advice / request.
  • I09c: roadside evidence via C10 to C06, monitoring only.

14.D.9 Failure containment

PartitionVehicle behaviourCentre behaviour
Telemetry lostLocal policy; continues within ADS authorityState UNKNOWN; capacity held; case owned; escalation available
Media lostUnchangedMedia health flagged; no frame shown as live; actions needing scene evidence unavailable
Passenger voice lostLocal interlocks and policyIndependent quality flag; field escalation
Primary centre lostKeeps prior accepted effects; rejects old epoch after fenceStandby promotion; fence per vehicle; reconcile before action
Operator workstation lostUnchangedLease expires; backup owner with new lease (P13 6.1)

14.D.10 Operational and legal responsibility

System roles are mapped to the permitted operation, the designated supervisor and the field-response organisation (OPS-025). The mapping is part of the operating approval, not of the software: the software enforces it through role, qualification and lease checks on I07. The DDT actor record and fallback responsibilities by actor (TBD-012) and the approved ODD (TBD-011) are held in the G2 constraint register.

14.D.11 Security, privacy and audit

Vehicle messages are bound to device identity and boot epoch; fences use signed grants with expiry, validated onboard. Commands carry command identity and expire, which limits the damage of a replayed or delayed message. Cabin channels are optional and require approval (TBD-043); exterior and cabin evidence is accessed in the context of a case. Every remote action, its guard evaluation, its onboard outcome and its evidence are journalled so that each effect can be attributed to an accountable role and a known authority epoch.

14.D.12 Verification approach

  1. Partition tests that independently cut telemetry, media, primary centre and workstation, asserting the containment table above.
  2. T-R02 (P24 17.1): an ODD limit or sensor degradation yields the correct response with no remote extension of the ODD; no remote command overrides ADS constraints.
  3. T-R03: expired or changed-scene advice is rejected onboard with a reason, and context is renewed if required.
  4. T-R05: loss of telemetry, media or voice yields independent quality flags with local policy and escalation.
  5. T-R06: centre partition and old operator; old-epoch requests rejected after fence installation; prior accepted effects reconciled.
  6. T-R07: with SOS, MRM failure and no field team, emergency and passenger work remain owned. T-R08: an alarm storm hides no P0, and service AI is denied motion authorisation.
  7. Durable deduplication and unknown-outcome tests; reconnect and case-closure tests showing no availability change without the P18 predicate.

14.D.13 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Assistance rather than remote driving. Remote DDT would put a network path inside the control loop and would require its own operating envelope, control arbitration, communications safety analysis and operator approval evidence. Contextual advice that the ADS may reject keeps the safety case with the vehicle and lets the remote centre add judgement without adding a control dependency.

Independent channels. A single health signal for the vehicle link would hide partial failures: media can fail while telemetry is fine, or the reverse. Independent health per channel lets each consumer degrade precisely.

Per-vehicle fencing. A centre-level switchover alone cannot guarantee that a vehicle stops honouring the old centre. Installing a fence on each vehicle, and acting only after its durable ACK, ensures that the vehicle accepts requests under only one authority epoch at a time; vehicles that cannot be fenced stay in degraded service rather than being handed over optimistically.

14.D.14 Open points

  • ADS-owner parameters for link loss, fallback, action capability, fence and journal (TBD-009); per-vehicle fence / dedup capability (TBD-041).
  • Failover mechanism of the regional core (TBD-002); freshness budgets (TBD-006).
  • Remote assistance in the MVP (TBD-023); remote driving outside the baseline (TBD-024).
  • Approved cabin channels (TBD-043); ODD and DDT actor record (TBD-011, TBD-012).

15.DDetailed specification

This section specifies the proposed roadside sensing and edge computing path of P15 (RM-13): the field deployment and its separation of sensing, compute and communication ownership; the data plane from I09a through I09b to the I09c envelope; the C10 eligibility gate that classifies every envelope as accepted, quarantine or diagnostic; association with vehicle evidence in C06; overload, reconnect and replay behaviour; the management plane; and the evidence, privacy and storage boundaries. Roadside observations supplement vehicle evidence for monitoring and operational review and never act on a vehicle.

15.D.1 Purpose and scope

Vehicle sensors see the road from one viewpoint at a time. A roadside installation at a complex junction, depot entrance or pick-up area can give the remote centre context that no single vehicle has: occluded approaches, queue formation, objects near a stopped vehicle. The value lies in operator context and case evidence. The risk lies in treating that context as authoritative: assuming that an area with no reported object is clear, linking a roadside track to the wrong vehicle, or letting an observation trigger a command. This chapter specifies a path that captures the value and contains the risk.

C10 Roadside ingestion and I09 are marked proposed and are separately gated; I09 roadside sensing is kept out of the MVP (TBD-021). The specification below defines the contract that any later adoption must meet. It covers the field trust zone, I09a–I09c, C10, the C06 association and presentation step, the edge management plane and the site services contract. The case and alarm handling that consume roadside evidence are specified in P16 9.1 and P17; action guards in P22.

15.D.2 Actors and responsibilities

ElementResponsibilityDoes not
Roadside sensingCaptures with time stamp and calibrationRef; reports coverage polygon with occlusion, health, quality and sensor revision on I09a (RSD-003).Claim coverage it cannot observe.
Edge / MEC observation workerDetects, tracks, classifies and summarises; transforms local frames to the agreed map frame; publishes scoped tracks with quality and lineage on I09b from a bounded buffer with priority queues (RSD-004).Assume a global object identity.
RSU + backhaul gatewayCarries envelopes over the selected V2X interface and authenticated IP backhaul with its own identity, profile and rate limit (RSD-005).Integrate sensing.
Edge managementRuns a separate control plane: signed model and config versions, staged release and rollback, resource and sensor health monitoring (RSD-006).Share the data plane.
C10 Roadside ingestion [proposed]Applies source, time, order, frame, calibration and coverage checks; classifies; quarantines; publishes coverage degradation (Appendix B C10).Drop silently; forward unchecked envelopes.
C06 Monitoring + case evidenceAssociates with I04 vehicle evidence, retains conflicting hypotheses, attaches provenance and coverage state, owns escalation.Override ADS state; command from observations.

15.D.3 Deployment and plane separation

The field trust zone is defined by site-scoped identity, clock and calibration. Everything inside it is trusted only to the extent that its identity, clock bound and calibration revision can be verified at C10. Three planes are kept apart:

Data plane
Sensing → edge worker (I09a) → RSU / backhaul (I09b) → C10 (I09c) → C06. Carries observations, coverage and health only.
Management plane
Edge management on its own control plane. Model and configuration changes are signed, versioned and released in stages with rollback; the version in force is visible in each envelope as modelRev. CPU, memory, queue age and sensor health are monitored here. Regional failover uses a new epoch and re-qualifies observations (RSD-007).
Site services
The PPA site services / installation contract covers power capacity, backup autonomy, thermal budget, cabinet, network, physical access and maintenance, with a separate sensor site where coverage requires it (RSD-008).

The separation is designed so that a fault or compromise in one plane cannot change the other: a management update cannot inject observations, and an observation cannot alter configuration.

15.D.4 Behaviour

Main flow: observation to evidence (D15.1).

  1. Sensors capture and send raw sensing with health heartbeat on I09a.
  2. The edge worker detects, tracks, classifies and summarises, and expresses each track in the agreed map frame with its uncertainty, quality and lineage.
  3. The worker publishes scoped tracks on I09b; the RSU / backhaul forwards them to C10 as authenticated I09c envelopes.
  4. C10 applies, in order, schema / source / access checks (RSD-009), clock bound, age and sequence gates (RSD-010) and frame / calibration / coverage checks (RSD-011).
  5. C10 classifies the envelope as accepted, quarantine or diagnostic (RSD-012; D15.3).
  6. Accepted observations go to C06 with their coverage state. C06 associates them with I04 pose, status, time and quality through a spatial-temporal gate that preserves uncertainty (RSD-020).
  7. C06 presents the evidence to the operator with quality, provenance and coverage state (RSD-024) and, where needed, opens or updates an owned case.

Exception flow: ineligible envelope.

  1. An invalid, stale, unknown-clock-bound, bad-calibration or lost-coverage envelope is quarantined, not dropped.
  2. The source receives a reject / diagnostic receipt.
  3. A coverage failure publishes coverage degradation with an owner to C06 (RSD-013). The affected area becomes unknown coverage in the operator view, never a clear road (RSD-015).

Exception flow: heartbeat expiry. Coverage is set UNKNOWN, the source time of the last valid sample is retained, and coverage degraded is published with an owner; no stale frame is shown as current (RSD-025).

Exception flow: overload. The edge reserves queue capacity for health and critical events, applies the explicit drop policy and reports queue age and dropped observations; C10 quarantines and publishes coverage degradation (RSD-027, TBD-019).

Alternative flow: reconnect and replay. A reconnecting edge uses a new epoch and passes resync and health checks before its observations are eligible; replayed data is historical only and never acts live (RSD-026). Repeated or replayed samples never refresh the original observation time (RSD-014).

Alternative flow: operator action on roadside evidence. Any action follows the P22 guards on the guarded I07 path; the ADS retains DDT and fallback independently (RSD-029). Return of roadside coverage never releases vehicle capacity; release stays with the P18 predicates (RSD-028).

15.D.5 Rules and invariants

R15.1
Supplement, never actuate. I09 feeds monitoring and operational review only; there is no observation-to-command bypass (RSD-001, RSD-029).
R15.2
Unknown is not clear. Unknown or lost coverage is never interpreted as the absence of objects (RSD-015).
R15.3
No time without a bound. An envelope with an unknown clock bound is rejected with time validity UNKNOWN (RSD-010).
R15.4
Original time is preserved. Deduplication by source, epoch and sequence; replay cannot refresh observedAt (RSD-014).
R15.5
Quarantine, do not drop. Every ineligible envelope is quarantined with a receipt to its source (RSD-012).
R15.6
Local identity only. trackKey is sourceId / bootEpoch / localTrackId; no global identity is assumed (RSD-017).
R15.7
Association is probabilistic. Each candidate vehicle link carries confidence, method and expiry (RSD-021).
R15.8
Conflicts are kept. Disagreeing roadside and vehicle claims stay as separate hypotheses; ADS state is not silently overridden (RSD-022).
R15.9
Lineage prevents double counting of multiple reports (RSD-023).
R15.10
No completeness claim. The path does not provide collision avoidance or perception completeness (RSD-034).
R15.11
Thresholds for age, association, coverage and queue size are agreed per use case and are not fixed in this baseline (RSD-019, TBD-016).

15.D.6 Data and state

The ObservationEnvelope of P15 8.2 is specified in RSD-016 and grouped by consuming check in D15.2. Its design follows one principle: each field exists because a gate needs it. Identity and scope fields (tenantId, siteId, sourceId, sensorIds[]) feed source and access checks; bootEpoch and seq feed the sequence gate and deduplication; observedAt, emittedAt, clockErrorBound_s and expiresAt feed the age and clock-bound gates; frameId, mapRev, calibrationRev and coverageRef feed the spatial checks; position_m, velocity_mps and uncertainty / covariance feed the C06 association gate; class, confidence, visibility and modelRev qualify the classification; evidenceRef links to authorised evidence; the signature or authenticated transport with payloadHash protects integrity.

CoverageHealth (RSD-018) is a separate record because coverage can change without any object being observed. It reports coverageId, polygon, exclusions and sampledAt, sensor availability, clock validity, calibration status, and occlusion, weather, queueAge and processing status. For C06, coverage of an area is in one of three conditions: covered and healthy, degraded with an owner, or UNKNOWN after heartbeat expiry. Envelope classification is one of accepted, quarantine or diagnostic. No D store is stated for C10; raw clips sit under the retention contract (15.D.8).

15.D.7 Interfaces used

  • I09a roadside sensing → edge worker: capture and health heartbeat.
  • I09b edge worker → RSU + backhaul: scoped tracks, quality and lineage.
  • I09c RSU / backhaul → C10 → C06: authenticated observations and health; reject / diagnostic receipt; scoped clip request and EvidenceRef.
  • I04 vehicle pose, status, time and quality for association; I07 guarded path for any resulting action.

CPM mapping and the radio profile require a separately verified adapter (RSD-033, TBD-018); sensor selection and the V2X interface are open (TBD-017).

15.D.8 Security, privacy and evidence storage

Each source has site-scoped identity; the RSU and backhaul have their own identity, profile and rate limit, so that a fault or compromise of one element is not mistaken for traffic from another and its rate stays bounded. Envelopes are signed or carried over authenticated transport with payloadHash, and are checked within the tenant scope before C06 sees them. Model and configuration changes come only through the signed management plane.

Raw clips can show people and vehicles unrelated to any case. They are governed by a purpose, access and retention contract (RSD-030, TBD-020). The edge sends summaries first; authorised evidence is fetched on request for a case and returned as EvidenceRef with source and retention. Regional placement of evidence is part of the same open contract. After a roadside-triggered action, case closure and fleet release stay separate predicates, and closure appends audit before the P18 release gate (RSD-032).

15.D.9 Observability and operations

  • Per source: heartbeat age, clock validity, calibration status, coverage condition, queue age, dropped observations, current modelRev.
  • At C10: envelopes by classification and by failing check, diagnostic receipts sent, coverage degradations open and their owners.
  • At C06: candidate links with confidence and expiry, conflicting hypotheses open, operator workload attributable to roadside evidence.
  • Regional observation workers scale independently of ADS control (RSD-031).

15.D.10 Verification approach

  1. Gate tests over D15.3: each check failing alone quarantines with a receipt and, where coverage is affected, publishes degradation.
  2. Transport and lifecycle tests: disconnect, reboot, reordering and duplicate delivery; reconnect under a new epoch; replay kept historical (RSD-035).
  3. Field-condition tests: occlusion, weather, false association and saturation, measuring quality, end-to-end age and operator workload (RSD-036).
  4. Boundary tests: no command originates from an observation; coverage return does not release capacity; disagreeing evidence produces two hypotheses.
  5. Inspection of the management plane: signed versions, staged release, rollback.

15.D.11 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Monitoring evidence rather than a perception input. Feeding roadside tracks into vehicle control would make the safety case depend on infrastructure owned and maintained by others, with its own clocks, calibration and failure modes. Keeping I09 as operator evidence lets the centre benefit from it without changing what the ADS is responsible for.

Separate ownership of sensing, compute and communication. These functions have different owners, lifecycles and failure modes. Separating them, with distinct identities and interfaces, allows each to be replaced or upgraded without assuming that one vendor or device integrates all three.

Quarantine over silent drop. Silent loss makes the absence of objects indistinguishable from the absence of data. Quarantine with a receipt and a published degradation keeps that distinction visible to the source owner and the operator.

Local track identity. A global identity would need cross-source fusion with its own error model. Treating each track as local and each vehicle link as a probabilistic candidate with expiry keeps association errors visible rather than baked into identity.

15.D.12 Open points

  • Adoption of C10 and I09 beyond the MVP (TBD-021).
  • Thresholds for age, association, coverage and queue size per use case (TBD-016).
  • Sensor selection and V2X interface (TBD-017); CPM mapping and radio profile (TBD-018).
  • Explicit drop policy under overload (TBD-019); raw-clip contract and regional placement (TBD-020).
  • Protocols for I09a and I09c (TBD-003); clock and loss parameters (TBD-007).

16.DDetailed specification

This section specifies the RM-14 roadside monitoring sequence end to end: how a roadside detection travels from the field trust zone through C10 eligibility checks into C06 as scoped evidence, how it is associated with vehicle I04 evidence without overriding it, how an operator may act on it only through the guarded I07 path, and how the case closes without implying fleet release. It also specifies the fault branches of 9.2 (link / edge loss, conflict and overload), the data each step relies on, the rules that hold throughout, and how the behaviour is verified. The path is proposed and separately gated (TBD-021); nothing here places roadside sensing in the MVP.

16.D.1 Purpose and scope

The sequence exists to give remote monitoring an additional, independently sourced view of the road around a vehicle: occlusions the vehicle cannot see, a stopped vehicle seen from outside, or a scene that helps an operator judge a vehicle-reported obstruction. Roadside observations supplement vehicle evidence; they never replace it and never actuate anything (RSD-001, ASM-020). The specification therefore treats every roadside observation as a claim with a source, a time bound, a frame and a coverage context, and every downstream use of it as conditional on that context being valid.

In scope: steps 01–19 of 9.1, the two fault branches of 9.2 and their detail figures (D16.1, D16.2, D16.3), and the responsibilities of C10 and C06 for roadside evidence (Appendix B C10, Appendix B C06). Out of scope: the roadside deployment topology and observation contract themselves (P15), the alarm logic that classifies a resulting case (P17), the action guards (P22) and the release predicates (P18), which this chapter invokes but does not redefine. The roadside path makes no claim of collision avoidance or perception completeness (RSD-034).

16.D.2 Actors and responsibilities

Actor / containerResponsible forNot responsible for
Sensor + edgeCapture, detect / track / quality (step 01); transform local frame to the agreed map frame; publish scoped tracks with quality and lineage; health heartbeat; reserve queue capacity for health / critical events and apply the explicit drop policy (RSD-004, RSD-027)Deciding whether an observation is eligible evidence; any vehicle-facing message

Sensing, edge compute and communication have separate ownership (RSD-002). Each owner is accountable for the health signal of its own function, so a coverage degradation published at step 06 always carries an owner (RSD-013).

16.D.3 Preconditions and inputs

Field trust zone
The site has a site-scoped identity, clock and calibration; each sensor reports its calibrationRef and sensor revision; the edge runs signed model and config versions under a separate control plane (RSD-003, RSD-006).
Envelope contract
Each I09c ObservationEnvelope carries the fields listed in I09c, in particular sourceId, bootEpoch, seq, observedAt, emittedAt, clockErrorBound_s, expiresAt, trackKey, frameId, mapRev, calibrationRev, coverageRef, evidenceRef and payloadHash (RSD-016). CoverageHealth accompanies it (RSD-018).
Use-case thresholds
Age, association, coverage and queue-size thresholds for the use case are agreed before the path is enabled and are not fixed in this baseline (RSD-019, TBD-016). The per-signal freshness limit F_i is owned by Platform (TBD-006, decided at G2).
Vehicle evidence
C04 is projecting validated I04 samples with observation quality (OPS-021); vehicle and roadside envelopes remain separate sources (OPS-048).
Operator
Actions in steps 10–18 require a qualified seat holding the current lease on the case and acknowledging the current caseRev (OPS-011).
Evidence contract
A purpose, access and retention contract for raw clips exists before any clip is requested (RSD-030, TBD-020).

16.D.4 Behaviour

Main flow: eligible observation leads to a reviewed, guarded response. The ADS continues local DDT and fallback independently for the whole flow; onboard DDT and fallback never wait on any step of this flow (OPS-019).

  1. Sensor + edge detects and tracks an object or condition, attaching quality, the local track identity and the sensor revision (step 01).
  2. The edge transforms the track into the agreed map frame and publishes it on I09b as an observation with its coverage context; the heartbeat continues on the same path so that silence can be distinguished from absence of events (step 02).
  3. The RSU / backhaul gateway wraps the observation in an authenticated envelope and forwards it on I09c (step 03).
  4. C10 evaluates identity, age, frame and dedup in order (step 04, D16.3): schema / source / access (RSD-009); clock bound, age and sequence (RSD-010); frame / calibration / coverage (RSD-011); dedup by source, epoch and sequence (RSD-014). All checks must pass; any failure leaves the main flow (alternative flow A).
  5. C06 obtains the matching I04 pose / status / time / quality for vehicles in the observation's coverage (step 07).
  6. C06 runs the time-space association gate. Each candidate link between a roadside trackKey and a vehicle carries confidence, method and expiry; association remains probabilistic and no global identity is inferred from local track IDs (step 08, RSD-017, RSD-020, RSD-021).
  7. C06 presents the evidence, any conflicts with vehicle-reported state, quality, provenance and coverage state to the operator owning the case (step 09, RSD-024). If no case exists, the condition is evaluated by the P17 detection and triage logic, which decides whether to open one.
  8. Where the summary is insufficient, the operator requests a scoped clip or history; C06 issues an authorised evidence request and receives an EvidenceRef with source and retention (steps 10–12). Edge summaries come first; raw evidence only on request (RSD-030).
  9. If an action is warranted, the operator submits an action request with rationale. C06 applies the P22 action-specific guards: current authority, action-specific evidence and onboard capability (step 13, OPS-076).
  10. C06 sends the guarded advice or request on I07 via C04 (step 14, RSD-029). The ADS receives, accepts or rejects it with a reason (step 15) and reports execution and observed outcome (step 16) as separate evidence (OPS-001).
  11. C06 reports outcome or escalation to the operator (step 17). The operator reviews the outcome and closes the case only with fresh state and accepted release authority (step 18, OPS-014).
  12. C06 appends the audit record; fleet availability is then a separate decision under the P18 release gate (step 19, RSD-032).

Alternative flow A: ineligible envelope (steps 05–06).

  1. C10 classifies the envelope as quarantine or diagnostic, never silently dropped (RSD-012).
  2. C10 returns a reject / diagnostic receipt to the source naming the failed check, so the field owner can correct it.
  3. If the failure is a coverage failure, C10 also publishes coverage degraded with an owner to C06 (RSD-013); the operator sees that a region is no longer observed, not that it is clear (RSD-015).
  4. An envelope with an unknown clock bound is rejected with time validity UNKNOWN; it is not re-timed with the receive time (RSD-010).

Alternative flow B: no action warranted. The operator reviews the evidence (step 09) and records that no action is required, with the evidence reference and case revision kept on the annotation (OPS-067). The case follows the normal closure rule; the roadside evidence remains attached for review.

Alternative flow C: ADS rejects the advice or request (step 15). The rejection reason is recorded, the case stays open, and C06 either queries state or initiates an approved fallback (OPS-009). No component automatically resends the request under a new ID (OPS-004); a renewed operator request passes the action-specific guards again with current evidence (OPS-076).

Exception flow D: link / edge loss (D16.1).

  1. Heartbeat expiry sets coverage UNKNOWN for the affected coverage; C10 retains the source time of the last valid sample and publishes coverage degraded with an owner (RSD-025).
  2. The operator view stops presenting any frame from that source as current (OPS-023).
  3. On reconnect, including after reboot, the edge uses a new bootEpoch; C10 performs resync and health checks and re-qualifies observations before any becomes eligible (RSD-026); regional failover likewise uses a new epoch and re-qualifies observations (RSD-007).
  4. Buffered samples delivered late, reordered or duplicated are deduplicated by source / epoch / seq and admitted as history only, with their original observation time (RSD-014, RSD-026).
  5. Return of coverage does not release any vehicle capacity (RSD-028).

Exception flow E: conflict or overload (D16.2). When roadside and vehicle evidence disagree, C06 keeps both claims as separate hypotheses with provenance and quality and presents them as a conflict; it does not overwrite vehicle-reported state (RSD-022). Under saturation, the edge protects health / critical traffic, drops according to the explicit policy (TBD-019) and reports queue age and dropped observations; C10 quarantines the affected observations and publishes coverage degradation (RSD-027).

16.D.5 Rules and invariants

  1. R16.1 No actuation path. No roadside observation reaches the vehicle except as part of an operator action that has passed the P22 guards on I07 (RSD-029, RSD-001).
  2. R16.2 Eligibility before use. C06 consumes only envelopes that C10 has classified as accepted (RSD-009, RSD-012).
  3. R16.3 Unknown is not clear. Unknown or lost coverage is never interpreted as a clear road; absence of detections in a degraded coverage region carries no meaning (RSD-015).
  4. R16.4 Time is preserved. The original observation time travels with the observation; repeated or replayed samples never refresh it (RSD-014, OPS-048).
  5. R16.5 Replay is history. Replayed or late samples are historical only and cannot enable a live action (RSD-026, OPS-023).
  6. R16.6 Association stays probabilistic. A vehicle link carries confidence, method and expiry; an expired link is not evidence (RSD-020, RSD-021).
  7. R16.7 Conflicts are retained. Disagreeing claims are kept side by side with lineage; multiple reports of the same object retain source lineage so they are not double counted (RSD-022, RSD-023).
  8. R16.8 Every failure is visible. Every rejected envelope yields a diagnostic receipt; every coverage failure yields coverage degraded with an owner (RSD-012, RSD-013).
  9. R16.9 Closure is not release. Case closure and fleet release are separate predicates; closure appends audit before the release gate is evaluated (RSD-032, OPS-015).
  10. R16.10 Independence of the ADS. No step suspends, delays or conditions onboard DDT or fallback (OPS-019).

C10 owns no D store (Appendix B C10); its outputs are classifications and events. The data that matters per stage is:

Recovery from any roadside failure restores only the eligibility of roadside evidence. It never changes vehicle mode, case state or fleet eligibility on its own.

16.D.9 Security, privacy and audit

Trust is established in layers: site-scoped identity within the field trust zone, separate RSU / backhaul identity and rate limit, signature or authenticated transport with payloadHash on each envelope, and C10 access checks scoped by tenantId (ASM-009). An envelope that authenticates but fails tenant or site scope is rejected, not reassigned. Edge models and configuration are signed and versioned, so modelRev on an observation identifies the signed model version that produced it (RSD-006).

Roadside capture can contain people who are not passengers. Raw clips therefore move only under a purpose, access and retention contract; summaries are sent by default and raw evidence only on an authorised, case-scoped request; replay is read-only (RSD-030, OPS-087). Every action decision and closure appends an audit record carrying the evidence references, policy version and actor (OPS-085); raw events and validation results are append-only (OPS-086). Audit and guard testing covers cross-tenant access, expired authority, future timestamps, unknown clock bounds and duplicate effects (OPS-088).

16.D.10 Observability and operations

  • Field health: CPU, memory, queue age and sensor health from edge management; dropped observations and queue age per source; coverage state per coverageId with its owner.
  • Ingest quality: counts of accepted, quarantined and diagnostic outcomes per source and per failed check, so a calibration drift or clock fault can show as a trend before it becomes a coverage loss.
  • Evidence age: end-to-end age from observedAt to presentation, measured against the freshness budget (TBD-006).
  • Operator load: roadside-originated cases, evidence requests and conflicts presented per seat, feeding the workload acceptance of P21 14.3.

Regional observation workers scale independently of ADS control (RSD-031), so roadside load can grow without contending with ADS control for capacity.

16.D.11 Verification approach

All cases are planned tests, not passed results (ASM-030). Each run records scenario, initial state, revisions, injected fault, trace and oracle result (OPS-094).

CaseInjectionOracle
DisconnectCut backhaul or edgeCoverage UNKNOWN; owner published; no stale frame shown as current; capacity unchanged (RSD-035)
RebootRestart edgeNew bootEpoch; no eligibility before resync; no track joined by key across epochs
Reordering / duplicateReorder and repeat envelopesOriginal observation time unchanged; duplicates produce no second evidence item
Clock / calibrationClock jump; unknown bound; calibration mismatchReject or quarantine with receipt; time validity UNKNOWN where applicable (P24 17.2)
Occlusion / weatherDegraded coverage conditionsCoverage state reflects exclusions; absence of detections not shown as clear (RSD-036)
False associationTwo vehicles within the gate; roadside contradicts vehicleBoth hypotheses with confidence; no override of ADS state
SaturationExceed edge capacityHealth traffic delivered; drops reported; quarantine and degradation published
Bypass attemptAction derived from roadside evidence without guardsRejected by the P22 guards

Measures are quality, end-to-end age and operator workload. Tests run in SIL / HIL / operator / vehicle trials as applicable, as G3 evidence (OPS-094).

16.D.12 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Monitoring, not actuation
Fusing roadside tracks into the vehicle's onboard perception would make ADS safety depend on a field installation with different ownership, calibration and availability. Keeping roadside data on the monitoring side keeps the ADS safety case independent of the roadside installation and lets the roadside path be gated, scaled or switched off independently.
Reject rather than repair
Re-timing an envelope with its receive time, or guessing a calibration, would turn an unknown into an apparently valid fact. Rejection with a diagnostic receipt keeps the fault with its owner and keeps the evidence honest.
Probabilistic association
A deterministic match on position would produce silent false links in dense traffic. Confidence, method and expiry make the uncertainty part of the record the operator acts on.
Keep both claims
Letting either source win automatically hides exactly the disagreements an operator most needs to see. Retaining both, with lineage, also prevents double counting when several sensors report the same object.
New epoch on reconnect
Continuing the old sequence after a reboot would let buffered samples be mistaken for live ones. A new epoch makes the discontinuity explicit and forces re-qualification.
Closure separate from release
A roadside-triggered case can close because the road condition is understood while the vehicle still needs inspection. Tying release to closure would return a vehicle to service on the wrong evidence.

  • Sensor selection and the selected V2X interface (TBD-017); CPM mapping and radio profile (TBD-018).
  • Explicit drop policy under overload (TBD-019).
  • Raw-clip purpose, access and retention contract and regional placement of evidence (TBD-020).
  • Gating of C10 and I09 as a whole (TBD-021).
  • Freshness budgets and clock-bound parameters (TBD-006, TBD-007); protocols (TBD-003).

10.1Signal families, decision context and missing-data behaviour

ADS / ODD

  • adsMode, engagementState, oddVerdict/reason, oddProfileRev

ODD or mode inconsistency opens a case. Cloud context never widens ODD.

Motion / localisation

Detect unexpected stop / deviation. Uncertain pose cannot prove location.

Perception / planning

  • sensorHealth, occlusionFlags, plannerStatus, blockageReason

Review ambiguity in context. Generic “AI confidence” cannot permit motion.

P0Collision / fire / SOS / failed fallback. Immediate escalation, no debounce.

17.DDetailed specification

This section specifies how vehicle and roadside signals become alarms and how alarms are handled until they clear (RM-03 / RM-04). It defines what each signal family may and may not be used to conclude, the validation every sample passes before detection, the detection, correlation, assignment, action and clear stages of the alarm lifecycle, the meaning of the P0–P3 response classes, the rules for acknowledgement, snooze, grouping and reopening, and how missing data are handled as events in their own right. Parameter values (freshness limits, persistence, hysteresis, stable intervals) are owned outside this chapter and are linked as open items.

17.D.1 Purpose and scope

Remote monitoring is only useful if an operator can trust that an alarm reflects current, valid evidence and that the absence of an alarm is not a guess. The design therefore starts from the signal, not from the alarm: every sample is validated for identity, schema, unit, epoch / sequence and time before it may contribute to detection, and a sample that fails validation is not ignored but raises its own event (OPS-037, OPS-043).

The P0–P3 classes are operational response classes that tell the operations centre how fast and with what escalation to respond. They are not ASIL classifications and carry no claim about the safety integrity of any onboard function (OPS-044, ASM-022). Onboard safety decisions stay with the ADS throughout; nothing in this chapter adds a cloud path into them (OPS-017).

In scope: the six signal families of 10.1, the lifecycle of 10.2 and its detail figures (D17.1, D17.2, D17.3). The case lifecycle and owner lease that an alarm feeds are defined in P13 6.1; the operator workspace in P21; the time-validity formula in P22 15.3.

Signals are interpreted per channel: loss of the evidence / media channel says nothing about the telemetry / alarm channel, and vice versa. Health of one channel is never inferred from another (OPS-020).

17.D.4 Behaviour

Main flow: from sample to cleared alarm (D17.1, D17.3).

  1. Receive. A sample arrives in its source envelope: I04 for vehicle signals, I09 for roadside observations. The two are never merged into one envelope (OPS-048).
  2. Validate. C04 (for I04) and C06 evaluate valid_i: identity, schema, unit, source, epoch / sequence, and timeOK_i using the bounded clock error of P22 15.3 (OPS-079). A sample without a finite clock bound has time validity UNKNOWN; a future-dated sample is rejected (OPS-080).
  3. Detect. C06 evaluates the versioned detection predicate for the signal. Non-P0 predicates require persistence and apply hysteresis so that a value oscillating around a limit does not open and close alarms repeatedly; P0 predicates fire on the first valid sample, with no debounce (OPS-043, OPS-044, TBD-025).
  4. Correlate. C06 groups the alarm by vehicle, cause and incident window. Correlated roadside evidence is attached with its quality and provenance. Severity, exposure (passengers on board or waiting, location) and dueAt are computed (transition 1 of D17.1).
  5. Triage. The alarm is given its response class P0–P3 and a case is opened with OpenCase(command, last observation, severity, deadline) (OPS-010).
  6. Assign. C06 assigns the case to one qualified seat under a single action lease with dueAt; the owner ACKs the current caseRev (OPS-011). ACK records ownership; it does not change alarm health.
  7. Act. Where an action is required, the owner requests it under the P22 action-specific guards, with current evidence and expected state (OPS-076).
  8. Verify. C06 observes the outcome on I04 (execution evidence, not receipt) and evaluates the clear condition (OPS-005).
  9. Clear. The alarm clears only when valid samples span the agreed stable interval with the clear condition holding (OPS-045, TBD-026). Clearing an alarm does not by itself close the case or release capacity; those follow P13 6.1 and P18 11.3.

Alternative flows.

  1. Reopen. Contradictory evidence after clear, or material new evidence on a resolved or closed case, returns the alarm to active handling and reopens the case (OPS-045, OPS-013).
  2. Common-cause grouping. When several vehicles alarm from one cause (a road closure, a regional link fault), C06 links them as one incident for coordination but keeps each vehicle's exposure, deadline and response class. The group's priority is never lower than its most urgent member, and resolving the group does not resolve any member without that member's own evidence (OPS-047).
  3. Snooze. An owner may snooze a P1–P3 alarm with a reason and an expiry; on expiry the alarm returns to active handling with its original detection time. P0 cannot be snoozed (OPS-046). Snooze defers attention; it does not change the case deadline unless the owner revises it with a reason.
  4. Worsening. A P2 alarm whose exposure increases, or whose predicate now meets a P1 or P0 condition, is re-triaged to the higher class; the case keeps its identity and history.
  5. Scheduled work. A P3 alarm results in work scheduled under explicit restrictions recorded against the vehicle; the restriction remains visible to C03 until cleared.

Exception flows.

  1. Missing / invalid data. A sample that fails validation, or a signal whose freshness lapses, raises its own event and marks that signal UNKNOWN; detection on that signal is suspended, not evaluated against the last value (transition 6 of D17.1). Where the unknown signal is required for the vehicle's active state, the event is itself a P1 trigger (unknown active state).
  2. Link loss. All signals on the channel become UNKNOWN; C03 holds the affected capacity and C06 preserves incident ownership (OPS-026). Read-only queries and emergency escalation remain available (OPS-075).
  3. Lease lapse. A lease that expires, a missing ACK or an urgent deadline leads to rejection of any action carrying the stale lease and assignment of a backup owner with a new lease (transition 5, OPS-012).
  4. Alarm storm. Under an alarm burst, P0 alarms are never hidden behind lower classes or grouping (P24 T-R08); new commitments are restricted when response capacity is exhausted (OPS-074).

17.D.5 Rules and invariants

  1. R17.1 Only samples with valid_i true contribute to detection or to action evidence (OPS-079).
  2. R17.2 Missing is never healthy: an absent, stale or invalid signal is explicit uncertainty with its own event (OPS-021, OPS-037).
  3. R17.3 Original observation time is preserved; repeated or replayed samples never refresh it, and cannot extend the stable interval needed for clear (OPS-048).
  4. R17.4 P0 has no debounce, cannot be snoozed and is never hidden by grouping (OPS-044, OPS-046).
  5. R17.5 ACK assigns ownership; it never clears health (OPS-045).
  6. R17.6 Clear requires valid samples spanning the agreed stable interval; contradictory evidence reopens (OPS-045).
  7. R17.7 Grouping keeps per-vehicle exposure and deadline (OPS-047).
  8. R17.8 Cloud context never widens the ODD; an ODD or mode inconsistency opens a case (OPS-038).
  9. R17.9 Manoeuvre progress is not achieved MRC; zero speed is not MRC (OPS-040).
  10. R17.10 Every open alarm and case has an owner and a deadline; expiry of ownership produces reassignment, never silent abandonment (OPS-012, OPS-016).
  11. R17.11 Detection predicates are versioned; an alarm records the predicate version that raised it, so a change of predicate never silently re-labels history (OPS-037).

17.D.6 Data and state

An alarm is a C06 record linked to a vehicle case in D5. It carries the vehicle, the triggering signal family and signal, the predicate version, the original observation time of the triggering sample, the response class, severity, exposure and dueAt, the owner and lease, and the evidence references used. The lifecycle positions are those of D17.1: validate / detect, correlate / assign, act / verify, clear / release, with the side positions escalation and missing / invalid data.

ClassTypical triggersCapacity effectEscalation basisParameter owner
P0Collision, fire, SOS, failed fallbackAffected vehicle heldImmediate; supervisor and emergency escalation available at onceOperations (TBD-008)
P1ODD exit, MRM, critical fault, unknown active stateHold capacityUrgent deadline; backup owner on missed ACKOperations
P2Assistance, obstruction, boarding failureAssessed per exposure; ETA revised where affectedEscalate if worseningOperations
P3Noncritical service or diagnostic issueExplicit restriction recordedScheduled workOperations

Remote knowledge per signal (CURRENT / DEGRADED / UNKNOWN, P18 11.2) is computed from validation and freshness and is held separately from the alarm. A signal can be CURRENT and still report a fault; a signal can be UNKNOWN without any alarm on its value. Raw events and validation results are kept append-only (OPS-086).

17.D.7 Interfaces used

I04
Telemetry / alarm channel: reliable events, heartbeat, seq, the 10.1 signals and channel metrics; Status(boot,seq). Command / result channel for verification evidence.
I09c
Accepted roadside observations, passed on by C10, with coverageRef, frame / map / calibrationRev, clock bound and source lineage.
I07
OpenCase, Assign(lease,dueAt), ACK(caseRev), Escalate / new lease, Action + evidence, Authorise scoped action.
C09
CaseChanged events to consumers such as C03 (capacity hold) and C02 (passenger communication) (C09).

17.D.8 Failure handling and recovery

FailureBehaviourRecovery
Clock jump or unknown bound at sourcetimeOK_i false or UNKNOWN; samples cannot be action evidence; queries stay usable (OPS-080)Valid clock bound re-established; new samples, not old ones, restore CURRENT
Sequence gapseqGap is itself a link metric; the gap qualifies the remote-knowledge state of the affected signals and is preserved as an evidence gapSubsequent valid samples; the gap remains in the record
Vehicle rebootNew bootEpoch; prior-epoch state is historyFresh samples under the new epoch
Detection predicate defectPredicate versions allow affected alarms to be identified and re-reviewedCorrected version released; history keeps the original label
Seat failureLease lapses; backup owner assigned; relief capacity used (OPS-068)Handover accepted by receiving owner (OPS-063)
Centre lossAlarms and cases survive in the durable store; authority moves under P20Backup centre resumes ownership after fencing

17.D.9 Security, privacy and audit

Samples are accepted only from authenticated producers within the tenant scope; identityOK and sourceOK are part of valid_i. Snooze, reclassification, grouping and clear are audited with actor, reason, time and case revision (OPS-067), because each of them changes what other operators will see. Service AI may summarise alarms within task scope but cannot clear, snooze a P0 or authorise motion (OPS-089). Passenger signals (SOS, occupancy) are personal data and follow the purpose-limited capture and scoped access rules of P22 15.4 (OPS-087).

17.D.10 Observability and operations

  • Per vehicle and channel: signal age, validity and remote-knowledge state, shown per signal in the workspace (OPS-064).
  • Per alarm: detection time, ACK time, resolution time and overdue state, the measures named for workload acceptance (OPS-073).
  • Per predicate version: alarm counts, reopen counts and clear-then-reopen intervals, used to tune persistence and hysteresis through a versioned release rather than ad hoc edits.
  • Per seat: open leases, oldest unacknowledged case and snoozed alarms with their expiries.

17.D.11 Verification approach

Planned caseInjectionOracle
T-R01Delay, reorder, clock jump, rebootStale / future data blocks motion; query stays usable; no refresh of observation time
T-R02ODD limit / sensor degradationCorrect class; case opened; no remote extension of ODD
T-R05Lose telemetry / media / voice independentlyIndependent quality flags per channel; UNKNOWN, not healthy
T-R07SOS + MRM failure / no field teamP0 raised without debounce; work remains owned
T-R08Alarm storm / unauthorised AINo hidden P0; grouping keeps per-vehicle deadlines; AI motion authorisation denied
Hysteresis boundarySignal oscillating at a predicate limitOne alarm, not a sequence of open / clear pairs
ACK without clearACK while fault persistsAlarm stays active; health unchanged
SnoozeSnooze P1 with expiry; attempt snooze on P0P1 returns at expiry; P0 snooze refused

The T-R cases are those of P24 17.1 and are planned, not passed. Boundary tests for each parameter are part of its definition (OPS-084).

17.D.12 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Response classes, not ASIL
Mapping operations priorities onto a functional-safety classification would imply that the centre participates in the safety function. It does not: the ADS retains DDT and fallback. Response classes describe the centre's obligations only.
No debounce for P0
Debouncing trades detection latency for fewer false alarms. For collision, fire, SOS and failed fallback, a false alarm is cheaper than a delayed response, so P0 accepts the trade-off explicitly.
Missing data as events
Treating silence as "no alarm" is a common way for monitoring systems to fail quietly. Making absence an event forces it to be owned.
ACK separate from clear
Combining them would let workload pressure clear alarms that are still true. Separation keeps "someone is on it" distinct from "it is fixed".
Separate envelopes
Merging I04 and I09 into one state would lose which source said what, and would let roadside data appear to be vehicle-reported. Keeping them apart preserves provenance through to the operator.
Generic confidence rejected
A single score summarising perception would be easy to display and hard to verify. Scene-bound evidence (sceneRev, mapRev, capture time) is reviewable.

17.D.13 Open points

  • Detection predicate, persistence and hysteresis per signal (TBD-025).
  • Stable interval for clear (TBD-026).
  • Freshness limit F_i and clock-bound parameters (TBD-006, decided at G2; TBD-007).
  • Response-class deadlines, seat / field coverage and escalation (TBD-008); remote response deadline components (TBD-010).
  • Complete telemetry schema (TBD-040).

Orthogonal states and guarded return to service

RM-05. ADS operation, assistance workflow, remote knowledge and fleet eligibility are separate dimensions. An ADS can continue its approved local behaviour while a remote assistance request is pending.

11.1Vehicle-reported operating state: selected transitions

11.2Assistance lifecycle runs independently of ADS operation

  1. REQUESTED / ASSIGNED
    • SceneRef + requestId + dueAt
    • Qualified owner + bounded lease
  2. ADVICE / VEHICLE REVIEW
    • Current scene / capability / expiry
    • ADS accepts or rejects advice
  3. RESOLVED / ESCALATED
    • Observed outcome or owned follow-up
    • No implied ADS mode transition

Remote knowledge

CURRENT / DEGRADED / UNKNOWN is per required signal. Fresh data may still report a fault. Unknown physical execution blocks conflicting reuse.

Fleet eligibility / case state

AVAILABLE / RESTRICTED / HELD differs from OPEN / ACTIVE / CLOSED. Closing a case never changes ADS mode or automatically clears an operational hold.

D18.1State machineAssistance request lifecycle, independent of ADS mode

The three stages of 11.2 split into their states and exits, following the P19 RM-06A sequence. Every transition changes only the assistance workflow; ADS mode, remote knowledge and fleet eligibility move independently (for example DDT_ACTIVE + RA_PENDING).

↓
RELEASE_ELIGIBLE = V ∧ C ∧ A ∧ F

Test cross-products, not only one state chain: DDT_ACTIVE + RA_PENDING; MRC + stale evidence; CLOSED case + critical fault; fresh telemetry + unresolved command. A reported zero speed never suffices for MRC or restart.

D18.2Decision logicRelease-predicate evaluation: V, C, A, F → RELEASE_ELIGIBLE

The four predicates of 11.3 evaluated as a conjunction. Each predicate is checked on its own evidence; a passing predicate never compensates for a failing one. Only a full pass lets C03 reassess availability, and even then no command is sent to the ADS.

18.DDetailed specification

This section specifies the RM-05 state model: the separate state dimensions that together describe a vehicle in remote operations, who owns and may change each one, which combinations are legal, and the guarded return-to-service process in which the four release predicates V, C, A and F are evaluated independently before C03 may reassess availability. It also specifies the failure cases where dimensions disagree, the audit carried by a release decision, and the cross-product verification that the chapter requires.

18.D.1 Purpose and scope

A single vehicle status field that tries to say "driving", "waiting for help", "connection lost" and "out of service" at once forces false implications: that resolving an assistance request restarts the vehicle, that a reconnect means the vehicle is fine, or that closing a case returns capacity. The design avoids this by holding each concern as its own dimension with its own owner and evidence, and by making return to service a conjunction of independent predicates rather than a transition of any one dimension (OPS-049, OPS-052).

In scope: the vehicle-reported operating state of 11.1 (as the centre observes it), the assistance lifecycle of 11.2 (D18.1), remote knowledge, fleet eligibility and case state, and the release predicates of 11.3 (D18.2, D18.3). The assistance transaction itself is in P19; centre change and fencing in P20; service-mode transitions for the whole service in P27.

18.D.2 State dimensions and ownership

DimensionStates (as stated)Owner of truthChanged byNever changed by
ADS operation (vehicle-reported)READY / STATIONARY, DDT ACTIVE, MRM EXECUTING, MRC REPORTED, OUT OF SERVICE, RE-ENTRY CHECKVehicle / ADS; observed by C04The ADS, and field action / failure evidence for OUT OF SERVICECase closure, assistance outcome, reconnect, release approval
Assistance workflowREQUESTED, ASSIGNED, ADVICE, VEHICLE REVIEW, RESOLVED, ESCALATEDC06RARequest, assignment, advice, onboard accept / reject, observed outcomeADS mode changes (it is informed by them, not driven)
Remote knowledgeCURRENT / DEGRADED / UNKNOWN per required signalC04 projection, used by C06 and C03Validation and freshness of samples (P22 15.3)Operator assertion; case state
Fleet eligibilityAVAILABLE / RESTRICTED / HELDC03Hold on incident or unknown; reassessment after RELEASE_ELIGIBLEConnectivity restoration alone; case closure alone (OPS-055)
Case stateOPEN / ACTIVE / CLOSED (lifecycle detail in P13 6.1)C06 in D5Case workflow, material new evidence (reopen)Never changes ADS mode or clears a hold (OPS-015)

The command journal in D3 (delivery and execution per commandId, P13 6.1) is a further independent record that the A predicate reads. UNKNOWN in that journal is observer knowledge, not a vehicle state (ASM-023).

18.D.3 Preconditions and inputs

Vehicle state
The vehicle reports its operating state, mrmState, mrcAchieved, standstill / secureState and fallbackReason on I04 with provenance (P17 10.1).
Required signals
The set of signals required for release of a given vehicle and mission type is defined, so that V can be evaluated as "all required signals CURRENT and mutually consistent". The set and its freshness limits are Platform parameters (TBD-006).
Release authority
The role that may approve release is mapped to the permitted operation and designated supervisor (OPS-025).
Mission context
C02 holds the passenger outcome; the D1 permit is current only for CONFIRMED with no pending cancel (BKG-047); C03 and C05 can reconcile route, energy and resource bundle.

18.D.4 Behaviour

Vehicle-reported transitions (11.1). The centre does not drive these transitions; it records them as observed and reacts on the other dimensions.

  1. engage: READY / STATIONARY → DDT ACTIVE on local readiness. Mission acceptance is a separate event on the command journal.
  2. fallback: DDT ACTIVE → MRM EXECUTING, triggered locally. C06 opens or updates a case at P1 (P17); C03 holds capacity.
  3. achieved: MRM EXECUTING → MRC REPORTED only with achieved-condition evidence and provenance; remaining hazards are assessed. Zero speed is not this evidence (OPS-040). A failed fallback is P0.
  4. eligible: MRC REPORTED → RE-ENTRY CHECK when the vehicle and the case are ready for reconciliation of readiness, ODD and authority plus physical and mission state (OPS-051).
  5. passed local checks: RE-ENTRY CHECK → READY / STATIONARY. This is the vehicle's own readiness; it is not service release.
  6. fails and field action / failure evidence: to OUT OF SERVICE, where the hold remains until evidence clears; no recovery path is assumed.

Main flow: guarded return to service (D18.2).

  1. An incident, fault or unknown places the vehicle in HELD; the hold records its cause and the case that owns it.
  2. The vehicle reaches a state from which return is possible (READY / STATIONARY after a passed RE-ENTRY CHECK), and the owner requests a release review on the current case revision.
  3. C06 evaluates V from C04: every required signal CURRENT and mutually consistent, local readiness and ODD status accepted (OPS-053).
  4. C06 evaluates C from the case and field recovery record: the cause removed, or an approved restriction recorded, and required field / inspection work complete with evidence attached by a qualified field responder (OPS-053, OPS-071).
  5. C06 evaluates A: current case revision, valid release authority, no blocking incident and no unresolved command in the D3 journal (OPS-054).
  6. C06 obtains F from C02, C03 and C05: passenger outcome known, D1 permit current, route, energy and resource bundle reconciled (OPS-054).
  7. If all four hold, the guarded approval is recorded and C03 reassesses availability. C03 sets AVAILABLE, or RESTRICTED where recorded restrictions remain. No command is sent to the ADS (OPS-055).
  8. The case may then close with the closing evidence (OPS-014); or it may have closed earlier, in which case the hold still requires this flow.

Alternative flows.

  1. Release with restriction. Where the cause cannot be removed but an approved restriction (for example an excluded area or mission type) addresses it, C holds on the recorded restriction and C03 reflects it as RESTRICTED. The restriction stays recorded until a later review removes it.
  2. Assistance resolves while ADS continues. DDT ACTIVE with an assistance request pending is a normal combination; RESOLVED changes only the assistance workflow (OPS-049). If no hold was placed, no release flow is needed.
  3. Fresh autonomous resolution. The ADS resolves the situation itself; the assistance request moves to RESOLVED on the observed outcome (transition 8 of D18.1), with no implied mode transition.

Exception flows.

  1. Evidence goes stale during review. If any required signal leaves CURRENT before the approval is recorded, V fails and the review restarts on fresh evidence; an approval is never recorded on evidence that has aged out.
  2. Case revision changes during review. A new caseRev (new evidence, reassignment) invalidates A; the review is repeated on the current revision.
  3. Material new evidence after release. The case reopens (OPS-013) and C03 holds again if the evidence affects safety or feasibility.
  4. Unresolved command. Unknown physical execution of a prior command blocks conflicting reuse of the vehicle (OPS-050); A cannot hold until the command reaches terminal evidence or is reconciled (P20 13.1).
  5. Deadline with outcome unknown. The uncertainty is retained as an owned exception with deadline, backup owner and fallback; re-entry is authorised only on current evidence (OPS-097).

18.D.5 Rules and invariants

  1. R18.1 The dimensions are independent: a change in one never implies a change in another (OPS-049).
  2. R18.2 RELEASE_ELIGIBLE = V ∧ C ∧ A ∧ F, each on its own evidence; no predicate substitutes for another (OPS-052).
  3. R18.3 Release approval only lets C03 reassess availability; it never commands motion (OPS-055).
  4. R18.4 Closing a case never changes ADS mode, clears a hold or releases capacity (OPS-015).
  5. R18.5 MRC REPORTED is not ready to drive; zero speed never suffices for MRC or restart (OPS-040).
  6. R18.6 Remote knowledge is per required signal; fresh data reporting a fault still counts as a fault (OPS-050).
  7. R18.7 Connectivity restoration alone cannot release capacity; reconnect does not trigger automatic re-entry (OPS-055, OPS-036).
  8. R18.8 OUT OF SERVICE holds until evidence clears (OPS-051).
  9. R18.9 Every open branch, including a hold that is not yet releasable, retains an owner and a deadline (OPS-016).

18.D.6 Data and state

A release decision is a record in D5 against the case. It carries the case revision evaluated, the result of each predicate with the evidence references it used (signal revisions and observation times for V; field record and restriction for C; authority, incident and journal check for A; passenger outcome, D1 permit and bundle reference for F), the approver and the remaining restrictions. A failed evaluation is recorded the same way, naming the failing predicate, so the hold's owner knows what must change.

Legal combination (examples)Meaning
DDT_ACTIVE + RA_PENDING + AVAILABLEADS continues approved behaviour while help is pending; capacity unaffected unless ETA is affected
MRC REPORTED + CURRENT + HELD + OPENVehicle stopped in an achieved condition; still held pending V, C, A, F
READY / STATIONARY + UNKNOWN + HELDVehicle may be ready locally but the centre cannot know; held
CLOSED + HELDCase work done; vehicle still awaiting release (for example inspection pending)
CURRENT + fault reported + HELDFresh data reporting a fault is a fault

No combination is forbidden by construction, because each dimension reflects what is actually known. What is forbidden is a derivation across dimensions, such as reading AVAILABLE from CLOSED.

18.D.7 Interfaces used

I04
Vehicle-reported state and required signals for V; command journal state for A.
I07
Case workflow, release decision (step 24 of P13 6.1).
C03 / C02 / C05
Hold and reassessment of availability; passenger outcome; energy and route feasibility (Appendix B C03).
C09
CaseChanged and availability changes to consumers.

18.D.8 Failure handling and recovery

Each failure resolves toward HELD. Where the centre is uncertain, the vehicle is held and the uncertainty is owned; where the vehicle is uncertain, the ADS acts locally and the centre observes. A release decision lost in transit is not re-inferred: C03 reassesses only on a recorded approval, and if the record cannot be confirmed the vehicle stays HELD. After a fault, projections are rebuilt from the durable journal without side effects and the predicates are re-evaluated on them (OPS-096).

18.D.9 Security, privacy and audit

Release authority is role-bound and checked against the current case revision; an approval by a role without that authority is rejected, not queued. Each release and each failed evaluation is audited with actor, time, case revision and evidence references (OPS-085). Service AI may draft a release summary but cannot record an approval (OPS-089).

18.D.10 Observability and operations

  • Held vehicles with cause, owner, deadline and the failing predicate.
  • Time from hold to release, broken down by the predicate that was last to pass.
  • Reopen after release, as a quality signal on the release process.
  • Vehicles in RESTRICTED with their restrictions, visible to C03 planning.

18.D.11 Verification approach

Verification tests cross-products, not single chains (OPS-095, D18.3). Beyond the four named combinations, each predicate is tested failing alone while the other three pass, to show that none compensates.

CaseSet-upExpected
DDT_ACTIVE + RA_PENDINGRequest pending while drivingNo mode change; no hold unless ETA affected
MRC + stale evidenceMRC reported, required signal staleV fails; HELD
CLOSED case + critical faultClose case, inject faultHold persists; case reopens on the fault
fresh telemetry + unresolved commandFresh signals, prior command UNKNOWNA fails; reuse blocked
Only V fails / only C / only A / only FThree pass, one failsNot release-eligible in every case
Zero speed without MRCspeed zero, mrcAchieved absentNot MRC; no restart
Reconnect onlyLink restored, nothing elseHELD unchanged (OPS-055)
Stale revision approvalApprove on old caseRevRejected

T-R02 and T-R07 of P24 exercise the dimension separation under ODD limits and failed MRM. All are planned tests.

18.D.12 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Single status enum
Rejected. It cannot express legal combinations such as DDT_ACTIVE + RA_PENDING without multiplying states, and every multiplication invites a transition that implies something untrue.
Release by case closure
Rejected. Case work and vehicle readiness finish at different times and are evidenced by different parties.
Weighted release score
Rejected. A score lets strong evidence in one area mask missing evidence in another. A conjunction makes each gap visible and owned.
Centre-commanded restart
Rejected. Release only changes what C03 may plan; motion follows a new mission accepted by the ADS, which keeps the ADS as the authority over its own readiness.

18.D.13 Open points

  • Required-signal sets and freshness limits per vehicle and mission type (TBD-006).
  • ODD and DDT fallback definitions that bound V (TBD-011, TBD-012).
  • Service-mode triggers and recovery thresholds that interact with fleet eligibility (TBD-028).
  • Operating limits for staffing and recovery that affect C (TBD-013).
  • Implementation and safety validation (TBD-052).
