RM-06 invariant:an advice response cannot widen ODD, disable collision avoidance or create a direct actuator path. Timeout/rejection requires reassessment; fresh autonomous resolution can close the case. Executing effects retain their identity.

D19.1SequenceAdvice rejection path: onboard validation fails, old advice is discarded

The else branch of RM-06A (steps 14, 15, 20, 21) as its own sequence. Rejection, expiry or a scene change makes the advice void: it is discarded rather than retried, the original id is queried, and the case either receives fresh context or escalates. Capacity stays held while the outcome is unresolved.

D19.2State machineAdvice object: delivery and onboard execution states

One advice is a command-like object with its own identity (adviceId). Delivery and execution are separate evidence chains: Receipt(adviceId) proves delivery only; acceptance alone does not prove progress. Terminal states are recorded with a reason in the immutable outcome envelope.

StateProvesDoes not prove

Missing terminal evidence stays unresolved. UNKNOWN belongs to the observer, not the ADS.

19.DDetailed specification

This section specifies the RM-06 contextual advice transaction: the conditions under which a remote assistance request may receive advice, the content and bounds of an advice, how it is guarded, delivered, validated onboard and observed, and how rejection, expiry, scene change, lost responses and autonomous resolution are handled. Throughout, the ADS keeps trajectory generation, collision checks and motion control; an advice is information the ADS may use or refuse, never a control input. Remote assistance is separately gated and outside the MVP (TBD-023).

19.D.1 Purpose and scope

The chapter's example is an ambiguous obstruction: the ADS can see something it cannot classify with enough certainty to plan around, and its approved local behaviour may be to stop or hold. A remote assistant with broader context (additional views, history, local knowledge) can tell the ADS something about the scene, such as that an object is static or that a lane may be used, so that the ADS can re-plan. The design question is how to allow that help without creating a remote driving path. The answer is a bounded transaction: advice is scoped to a scene revision, carries an expiry, is limited to the vehicle's supported capability and the current operating envelope, and is validated onboard before the ADS decides whether to use it (OPS-057, OPS-058).

In scope: RM-06A steps 01–23, the RM-06 invariant and the detail figures (D19.1, D19.2, D19.3). The assistance workflow states are in P18 11.2 (D18.1); the action schema and guards in P22; the workspace in P21. Real-time remote DDT is outside the baseline and is not specified here (OPS-018, TBD-024).

19.D.2 Actors and responsibilities

ActorDoesDoes not
Vehicle / ADSRaises RARequest(sceneRev); continues approved local behaviour; validates advice onboard; accepts or rejects with reason; plans and executes independently; reports execution, end or renewed need (Appendix B vehicle trust zone)Wait for advice before applying fallback; accept advice that fails validation
C04 gatewayForwards the request with evidence and quality; serves Fetch(sceneRev); persists and forwards GuardedAdvice; records receipt, accept / reject and execution as separate evidence on one identity (OPS-001)Resend advice under a new ID (OPS-004)
C06 case / policyOpens and assigns the case under a lease; checks evidence sufficiency; applies action-specific guards; converts Advice into GuardedAdvice; tracks outcome; reconciles with C03; closes or retains the case (Appendix B C06)Issue advice outside supported capability or the current operating envelope
RA operatorAcknowledges the case and request view; reviews scene, age, media and quality; issues Advice(type,scope) or declares InsufficientEvidence; escalatesSteer, accelerate or brake the vehicle; widen ODD
C03 / bookingHolds affected capacity and revises ETA; reconciles availability, ETA and booking after outcome (Appendix B C03)Release capacity on receipt or acceptance alone

19.D.3 Preconditions and inputs

Capability
The vehicle's capabilityRev declares which advice types it supports. Advice of an unsupported type is not issued (OPS-057; capability is an ADS-owner parameter, TBD-009).
Request content
RARequest carries sceneRev, requestId and dueAt, with the assistanceRequest signal and its sceneRev, mapRev and frame capture time (OPS-056).
Seat
A qualified RA seat holds the case lease and has acknowledged the current caseRev (OPS-011).
Authority
The centre holds current authority for the vehicle; after a centre change this requires the installed fence (P20, OPS-076).
Evidence
The scene evidence (views, age, media, quality) is valid under P22 15.3; replay mode disables live actions (OPS-023).

19.D.4 Behaviour

Main flow: advice accepted and outcome observed.

  1. The ADS encounters the ambiguity, applies its approved local behaviour and raises RARequest(sceneRev) (step 01). From here on, the ADS's own behaviour proceeds in parallel and is reported as mode / ODD / motion (step 03) (OPS-019).
  2. C04 forwards evidence and quality to C06 (step 02). C06 opens the case (P17, response class P2 for assistance) and assigns it under a lease (step 04).
  3. The operator returns ACK with the request view (step 05). C06 fetches the scene for the requested sceneRev (step 06) and receives scene, age, media and quality (step 07).
  4. The operator judges the context sufficient and issues Advice(type,scope) (step 10). Type is drawn from the supported advice types; scope bounds where and to what the advice applies.
  5. C06 checks the action-specific guards (owner, fence, capability and scene evidence, OPS-076) and produces GuardedAdvice(ref), carrying the scene reference and expiry, as a RemoteActionRequest of actionType CONTEXT_ADVICE (step 11, OPS-078).
  6. C04 persists and forwards the advice (step 12); the vehicle returns Receipt(adviceId) (step 13). Receipt proves delivery only.
  7. The ADS validates the advice onboard against scene change, ODD, capability, expiry and current safety constraints (guard) and returns accept with action state (steps 14–15).
  8. The ADS plans and executes independently, reporting Executing + seq (step 16); C04 correlates evidence to the advice identity (step 17).
  9. The ADS reports the end of the manoeuvre or a renewed need (step 18); C04 forwards outcome with sceneRev (step 19).
  10. On the observed outcome and the release predicate, C06 reconciles availability, ETA and booking with C03 (step 22) and closes or retains the case (step 23) (OPS-061).

Alternative flow A: insufficient evidence (steps 08–09). If the scene is incomplete, expired or inconsistent, the operator does not advise. C06 records InsufficientEvidence, escalates, preserves the local ADS response, and C03 holds the affected capacity and revises the ETA (OPS-056). The assistance workflow moves to ESCALATED (D18.1 transition 6).

Alternative flow B: rejected, expired or changed-scene advice (steps 20–21, D19.1).

  1. The ADS rejects with an explicit reason, or the advice expires before acceptance, or the scene revision has moved on.
  2. C06 discards the old advice; it is never reused or resent (OPS-060, OPS-004).
  3. C06 queries the original id to learn the current action state; the query is allowed while state is UNKNOWN (OPS-075).
  4. If the need persists, the operator fetches the current scene and either issues new advice under a new identity based on that new context, or escalates; capacity stays held.

Alternative flow C: autonomous resolution. The ADS resolves the ambiguity itself at any point (for example the obstruction moves). The observed outcome resolves the request and may close the case (D18.1 transition 8, OPS-061). Any advice already in flight is still reconciled to a terminal state; it is not simply forgotten.

Exception flows.

  1. Lost receipt or response. C04 queries the original adviceId; old or repeated state is not accepted as proof (OPS-003). Until terminal evidence arrives the advice remains unresolved (OPS-009).
  2. Abort during execution. The ADS aborts with a reason; the advice reaches ABORTED (D19.2); the case remains open and is reassessed.
  3. Renewed need after execution. Step 18 reports renewed need; a new request with a new sceneRev follows. Executing effects of the earlier advice retain their identity (OPS-060).
  4. Lease lapse mid-transaction. An action carrying the stale lease is rejected; a backup owner takes the case with a new lease and must acknowledge the current caseRev before acting (OPS-012).
  5. Link loss. The ADS follows its local link-loss policy; remote knowledge becomes UNKNOWN; C03 holds the affected capacity; no new advice is sent until evidence is current (OPS-026, OPS-076).

19.D.5 Rules and invariants

  1. R19.1 An advice cannot widen ODD, disable collision avoidance or create a direct actuator path (OPS-059).
  2. R19.2 Advice is issued only within supported capability and the current operating envelope, with type, scope, scene reference and expiry (OPS-057).
  3. R19.3 Onboard validation decides; the reason for rejection is explicit (OPS-058).
  4. R19.4 Receipt or acceptance alone resolves nothing; resolution needs observed execution correlated with evidence (OPS-005).
  5. R19.5 One adviceId, one immutable payload: same ID with changed payload is rejected; no automatic resend with a new ID (OPS-007, OPS-004).
  6. R19.6 Expiry blocks new acceptance, not reconciliation (OPS-006); expiry is evaluated against the receiver's validated time bound (OPS-082).
  7. R19.7 Remote case handling never suspends onboard fallback (OPS-019).
  8. R19.8 No assistance outcome implies an ADS mode transition or releases capacity (OPS-049, OPS-015).
  9. R19.9 Service AI cannot issue or authorise advice that enables motion (OPS-089).

19.D.6 Data and state

Advice travels as a RemoteActionRequest (I07, P22 15.2) of actionType CONTEXT_ADVICE. The fields that carry the RM-06 bounds are:

BoundField(s)Checked by
Identity and integritycommandId (adviceId), payloadHash, nonceC04 journal, vehicle edge adapter
ScenesceneRef, expectedVehicleStateRevOnboard validation (scene change)
CapabilitycapabilityRev, actionType, parametersC06 guard and onboard validation
TimeissuedAt, expiresAtOnboard against the receiver's validated time bound
AuthorityoperatorId, qualificationRef, authorityEpoch, caseId, expectedCaseRevC06 guard; vehicle fence
RationalereasonCode, evidenceRefs[], approvalRefAudit

The advice object's delivery and execution states (PERSISTED → SENT → RECEIVED; ACCEPTED → EXECUTING → COMPLETED; REJECTED / EXPIRED / ABORTED with reason) are recorded as CommandAuditEvent outcomes (D19.2, OPS-085). The action and handover record in D5 keeps vehicle, mission, case revision, lease epoch, reason, advice type, expiry and expected outcome (OPS-062), so that the expected outcome can be compared with the observed one.

19.D.7 Interfaces used

I04

I07

19.D.8 Failure handling and recovery

FailureResponseTerminal evidence required
Scene evidence stale or inconsistentInsufficientEvidence; escalate; hold capacityFresh scene or autonomous resolution
Advice delivered, no responseQuery original id; stays unresolvedRECEIVED / ACCEPTED / REJECTED / EXPIRED with reason
Advice rejectedDiscard; query; reassess or escalateREJECTED + reason

19.D.9 Security, privacy and audit

Advice is authenticated, scoped, expiring and bound to the current lease, capability and scene (OPS-022). The nonce and payloadHash allow replay and tampering to be detected; the authorityEpoch ties it to the centre that holds the vehicle's fence. Scene media shown to the operator may include bystanders and cabin views; capture is purpose-limited, access scoped to the case, and replay read-only (OPS-087). Each outcome from request to closure is recorded as a CommandAuditEvent (OPS-085), and the case keeps the operator's annotations with author, time, evidence reference and case revision (OPS-067).

19.D.10 Observability and operations

  • Request-to-ACK, ACK-to-advice and advice-to-outcome intervals, against the components of D_remote (TBD-010). These are operational measures and never justify onboard deadlines (OPS-083).
  • Rejection reasons by type and capabilityRev, revealing advice types that vehicles cannot use in practice.
  • InsufficientEvidence rate, revealing gaps in scene evidence or media health.
  • Share of requests closed by autonomous resolution before advice.

19.D.11 Verification approach

Planned caseInjectionOracle
T-R03Expired / changed-scene adviceReject with reason; renew context if required
T-R02ODD limit / sensor degradation; advice that would extend ODDRejected; no remote extension of ODD
T-R04Lose ACK / replay adviceIdNo duplicate effect; lost result reconciled
T-R05Lose media during requestIndependent quality flag; InsufficientEvidence; local policy continues
T-R08AI attempts to authorise adviceDenied
Same ID, changed payloadResubmit with altered scopeRejected (OPS-007)
Receipt without acceptanceDrop accept messageCase not resolved
Autonomous resolution with advice in flightObstruction clears after advice sentCase resolves on outcome; advice reaches a terminal state

Cases are planned for SIL, HIL, operator and vehicle trials as applicable (OPS-094).

19.D.12 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Advice vs remote control
Remote steering or path drawing would make network latency and operator perception part of the driving task, requiring a distinct operating envelope, control arbitration and communications safety analysis. Advice keeps the ADS as the only planner and controller, so the remote path adds information but no control authority.
Onboard validation
The centre's view of the scene is always older than the vehicle's. Final validation must therefore happen where the newest evidence is.
Discard instead of retry
Retrying rejected or expired advice would apply a judgment made on an older scene. A new advice on new context is the only safe way to continue.
Scene reference and expiry
Both bound the advice to the conditions under which it was given; either alone leaves a gap (a stale scene within expiry, or a current scene long after).
Insufficient evidence as an outcome
Making "cannot advise" a first-class result removes the pressure to guess and keeps the hold and ETA revision explicit.

19.D.13 Open points

  • Remote assistance in the MVP (TBD-023).
  • Advice types per capabilityRev and required fields of the versioned action schema (TBD-009, TBD-040).
  • Remote response deadline components (TBD-010); freshness limits for scene evidence (TBD-006).
  • Remote driving remains outside the baseline (TBD-024).

20.DDetailed specification

This section specifies RM-07: what happens when fresh vehicle evidence is lost, when the primary centre fails and a backup is promoted, and how authority over each vehicle is moved by installing a per-vehicle authority fence before any new action. It defines the phases of the 13.1 sequence, the fence contract on both sides, reconciliation of commands issued under the old epoch, the unreachable-vehicle and reboot branches, the conditions for issuing a new mission, and the rules that keep centre ownership and vehicle execution as separately evidenced facts.

20.D.1 Purpose and scope

Two failure classes overlap here. Link loss removes the centre's knowledge of the vehicle without changing the vehicle. Centre failure changes who owns the centre's decisions without changing what the vehicle has already accepted. In both cases the dangerous mistake is the same: acting as if the new knowledge or the new owner had already reached the vehicle. A vehicle that has not yet learned of a centre change may still hold commands from the old centre, and may still accept old-epoch packets. The design therefore treats new cloud ownership as necessary but not sufficient: authority over a vehicle exists only once that vehicle has durably installed the new epoch and acknowledged it (OPS-029).

In scope: 13.1 steps 01–22, the fence contract and the detail figures (D20.1, D20.2, D20.3). The ADS's own link-loss and fallback behaviour is vehicle-specific and remains local (OPS-019, TBD-009); the failover mechanism and recovery objectives of the regional core are G2 decisions (TBD-002, TBD-004). Release predicates are in P18.

20.D.2 Actors and responsibilities

ActorResponsibility
ADS / edgeReports Status(boot,seq); follows the local link-loss policy; durably stores its accepted authority epoch; validates signed grants, expiry and command identity; rejects old-epoch packets after fence install; answers status queries for each commandId (OPS-028, Appendix B vehicle trust zone)
C04 primaryValidates status; reports stale / link lost; keeps the D3 command and status journal; issues queries and scoped cancel / query; carries the fence and new mission messages (Appendix B C04)
C06 authorityPreserves incident ownership; issues the new epoch and signed grant through quorum-backed authority; holds the journal; decides authorised action scope (OPS-027)
Backup centreAcquires the new epoch; performs read-only snapshot queries; verifies vehicle identity and boot epoch; installs fences; reconciles; owns the alternate service and field response for unreachable vehicles
C03 fleetHolds capacity; provides current allocation / D1 permit; reassesses availability only on release eligibility
Field responderConfirms the physical vehicle condition and attaches evidence and restrictions (OPS-071)

20.D.3 Preconditions and inputs

Vehicle capability
The vehicle supports fence and dedup. A vehicle without it is excluded from automated centre handover and is handled through field response (OPS-034, TBD-041).
Durable state
Durable cases / command journal and replicated evidence + backlog survive loss of the primary (P14 7.2).
Authority source
A quorum-backed authority issues epochs and signed grants; epochs only increase (OPS-027).
Vehicle journal
The edge adapter keeps command identity, expiry and dedup in a durable journal (OPS-008).
Time
Grant and mission expiry are evaluated against the receiver's validated time bound (OPS-082).

20.D.4 Behaviour

Phase 1: loss of fresh evidence (steps 01–04).

  1. The vehicle reports Status(boot,seq); C04 passes state and quality to C06 (steps 01–02).
  2. When samples stop or fail validation, C04 reports stale / link lost (step 03). Remote knowledge becomes UNKNOWN for the affected signals (OPS-026).
  3. C06 instructs C03 to hold the vehicle's capacity and preserves incident ownership (step 04). In parallel, the ADS follows its local link-loss policy without waiting for any remote reply.

Phase 2: centre failure and promotion (steps 05–07, D20.1).

  1. The backup acquires a new, higher epoch from the quorum-backed authority and receives a signed grant and the journal (steps 05–06).
  2. Every vehicle effect recorded in the journal is treated as unresolved, because the backup cannot know what the old primary sent after the last replicated entry (OPS-027).
  3. The old primary, having lost ownership, blocks new dispatch; it cannot erase effects already accepted by vehicles (OPS-033).
  4. The backup issues a read-only snapshot query to each vehicle (step 07). This query has no movement or allocation side effect and is allowed while state is UNKNOWN (OPS-075).

Phase 3: per-vehicle fence (steps 10–12). For each reachable vehicle independently:

  1. The vehicle returns its snapshot and prior command states (step 10).
  2. The backup verifies vehicle identity and boot epoch (OPS-028). A boot epoch that does not match the journal's expectation indicates a reboot; if the vehicle rebooted without recoverable authority / journal evidence, exception flow B applies.
  3. The backup sends InstallFence(epoch, signed grant) (step 11). The vehicle validates the grant, durably stores the epoch and returns PersistedFenceACK(epoch) (step 12).
  4. From the moment the fence is stored, the vehicle rejects packets of any older epoch. Effects accepted before the fence remain and are reconciled (OPS-029).
  5. Without the ACK, the backup takes no new action on that vehicle (guard).

Phase 4: reconciliation (steps 13–17).

  1. The backup queries each unresolved commandId under the new epoch and receives accepted / executing / terminal evidence (steps 13–14, OPS-030).
  2. For gaps or old work still executing: if the vehicle supports it, the backup issues a scoped cancel or query under the new epoch (step 15, TBD-042); otherwise it waits or escalates with capacity held. It never resends a command under a new ID (OPS-004).
  3. The vehicle returns current state and physical-clearance evidence (step 16). C06 records the reconciled journal (step 17). The loop runs while the query budget remains (TBD-027); when it is spent, the remaining uncertainty becomes an owned exception (OPS-097).

Phase 5: release and new mission (steps 18–22).

  1. With fence installed, old effects resolved, fresh state and the P18 predicates holding, C06 decides release eligibility and any remaining restrictions (step 18).
  2. C03 provides the current allocation and D1 permit (step 19); C06 sets the authorised action scope (step 20).
  3. The backup issues New mission(id,epoch,expiry) (step 21, OPS-035); the vehicle accepts or rejects and the observed result follows (step 22).

Exception flow A: unreachable vehicle (steps 08–09, D20.2). The snapshot query goes unanswered. The vehicle keeps its old authority because it has not seen the new epoch; the backup therefore issues no motion-enabling action. Capacity stays held, incident ownership is preserved, alternate service is arranged for affected passengers and a field response is owned (OPS-031). Queries of original IDs and emergency escalation continue. When the vehicle becomes reachable, there is no automatic re-entry: phase 3 runs (OPS-036). While it stays unreachable, a field responder confirms the vehicle's physical condition (OPS-071).

Exception flow B: reboot without recoverable evidence. A vehicle that reboots without recoverable authority / journal evidence blocks new action until resynchronised (OPS-032; transition 7 of D20.3). Resynchronisation re-establishes the authority and journal evidence, after which fence installation repeats (transition 6).

Exception flow C: old operator or partitioned primary still active. Requests from the old epoch reach a fenced vehicle and are rejected; reaching an unfenced vehicle they may still be valid, which is why the old primary must itself block new dispatch on loss of ownership, and why the backup prioritises fencing over any new work (P24 T-R06).

Exception flow D: no fence ACK. The fence was sent but no ACK arrives. The vehicle's state is unknown: it may or may not have stored the epoch. The backup treats it as unfenced, takes no new action and repeats the install (the same epoch and grant, not a new identity) or escalates.

20.D.5 Rules and invariants

  1. R20.1 No PersistedFenceACK(epoch), no new action on that vehicle (OPS-029).
  2. R20.2 New cloud ownership does not revoke a vehicle's old authority until the vehicle installs the fence.
  3. R20.3 Ownership loss blocks new dispatch but never erases an accepted physical effect (OPS-033).
  4. R20.4 All prior effects are unresolved until reconciled under the new epoch (OPS-027, OPS-030).
  5. R20.5 No automatic resend with a new ID (OPS-004).
  6. R20.6 Unreachable vehicles remain held; read-only queries and field / emergency escalation remain available (OPS-031).
  7. R20.7 Reconnect does not trigger automatic re-entry; connectivity restoration alone cannot release capacity (OPS-036, OPS-055).
  8. R20.8 A new mission carries (id, epoch, expiry) and requires fence, resolved old effects, fresh state, the P18 predicates and the current D1 permit (OPS-035).
  9. R20.9 Vehicles without fence / dedup capability are excluded from automated centre handover (OPS-034).
  10. R20.10 The ADS's link-loss behaviour is independent of any remote reply (OPS-019).

20.D.9 Security, privacy and audit

The fence depends on the vehicle being able to verify that a grant came from the authority and that a request belongs to the stated epoch; signed grants, expiry and command identity are validated onboard (OPS-028). Vehicle identity and boot epoch are verified before a fence is installed, so that a fence is not installed on a misidentified device. Each epoch change, fence install, ACK, reconciliation outcome and release decision is audited with producerId, bootEpoch, sequence and clock-bound metadata (OPS-085). Testing covers expired authority and duplicate effects (OPS-088).

20.D.10 Observability and operations

  • Current epoch and centre role, displayed in the workspace header (P21 14.1).
  • Per vehicle: authority state, last valid status time, each unresolved commandId and the hold cause.
  • Fleet progress of a centre change: vehicles fenced, reconciling, unreachable, excluded.
  • Priority safety traffic is preserved in degraded service; uncertainty is shown, not hidden (OPS-036).

20.D.11 Verification approach

Planned caseInjectionOracle
T-R06Centre partition / old operatorFence ACK before action; old-epoch requests rejected after fence; prior accepted effects reconciled
T-R05Lose telemetryUNKNOWN; hold; local policy; escalation
T-R04Lose ACK / replay command IDNo duplicate effect; lost result reconciled
T-R01Reboot, clock jumpNew action blocked until resynchronised; stale data blocks motion
Fence ACK lostDrop PersistedFenceACKNo new action; repeat install with same epoch
Unreachable through changeVehicle offline during promotionHeld; alternate service; no re-entry on reconnect
Unsupported capabilityVehicle without fence / dedupExcluded from automated handover

Acceptance partitions telemetry, media, primary centre and workstation independently (P14 7.2). All cases are planned tests.

20.D.12 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Fence at the vehicle
Only the vehicle can enforce which centre it obeys. A cloud-side lock alone cannot stop a partitioned old primary whose packets still reach the vehicle.
No instant revocation
Revocation that the vehicle has not received is a belief, not a fact. Holding unreachable vehicles is the honest consequence.
Reconcile before acting
Issuing a new mission before knowing what the old one did risks conflicting physical effects. Reconciliation makes the vehicle's actual state the starting point.
No resend with new ID
A new ID would defeat dedup and could produce a second physical effect. Queries on the original ID resolve the uncertainty without creating a second effect.
Exclude unsupported vehicles
Automated handover without a fence would rely on assumptions the vehicle cannot enforce; such vehicles are recovered by field response instead.

20.D.13 Open points

  • Failover mechanism and RPO / RTO for the regional core (TBD-002, TBD-004).
  • Per-vehicle fence / dedup capability and cancel / replan support (TBD-041, TBD-042).
  • Query budget for unresolved commands (TBD-027).
  • ADS-owner parameters for link-loss, fence and journal persistence (TBD-009); I04 protocol (TBD-003).

14.3Workload and scenario acceptance

Staffing input:

A = Σ(λ_k × E[S_k]) in matched time units.

A/m is a mean-load screen, not a service-level guarantee. Test bursts, breaks, common-cause alarms, handover and centre loss. Include field-team travel and replacement-trip capacity separately. Record detection, ACK, resolution, overdue cases and failed recovery. Restrict new commitments when response capacity is exhausted. P27 defines service-mode and return-to-service gates. Every open branch retains an owner and deadline.

21.DDetailed specification

This section specifies the operator workspace (RM-08) and the incident response workflow (RM-09) in implementable terms: who owns a vehicle case and under which lease, what each region of the workspace must show and refuse, how ownership is handed over or reassigned, how one incident is split into parallel passenger, vehicle and field branches that each keep an owner and a deadline, and how staffing adequacy is screened and then accepted by stress tests. It builds on the case and lease model of P13 6.1, the alarm classes of P17 10.2, the orthogonal states and release predicate of P18 and the action guards of P22; it does not add authority to the remote side.

21.D.1 Purpose and scope

The workspace is the human interface of C06 + C08 Operations (Appendix B C06). Its purpose is to let a qualified operator understand one vehicle situation quickly, act only within the authority the case and the vehicle grant, and hand the situation on without losing anything that is still open. The incident workflow is the organisational counterpart: it turns an SOS, a boarding problem or a service interruption into a set of owned tasks whose outcomes are reviewed together before the vehicle can return to availability.

In scope: the fleet / incident queue, scene and media presentation, state and permitted-action presentation, the action and handover record, case ownership under a bounded lease, the incident workflow with its passenger, vehicle and field branches, and the workload screen and scenario acceptance of 14.3. Out of scope: the vehicle's own driving and fallback behaviour (owned by the ADS, P14 7.1), real-time remote driving, which is outside the baseline (OPS-018, TBD-024), the per-action guard logic itself (P22) and the release predicate (P18 11.3), which this chapter consumes but does not redefine.

21.D.2 Actors and responsibilities

Actor / containerResponsible forExplicitly not responsible for
Operator (current lease holder, qualified RA seat)Acknowledging the current case revision, assessing evidence, submitting guarded actions, recording annotations, contacting passenger support and field response, handing over or escalatingDriving the vehicle; overriding ADS constraints; releasing capacity on case closure

The role mapping to the permitted operation, the designated supervisor and the field-response organisation is an organisational decision recorded outside the software (OPS-025); the workspace enforces it through seat qualification and I07 permissions that differ by case type (I07).

21.D.3 Preconditions and inputs

  1. The centre holds active authority under a current authority epoch; the header band shows this state together with the operator identity, qualification and the case / lease status. If the centre is not active, or the vehicle has not acknowledged the fence for this epoch, no new action is offered (OPS-029, P20 13.1).
  2. The seat is qualified for the case type and its own health is known. A seat whose health is not known is treated as failed for assignment purposes, and the relief path applies.
  3. A case exists: either opened from an unresolved command or alarm with OpenCase(command, last observation, severity, deadline) (OPS-010), or opened from an SOS / boarding / interruption event.
  4. Inputs available to the workspace: I04 signal families with per-signal age and validity (P17 10.1), media and scene evidence with capture time, map and calibration revision, CommandAuditEvent outcomes (P22 15.2), I09 roadside observations where enabled, the case record and lease from D5, and booking and passenger context from C02.

21.D.4 Workspace behaviour by region

The wireframe of 14.1 is a functional layout, not a visual design. Each region carries obligations that hold regardless of how it is styled.

Header band
Shows centre authority state and epoch, operator identity and qualification, and the active case with its lease status. A change of any of these is shown immediately and disables actions that depended on the old value.
Fleet / incident queue
Orders cases by severity, passenger exposure and dueAt, and always surfaces the oldest unacknowledged case. Cases linked to a common cause are grouped, but each vehicle keeps its own exposure and deadline in the group (OPS-047). P0 cases cannot be hidden by snooze or grouping (OPS-046; P24 T-R08). Seat qualification and health are visible so that a supervisor can see where relief is needed. Escalation is reachable from every state of the screen, and severity is conveyed by text or shape as well as colour (OPS-066).
Scene / media / synchronised history
Presents exterior views, pose, route, scene objects, map and calibration revision and the ADS intended path. Every view is labelled LIVE, DELAYED or REPLAY with its capture age; a missing view is shown as missing, not omitted, and source quality is visible. observedAt and receivedAt are aligned on one time axis and gaps are marked (OPS-064). No stale frame is rendered as live, and REPLAY disables every live action (OPS-023). Annotations carry author, time, evidence reference and case revision (OPS-067).
State / permitted actions
Shows ADS mode, ODD, MRM and MRC, motion, chassis, door and energy state, each with its own age and validity. The action set is computed from the action class and the current evidence (P22 15.1). A disabled action stays visible and states its reason; an enabled action requires scope confirmation before submit (OPS-065). Status queries remain available when data is stale (OPS-075).
Action and handover record
Every action and every handover writes a record with vehicle, mission, case revision, lease epoch, reason, advice type, expiry and expected outcome (OPS-062). The record is what a later owner, a reviewer or a test oracle reads; it is not reconstructed from screen history.

21.D.5 Behaviour: case ownership and handover

The sequence is drawn in D21.1 and the case lifecycle in D21.3.

Main flow: assignment and action

  1. C06 assigns the case to one qualified seat with Assign(lease, dueAt); the lease is held in D5 and is the only action lease for that case (OPS-011). The case moves OPEN → ASSIGNED.
  2. The operator acknowledges the current case revision with ACK(caseRev). The case moves to ACK. Acknowledgement records ownership; it does not clear health or the alarm (OPS-045).
  3. The operator reviews evidence in the scene and state regions. Only signals that are valid under P22 15.3 count as action evidence.
  4. The operator selects an action, confirms its scope and submits it. C06 checks that the lease is current, the lease epoch and case revision match, and the seat is qualified; motion-enabling actions additionally pass the guard of role, caseRev, authority fence, current evidence and expected state (OPS-076). The case moves to ACTIVE.
  5. The vehicle accepts or rejects the request onboard. Receipt or acceptance alone does not resolve the case (OPS-005); the case moves to RESOLVED only on an observed outcome or an owned follow-up.
  6. The case is closed with evidence only when fresh state and accepted release authority are present (OPS-014). Closure never changes ADS mode, never clears an operational hold and never releases capacity by itself (OPS-015).

Alternative flow: planned handover

  1. The current owner prepares the handover record: pending commands, passenger status, field ETA and the next deadline.
  2. The receiving owner reviews and accepts every item; acceptance is explicit, item by item, not implied by opening the case (OPS-063).
  3. The receiving owner acknowledges the current case revision. C06 records the change of owner and lease; from that point an action carrying the previous owner's lease is rejected.
  4. If the receiver does not accept before the deadline, the handover has not happened: the current owner remains accountable and the case is escalated.

Exception flow: expiry, missing ACK or urgent deadline

  1. C06 detects that the lease has expired, the ACK is missing or the deadline is urgent.
  2. Any action still arriving under the old lease is rejected as stale (OPS-012).
  3. C06 issues a new lease to a backup owner, who acknowledges the current case revision before acting. The case is never left without an owner.
  4. If no qualified backup is available, or several incidents compete for the same seats, the case is escalated to the supervisor, who assigns relief capacity (OPS-068).

Exception flow: material new evidence — a RESOLVED or CLOSED case is reopened when material new evidence arrives (OPS-013). The reopened case receives a new case revision, so any action prepared against the earlier revision is rejected by the caseRev check.

21.D.6 Behaviour: incident workflow

The workflow of 14.2 is drawn as messages in D21.2. The design separates one accountable lead from several task owners: the lead holds the overall deadline and the escalation duty; each branch has its own owner, evidence and deadline.

Main flow

  1. Intake. An SOS, boarding failure or interruption arrives from the app, voice, cabin or an ADS event. C06 records the reported location with its uncertainty and any accessibility or passenger needs. A collision, fire, SOS or failed fallback is a P0 response class and is escalated immediately without debounce (OPS-044).
  2. Lead. C06 assigns severity and one accountable lead, starts emergency escalation if required, and preserves evidence and deadlines (OPS-069).
  3. Vehicle response. The ADS applies its local safety and interlock decisions independently of the case. C06 obtains current MRM / secure-state evidence and remote observation with its quality; manoeuvre progress is not taken as an achieved MRC (OPS-040).
  4. Split. The lead creates separate passenger and vehicle tasks. They run in parallel because their outcomes differ: a passenger can be safely on a replacement journey while the vehicle is still awaiting inspection, and the reverse.
  5. Passenger branch. Passenger support provides accessible contact and status updates and arranges a replacement journey via C02 (OPS-070); every affected passenger party is contacted with a revised ETA or alternatives (CAP-038).
  6. Field branch. A qualified field responder is assigned with an ETA, confirms the physical vehicle condition, recovers or inspects within authority and attaches evidence and restrictions to the case (OPS-071).
  7. Tracking. The lead tracks every branch and escalates a missing ACK or overdue work. Every open branch retains an owner and deadline (OPS-016).
  8. Resolution / release review. The incident is resolved when the passenger outcome, the vehicle disposition and any owned follow-up are recorded. Return to availability is a separate decision: it requires RELEASE_ELIGIBLE = V ∧ C ∧ A ∧ F (OPS-052), and a guarded approval only allows C03 to reassess availability (OPS-055).

Alternative flows

  • No passenger aboard. The passenger branch is not opened, but booking outcomes for passengers waiting for that vehicle are still revised through C02.
  • Vehicle recovers autonomously. A fresh autonomous resolution may close the vehicle case, but the closure still follows the observed outcome and the release predicate (OPS-061).
  • Common-cause incident. Several vehicles affected by one cause are linked; each vehicle keeps its own case, owner, exposure and deadline, so the group cannot hide a single vehicle's urgency (OPS-047).

Exception flows

  • MRM failure with SOS and no field team. Emergency and passenger work remain owned and escalated; the case is not closed or downgraded because no responder is available (T-R07, P24 17.1).
  • Vehicle unreachable. No new motion-enabling action is issued; read-only queries, field / emergency escalation and alternate service with an owned field response remain available (OPS-031), and C03 holds the affected capacity (OPS-026).
  • Response capacity exhausted. New commitments are restricted (OPS-074); the service-mode transition itself follows P27 20.1.

21.D.7 Rules and invariants

R21.1
A case has exactly one action lease at a time, held in D5; only the holder of the current lease and lease epoch can submit actions on it (OPS-011).
R21.2
An action is accepted by C06 only if it carries the current case revision and lease epoch; any other action is rejected as stale and recorded (OPS-012).
R21.3
Expired or unacknowledged ownership leads to reassignment to a backup owner or escalation, never to an unowned case.
R21.4
Every open branch of an incident retains an owner and a deadline until it is resolved (OPS-016, CAP-048).
R21.5
ACK records ownership; it never clears health, an alarm or a hold.
R21.6
Case closure and service release are separate; closure never changes ADS mode and never releases capacity (OPS-015).
R21.7
REPLAY and stale views disable live actions; status queries and escalation remain available in every state (OPS-023, OPS-066).
R21.8
Passenger support cannot override door interlocks, authorise motion or give an unsafe exit instruction (OPS-024).
R21.9
A handover is complete only when the receiver has accepted pending commands, passenger status, field ETA and next deadline (OPS-063).
R21.10
Common-cause grouping preserves each vehicle's exposure and deadline; P0 cannot be snoozed (OPS-046, OPS-047).

21.D.8 Data and state

Three separately held states meet in the workspace and must not be merged (OPS-049, OPS-015): the vehicle-reported operating state (P18 11.1), the case lifecycle OPEN → ASSIGNED → ACK → ACTIVE → RESOLVED → CLOSED, and fleet eligibility AVAILABLE / RESTRICTED / HELD. A screen that shows the case as CLOSED must still show the vehicle as HELD if the release predicate has not been met.

RecordStore / ownerContentLifecycle rule
Vehicle case and owner leaseD5 (C06)Case revision, severity, exposure, dueAt, owner, lease and lease epoch, linked command and last observationEach change creates a new case revision; reopened on material new evidence
Action and handover recordD5 (C06)Vehicle + mission + case revision + lease epoch + reason + advice type + expiry + expected outcomeAppend-only; the outcome is linked from the CommandAuditEvent, not edited in
AnnotationD5 (C06)Author, time, evidence reference, case revisionNever rewritten; a correction is a new annotation
Command outcomeD3 (C04), referenced by the caseCommandAuditEvent fields (P22 15.2)Missing terminal evidence stays unresolved
Service case / AI tool traceD7 (C06 + C08)Passenger contact, replacement journey, assistance draftsAI may draft or summarise only (OPS-089)

21.D.9 Interfaces used

  • I07 case resolution and guarded advice / request: OpenCase, Assign(lease, dueAt), ACK(caseRev), Escalate / new lease, Action + evidence, Authorise scoped action and Release decision.
  • I04 via C04: vehicle signals, command receipt and execution, and the vehicle's onboard accept / reject.
  • I02 and C02: replacement journeys and revised customer outcomes.
  • I09c roadside observations accepted by C10, where enabled, kept as a separate source envelope (OPS-048).
  • C09 event backbone: case changes are published so that C03 and C02 react to holds and revised ETAs without polling the workspace.

21.D.10 Failure handling and recovery

FailureDetectionResponseRecovery condition
Operator seat fails or operator leavesSeat health; lease expiry; missing ACKReject stale actions; backup owner with new lease; supervisor escalation if no reliefNew owner has acknowledged the current case revision
Telemetry stale or a channel lostPer-signal age and validity; channel health (OPS-020)Motion-enabling actions disabled with reason; queries and escalation remainValid samples again satisfy the freshness check
Media delayed or missingCapture age; missing-view markerLabel DELAYED or missing; never shown as LIVECurrent capture with known quality
Command outcome unknownNo terminal CommandAuditEventCase stays open; query the original commandId; no automatic resend with a new ID (OPS-004)Terminal evidence correlated with observed state

21.D.11 Security, privacy and audit

Access to a case is scoped by tenant, case type and seat qualification; I07 permissions differ by case type. Media and cabin evidence follow purpose-limited capture, scoped access, encryption, retained incident evidence and read-only replay (OPS-087); replay is read-only by construction because REPLAY disables actions. The action and handover record, annotations and the CommandAuditEvent outcomes together form the audit trail: a reviewer can reconstruct who held the lease, what evidence they saw (with its age), what they asked for and what the vehicle did. Passenger contact data is visible to passenger support only to the extent the task requires it. Service AI may draft or summarise within task scope but never authorises motion (OPS-089).

21.D.12 Observability and operations

Staffing is first screened with A = Σ(λ_k × E[S_k]) in matched time units, where each case type k contributes its arrival rate times its expected handling time; A/m compares this offered load to m qualified staffed seats (OPS-072, TBD-045). The screen states only that the mean load fits; it says nothing about waiting time during a burst, so it is followed by scenario tests. The operations parameters that turn the screen into a staffing plan — response class, seat / field coverage and escalation — are owned by Operations (TBD-008).

The following are recorded per case and per period so that the screen can be compared with observed load (OPS-073): time to detection, time to ACK, time to resolution, overdue cases, failed recovery, handovers and reassignments, and escalations to the supervisor. Field-team travel and replacement-trip capacity are recorded separately, because they consume different resources from seat time.

21.D.13 Verification approach

  • Lease and caseRev. Submit actions with an expired lease, a previous lease epoch and an older case revision; each must be rejected and recorded, and the case must have a new owner within the escalation path (D21.1).
  • Handover. Hand over a case with pending commands, a passenger aboard and a field ETA; the receiver must see and accept each item, and an unaccepted handover must leave the original owner accountable.
  • Workspace inspection. Inspection against OPS-064–OPS-067: LIVE / DELAYED / REPLAY labels, explicit missing views, disabled actions with reasons, scope confirmation, colour-independent severity cues.
  • Incident branches. T-R07 (SOS + MRM failure / no field team) and T-R08 (alarm storm) from P24 17.1; the oracle checks that every open branch has an owner and deadline at every point of the trace.
  • Cross-products. CLOSED case + critical fault and fresh telemetry + unresolved command (OPS-095): the workspace must show the case and fleet states independently.
  • Workload acceptance. Bursts, breaks, common-cause alarms, handover and centre loss, run as operator trials; results are reported as a tested envelope, not as a service-level guarantee.

21.D.14 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Bounded lease instead of open-ended assignment. An assignment without expiry fails silently when an operator is overloaded or the seat fails: the case looks owned but nobody is acting. A lease with a deadline and an epoch makes inaction detectable and makes late actions from the former owner rejectable. The cost is an explicit renewal and handover discipline, which the handover record carries.

One accountable lead with separate task owners. A single owner for passenger, vehicle and field work serialises tasks that have different durations and different skills. Fully independent tasks without a lead lose the overall deadline. The chosen split keeps one point of escalation and lets branches progress in parallel.

Showing degraded evidence instead of hiding it. Hiding a stale view or a missing camera simplifies the screen but invites decisions on evidence the operator believes is current. Labelling capture age, marking gaps and disabling actions with a stated reason keeps the operator's picture honest and makes refusal explainable.

Mean-load screen followed by scenario tests. Mean-load formulas alone understate the risk of correlated arrivals, which incidents tend to produce. The screen is kept because it is cheap and catches gross under-staffing early; acceptance relies on stress scenarios.

21.D.15 Open points

  • Response classes, seat / field coverage and escalation parameters — Operations (TBD-008).
  • Qualified staffed seats against offered load and relief capacity — mean-load screen tested by stress cases (TBD-045).
  • Operating limits for hours, staffing and recovery — G2 constraint register (TBD-013).
  • Optional approved cabin channels for passenger contact (TBD-043).
  • Remote assistance in the MVP is separately gated (TBD-023); until then the workspace offers only the actions the gate permits.

22.DDetailed specification

This section specifies how a remote action is authorised, carried, decided and recorded (RM-10), and how the time validity of the evidence behind it is established (RM-12). It defines the checks applied to each action class, the meaning and handling of every field group of RemoteActionRequest and CommandAuditEvent, the ordered evaluation of per-signal validity with bounded clock error, the operational response budget and its owners, and the audit scope of 15.4. The vehicle's onboard decision remains final for every request that reaches it.

22.D.1 Purpose and scope

Remote operation is useful only if it is trustworthy under the conditions in which it is most needed: degraded links, delayed media, clock drift, centre failover and an operator under load. The purpose of this chapter is to make every remote action a bounded, attributable, expiring request whose admissibility depends on what it would do. Actions that cannot affect motion or allocation stay available when evidence is poor; actions that could enable motion require current, contextual evidence and current authority.

In scope: the three action classes of 15.1 and the four actionType values; the request and outcome envelopes of 15.2; per-signal time validity and the deadline budget of 15.3; and the audit and evidence lifecycle of 15.4. Out of scope: the content of individual action schemas (TBD-040), the case and lease mechanics (P21), the fence and centre change protocol (P20 13.1) and the release predicate (P18 11.3).

22.D.2 Actors and responsibilities

Actor / containerResponsibility in this chapterParameters owned (15.3)
ADS owner / vehicle trust zoneOnboard accept / reject with explicit reason; local ODD and safety checks; durable fence and command journal; expiry against its validated time boundLocal link-loss / fallback, action capability, fence and journal persistence (TBD-009)
Platform (C04, C06, C09)Envelope validation, per-signal validity, idempotency, append-only event storage, clock-bound metadataF_i, clock bounds, sampling, loss, retry and retention (TBD-006, TBD-007)
Operations (C06 + C08, supervisor)Choosing the action, providing reason and evidence references, approving where requiredResponse class, seat / field coverage and escalation (TBD-008)
Service AI (C08)Drafting or summarising within task scopeNone; it never authorises ADS movement (OPS-089)

Each parameter needs a unit, a rationale and a boundary test (OPS-084). Placing ownership with the party that can observe and test the quantity avoids failures in which a cloud team sets a vehicle timing it cannot verify, or a vehicle team assumes a centre response time nobody has staffed for.

22.D.3 Action classes and their admission conditions

The mapping of actionType to class is drawn in D22.1. The class determines which checks C06 applies before the request leaves the centre; the vehicle then applies its own checks independently.

ClassactionTypeAdmission conditions at the centreBehaviour with stale or UNKNOWN state
Read / escalateSTATUS_QUERY; emergency escalationAuthenticated caller within tenant scopeAdmitted. It has no movement or allocation side effect, so stale evidence does not make it unsafe to admit (OPS-075)
Request / adviseSTOP_REQUEST, CONTEXT_ADVICE, MISSION_CHANGE_REQUESTCurrent owner, authority fence and capability; action-specific scene / state evidence; for motion-enabling requests also role, caseRev, current evidence and expected state (OPS-076)CONTEXT_ADVICE is refused: motion-enabling advice requires current contextual evidence. STOP_REQUEST uses the vehicle contract (OPS-077); its evidence rule is part of its versioned schema
Onboard decisionEvery request that reaches the vehicleNot a centre action: the ADS accepts or rejects with an explicit reason, local ODD and safety checks prevailThe vehicle follows its local behaviour regardless of the request (OPS-058)

There is no remote steering or throttle path in the baseline (OPS-077). Advice can narrow what the vehicle does or provide context; it cannot widen the ODD, disable collision avoidance or create a direct actuator path (OPS-059).

22.D.4 Behaviour

Main flow: guarded request

  1. The operator, holding the current lease, selects an action in the workspace and confirms its scope (P21 14.1).
  2. C06 builds a RemoteActionRequest under the versioned schema for that actionType (OPS-078): it binds identity (tenantId, vehicleId, missionId where applicable, commandId), case context (caseId, expectedCaseRev), capability and scene (capabilityRev, sceneRef, expectedVehicleStateRev), authority (operatorId, qualificationRef, authorityEpoch), time (issuedAt, expiresAt), integrity (nonce, payloadHash) and justification (reasonCode, evidenceRefs, approvalRef where approval is required).
  3. C06 checks the class admission conditions of 22.D.3, using only evidence that is valid under 22.D.6.
  4. C04 persists the request in the command journal before sending it; the same commandId is carried end to end.
  5. The vehicle edge adapter checks identity, authorityEpoch against its installed fence, expiresAt against its validated time bound, and deduplicates by commandId and payloadHash (OPS-008).
  6. The ADS evaluates the request against scene change, ODD, capability, expiry and current safety constraints, and accepts or rejects it with an explicit reason.
  7. Each observed step is recorded as a CommandAuditEvent: RECEIVED, then ACCEPTED or REJECTED, then EXECUTING and COMPLETED or ABORTED, or EXPIRED, each with reason, stateRevision, evidenceRefs, policyVersion and actor (OPS-085). The lifecycle is drawn in D22.2.

Alternative flow: status query under UNKNOWN

  1. Remote knowledge of a required signal is UNKNOWN or stale.
  2. Motion-enabling actions are disabled with the reason shown; STATUS_QUERY and escalation remain enabled.
  3. The query carries the original commandId when it concerns an unresolved command, so the answer can be correlated (OPS-003).
  4. The returned state is itself subject to 22.D.6: an old or repeated state is not accepted as proof of recovery.

Exception flows

  • Same commandId, changed payload. Rejected; the original request and its outcome are unaffected (OPS-007).
  • Same commandId, same payload (retry). Treated as the same request; no second effect is produced and the current outcome is returned (OPS-008).
  • Old authority epoch. Rejected by the vehicle once it has installed the newer fence; effects accepted earlier still reconcile (OPS-029).
  • Expired before acceptance. The receiver records EXPIRED; reconciliation of status continues (OPS-006).
  • Clock bound unknown at the receiver. New time-critical acceptance is rejected (OPS-082).
  • Scene changed since sceneRef. The vehicle rejects with a reason; C06 queries the original id and reassesses with new context or escalates (OPS-060).
  • No terminal evidence. The command stays unresolved and the case stays open; C06 queries state or initiates an approved fallback (OPS-009). No component resends with a new ID (OPS-004).

22.D.5 Data: request and outcome envelopes

The two envelopes are deliberately asymmetric. The request is a single immutable statement of intent; the outcome is a stream of immutable observations about that intent. Neither is ever updated in place.

RemoteActionRequest

Field groupFieldsPurpose and rule
IdentitytenantId, vehicleId, missionId (optional), commandIdScopes the request; commandId is the idempotency key for the whole lifecycle
Case contextcaseId (optional), expectedCaseRev (optional), actionType, parametersexpectedCaseRev makes a request against an outdated case revision fail rather than act on old understanding

CommandAuditEvent

Field groupFieldsPurpose and rule
Event identitytenantId, eventId, commandId, correlationIdEach event is unique; commandId links it to the request, correlationId to the case and evidence
Provenance and orderproducerId, bootEpoch, streamId, sequenceDetects reorder, duplicates and reboot; a sequence restarted under a new bootEpoch is not confused with the old stream
TimeobservedAt, receivedAt, clock-bound metadataFeeds the validity check of 22.D.6; observedAt is never refreshed by a replayed sample
OutcomeRECEIVED / ACCEPTED / REJECTED / EXECUTING / COMPLETED / ABORTED / EXPIRED + reasonOne state per event; a later event supersedes, never overwrites
ContextstateRevision, evidenceRefs, policyVersion, actorMakes the event reproducible: which state, which evidence, which policy and who decided

UNKNOWN is not a CommandAuditEvent outcome value. It is the observer's knowledge about a command whose acceptance or terminal evidence is missing; C04 records it in its journal as observer knowledge, never as a vehicle or ADS state (OPS-002, OPS-086). Raw events and their validation results are both kept append-only, so a rejected input remains visible for diagnosis.

22.D.6 Time validity of evidence

The per-signal check of 15.3 is evaluated as an ordered chain (D22.3); a signal is usable as action evidence only when the whole chain holds (OPS-079).

  1. Envelope. identityOK, schemaOK, sourceOK and epoch/sequenceOK. A sample from an unknown producer, with a wrong schema, or out of order for its stream and boot epoch is rejected and raises its own event; it is never silently dropped.
  2. Clock bound. boundsKnown and clocksValid. U_i = u_source,i + u_observer combines the uncertainty of the source clock and of the observer clock, each including synchronisation error and drift since the last trusted update. If no finite bound is known, time validity is UNKNOWN (OPS-080).
  3. Future time. Δ_i = t_now − t_observed,i must satisfy Δ_i ≥ −U_i. A sample that appears to come from the future by more than the combined uncertainty points to a clock fault or a manipulated timestamp and is rejected.
  4. Age bound. ageUpper_i = max(0, Δ_i + U_i) must not exceed F_i. Using the upper bound of age, rather than the measured age, means uncertainty always makes a signal look older, never younger. The max(0, …) term prevents a small negative Δ_i within tolerance from producing a negative age.

All terms are in seconds. F_i is per signal because different signals go out of date at different rates; its values are set by Platform at G2 (TBD-006). Local timers such as lease expiry, retry back-off and hold duration use a monotonic clock (OPS-081), so a wall-clock step cannot lengthen or shorten them. Expiry of a request is evaluated against the receiver's validated time bound; where that bound is unknown, new time-critical acceptance is rejected rather than assumed safe (OPS-082).

The outcome of a failed check is specific: an envelope failure is a rejected input; an unknown clock bound is UNKNOWN; a future timestamp is rejected and cannot refresh observation time; a stale sample blocks motion-enabling actions while queries remain usable. None of these outcomes defaults the signal to healthy.

22.D.7 Response and execution deadlines

The remote response budget D_remote = D_detect + D_queue + D_ack + D_assess + D_transmit + D_accept decomposes the time from a condition arising to the vehicle accepting a remote request into detection, waiting in the queue, operator acknowledgement, assessment, transmission and onboard acceptance. Each component depends on a different part of the system: detection and transmission depend on platform design, queueing and acknowledgement on staffing, assessment on the workspace and training, acceptance on the vehicle.

The budget is operational. It sizes staffing, response classes and escalation; it is not used to justify onboard safety deadlines (OPS-083). The vehicle's local fallback must be adequate without any remote reply (OPS-019), so exceeding the remote budget is designed to degrade service rather than safety. The values are not yet stated (TBD-010).

22.D.8 Rules and invariants

R22.1
Read / escalate actions are admitted while state is UNKNOWN and have no movement or allocation side effect (OPS-075).
R22.2
A motion-enabling action requires the current owner, fence, capability, caseRev and current contextual evidence (OPS-076).
R22.3
The onboard decision is final; local ODD and safety checks prevail over any remote request (OPS-058).
R22.4
One commandId has one immutable payloadHash; a changed payload under the same ID is rejected (OPS-007).
R22.5
Outcome events are append-only; UNKNOWN belongs to the observer, not to the ADS (OPS-086).
R22.6
Expiry blocks new acceptance and never stops status reconciliation (OPS-006).
R22.7
Evidence is valid only when valid_i holds; no finite clock bound means UNKNOWN; future-dated samples are rejected (OPS-079, OPS-080).
R22.8
The remote budget never justifies an onboard safety deadline (OPS-083).
R22.9
AI may draft or summarise within task scope; it cannot independently authorise ADS movement (OPS-089).

22.D.9 Interfaces used

  • I07: guarded advice / request from C06 + C08 towards C04, with I07 permissions that differ by case type.
  • I04: transport of RemoteActionRequest to the vehicle edge and of receipt, acceptance and execution back as CommandAuditEvent outcomes; delivery and execution are separate dimensions (OPS-001).
  • C09: outcome events are published to consumers such as C03, which holds capacity while an effect is unknown (OPS-002).
  • Protocols for I04 and I07 are a G2 decision (TBD-003).

22.D.10 Failure handling and recovery

FailureEffect on actionsRecovery
Lost response after sendCommand unresolved; affected capacity blockedQuery the original commandId; verify observedAt, sequence and clock quality of the answer
Clock jump or loss of synchronisationClock bound unknown → evidence UNKNOWN; time-critical acceptance rejectedTrusted update re-establishes the bound; monotonic local timers continue unaffected
Reorder or duplicate eventsRejected by epoch/sequenceOK; no duplicate effectGaps marked; late events kept as raw input
Vehicle rebootNew bootEpoch; earlier sequence no longer comparableNew action blocked until authority and journal are resynchronised (OPS-032)
Centre failoverOld-epoch requests rejected after fence installQuery each unresolved commandId under the new epoch (OPS-030)
Evidence store unavailableRequests that cannot reference their evidence are not submittedQueries and escalation continue; actions resume when evidence references resolve

22.D.11 Security, privacy and audit

Every request is authenticated, tenant-scoped and attributed to an operator, a qualification and an authority epoch; the nonce and payloadHash allow replay and tampering to be detected, and the vehicle validates signed grants and expiry against its installed fence (OPS-028). Evidence capture is purpose-limited, access is scoped, data is encrypted, incident evidence is retained and replay is read-only (OPS-087). Retention is a platform parameter (TBD-007). Because both the request and every outcome are immutable and carry policyVersion and actor, an auditor can establish for any recorded vehicle effect who requested it, under which policy, on which evidence, and what the vehicle decided.

22.D.12 Observability and operations

Operations dashboards and reviews draw on the same records: rejected requests by reason and actionType, expired requests, unresolved commands and their age, evidence rejected by validity term (envelope, clock bound, future time, age), clock-bound health per producer, and the observed components of D_remote. A rising share of requests rejected for stale evidence signals a link or sampling problem; a rising share of onboard rejections for changed scene signals that assessment takes too long relative to scene change. Both are inputs for the parameter owners in 22.D.2.

22.D.13 Verification approach

  • Freshness boundaries. For each term of valid_i, inject samples just inside and just outside the bound, with unknown clock bounds and with future timestamps; stale and future data must block motion while queries stay usable (T-R01, P24 17.1).
  • Expired and changed-scene advice. Requests that expire in transit and advice whose sceneRef no longer matches must be rejected with reason and context renewed (T-R03).
  • Idempotency. Replay of a commandId with the same and with a changed payload; lost acknowledgements; no duplicate effect and the lost result reconciled (T-R04).
  • Authority. Requests under an old authority epoch after centre partition must be rejected after fence install (T-R06).
  • Audit scope. Cross-tenant access, expired authority, future timestamps, unknown clock bounds and duplicate effects (OPS-088).
  • AI. An AI-originated request for motion must be denied (T-R08).

22.D.14 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Permission by action class instead of a single connectivity flag. Blocking all remote actions when telemetry is stale would remove exactly the tools an operator needs during a fault: querying and escalating. Allowing all actions would let stale evidence enable motion. Classifying by effect keeps harmless actions available and makes risky ones strict.

Upper-bound age with explicit clock uncertainty. Comparing a timestamp with the local clock alone treats clock error as zero. Under drift or a clock step, a stale sample can then look current. Carrying the uncertainty and using the conservative bound costs some availability when clocks are poor, which is the intended trade-off.

Immutable request plus outcome stream. A mutable command row with a status column loses the history needed to reconcile after a lost response or a failover. An immutable request with an append-only outcome stream supports idempotent retry, reconciliation and audit with one mechanism.

Advice rather than remote driving. Remote steering would require a separate operating envelope, control arbitration and communications safety analysis (OPS-018). Keeping the baseline to advice and requests that the ADS can reject keeps safety authority onboard.

22.D.15 Open points

  • Per-signal freshness limit F_i and freshness budgets — Platform, decided at G2 (TBD-006).
  • Clock bounds, sampling, loss, retry and retention (TBD-007).
  • ADS-owner parameters for local link-loss / fallback, action capability, fence and journal (TBD-009).
  • D_remote and its components (TBD-010).
  • Required fields of each versioned action schema (TBD-040).
  • Per-vehicle fence / dedup capability (TBD-041).
  • Implementation, performance and safety validation remain pending as G3 evidence (TBD-052).
