27.DDetailed specification

This section specifies how the service degrades and recovers when demand pressure or supply loss makes the current service promise infeasible. It defines the service-mode model (NORMAL, CONSTRAINED, SUSPENDED) as an admission control over new commitments, the impact assessment that precedes any mode decision, the three parallel recovery outcomes for passengers, assets and resources, the return-to-service gate, and the response-capacity condition for staffing. The model sits above the orthogonal vehicle, assistance and case states of P18 and never changes them.

27.D.1 Purpose and scope

Continuity is not the absence of failure but a bounded, observable reduction of service while affected passengers are supported and capacity is restored on evidence. The purpose of this specification is to make every reduction explicit (what is restricted, where, for how long and on whose authority), to protect commitments already accepted, and to return capacity only through a gate that cannot be passed by a single favourable signal.

In scope: the propagation of demand pressure and supply loss into an impact assessment; service-mode transitions and their effect on admission; parallel passenger, vehicle / site and resource recovery; the return-to-service gate; the response-capacity screen and its stress tests; and the degraded-period record. Out of scope: local ADS safety decisions, which remain independent of the service-mode model (CAP-033, ASM-014); remote assistance content (P19); and compensation policy itself, of which only the ownership is specified here.

27.D.2 Actors and responsibilities

Actor / containerResponsibility
C06 Operations (Appendix B C06)Opens and owns the case for each supply-loss signal; requests the impact assessment; assigns a qualified field responder; reserves relief / field capacity; escalates a recovery shortfall; holds the release review.
C03 Joint reservation authority (Appendix B C03)Identifies affected bookings and intervals; holds affected capacity; recomputes reachable vehicles, usable hubs and supply; reserves replacement journeys; reassesses availability after a guarded release.
C02 Booking / activities (Appendix B C02)Applies the admission restriction to new offers; contacts affected passenger parties; revises ETA and offers alternatives; tracks each handover and resolution; issues or withholds the dispatch permit.
C05 Energy / EMS adapters (Appendix B C05)Reports site outage and energy shortfall; revises feasible energy and site slots.
C04 Fleet / vehicle adapter (Appendix B C04)Reports vehicle fault and communication loss; retains fault and command history.
Vehicle / ADS (Appendix B vehicle trust zone)Owns driving and fallback; its local safety decisions do not wait for, and are not changed by, the service mode.
Accountable ownerApproves each service-mode transition; owns the degraded-period record and its next review.
Qualified field responderObserves secure state and clearance, inspects and records restrictions (CAP-042).
Compensation / refund ownerOwns the compensation / refund decision for affected passengers (CAP-040).

27.D.3 Preconditions and inputs

  • Triggers, persistence conditions and recovery thresholds with hysteresis are configured for the affected scope before operation (TBD-028).
  • An accountable owner and a backup are named for transition approval and for each case type (CAP-048).
  • Inputs to the impact assessment: D1 bookings with their current revision and permit state; D2 bundles and intervals; fleet counts by category (P25 18.2); hub capability from C05; open cases in D5 / D7; qualified staffed seats and field-team positions.
  • Supply-loss signals arrive as MissionObserved (vehicle fault, communication loss), EnergyUpdated (site outage, energy shortfall) and staffing information (staff absence). Demand pressure is derived from request arrivals by zone and time, directional imbalance, trip length and turnaround duration.

27.D.4 Service-mode model

The service mode governs admission of new commitments only (D27.1). It is held per affected scope recorded for the degraded period (zone / time as used for the admission restriction) and is orthogonal to ADS operation, assistance workflow, remote knowledge and fleet eligibility (P18 11.1–11.2).

ModeNew offersAccepted journeysSupportRequirement
NORMALAdmitted when the service promise is feasibleServed as committedNormalCapacity and evidence current
CONSTRAINEDRestricted by zone / timeProtectedNormal plus recovery workCAP-029
SUSPENDEDAffected new commitments stoppedProtected where feasible; otherwise recovered under 20.2Maintained, with local fallbackCAP-030

Transitions use configured triggers, persistence and owner approval (CAP-031). Persistence means a trigger must hold over its configured condition before a transition is proposed, so a single sample cannot change the mode. Recovery thresholds include hysteresis (CAP-032): the condition for leaving a mode is stricter than the condition that caused entry, so the mode does not oscillate around one threshold. The diagram steps through adjacent modes; whether a direct transition between NORMAL and SUSPENDED is permitted is not stated and is settled with the trigger configuration (TBD-028). In addition, new commitments are restricted when response capacity is exhausted (OPS-074).

27.D.5 Behaviour

Main flow: supply loss to recovery (D27.2).

  1. C04 reports a vehicle fault or communication loss (MissionObserved), or C05 reports a site outage or energy shortfall (EnergyUpdated). C06 opens or updates a case (CaseChanged) with severity and deadline.
  2. C06 requests an impact assessment. C03 identifies affected bookings and intervals and recomputes reachable vehicles, usable hubs and qualified response capacity (CAP-034). Already accepted commitments and unknown physical effects are preserved: a vehicle whose execution state is unknown keeps its occupancy (CAP-035, BKG-038).
  3. C03 holds the affected capacity and recomputes supply. Unmet demand and passenger exposure are recorded (CAP-036).
  4. If the configured trigger holds with persistence, the accountable owner approves the transition and C02 applies the admission restriction for the affected scope. A degraded-period record is opened (CAP-037).
  5. Three outcomes proceed in parallel and draw on the same finite fleet, site and staffing resources:
    1. Passenger. C02 contacts every affected passenger party, explains the revised ETA and alternatives (CAP-038); C03 reserves feasible replacement journeys; each handover and resolution is tracked (CAP-039); the compensation / refund owner decides (CAP-040).
    2. Vehicle / site. Fault and command history are retained; a qualified field responder observes secure state and clearance, inspects and records restrictions; unresolved physical effects are reconciled (CAP-041, CAP-042).
    3. Resource. Relief and field capacity are reserved including staff travel and queues; cargo custody, storage and returns are handled; passenger and cargo plans are revised; a recovery shortfall is escalated (CAP-043). C05 revises feasible energy and site slots.
  6. When the cause is addressed, C06 runs the release review: the return-to-service gate is evaluated (27.D.6). On pass, C03 reassesses availability; the gate does not command the ADS to move (OPS-055).
  7. After sustained recovery is observed, the accountable owner approves the transition to a less restrictive mode and C02 widens offers (CAP-046). The degraded-period record is closed with its recovery evidence.

Alternative flows.

  1. Demand pressure without supply loss. Peak arrivals, directional imbalance, longer trips or slow turnaround make new offers infeasible in a zone / time. The impact assessment runs without a vehicle case; the usual outcome is CONSTRAINED for the affected scope. No field responder is required, but unmet demand is recorded.
  2. Staff absence. Qualified response capacity is recomputed; if the response-capacity condition fails, new commitments are restricted (OPS-074) and relief capacity is requested.
  3. Recovery within persistence. If a trigger clears before its persistence condition is met, no transition is proposed; the case still records the event.

Exception flows.

  1. Owner approval unavailable. The case escalates to the backup owner (CAP-048); admission is not widened while approval is pending.
  2. Connectivity restored, evidence incomplete. Connectivity restoration alone cannot release capacity (CAP-045); the vehicle stays held until the gate passes.
  3. Recovery shortfall. If relief, field or replacement capacity is insufficient, the shortfall is escalated, the admission restriction is reviewed, and passenger outcomes remain owned until resolved.
  4. Material new evidence. A resolved case is reopened (OPS-013, P13 6.1); capacity released on the previous evidence is re-held if the new evidence invalidates a gate conjunct.
  5. Several affected parties on one vehicle. Each passenger party has its own outcome and handover; one replacement journey does not close the outcome of another party.

27.D.6 Return-to-service gate

Capacity returns to service only when all five conditions hold (CAP-044, D27.3). The gate corresponds to the release predicate of P18 11.3, in which no predicate substitutes for another (OPS-052).

Gate conditionRelease predicateEvidenceTypical failure
Cause addressedC corrective actionCause removed or approved restriction recorded; field / inspection work complete if requiredFault cleared by reboot only, cause unknown
Fresh evidenceV vehicle evidenceCurrent, mutually consistent required signals; local readiness and ODD status acceptedRepeated or old state presented as recovery
Authorised releaseA authorised ownershipCurrent case revision + valid release authority; no blocking incident or unresolved commandLease expired; unresolved command
Feasible next missionF feasible missionRoute, energy and resource bundle reconciled; D1 permit currentEnergy below bound; hub unavailable
Passenger outcome resolvedF feasible mission (passenger outcome known)Every affected party’s handover and resolution recordedParty not contacted; replacement not confirmed

Passing the gate returns a vehicle or hub to C03’s availability assessment; it does not by itself change the service mode. Widening offers is a separate decision that requires sustained recovery across the affected scope.

27.D.7 Response capacity

The offered load is A = Σ λ_k E[S_k], where λ_k is the arrival rate of case type k and E[S_k] the expected handling time of that type, both in matched time units (CAP-047, OPS-072). A < qualified staffed seats is only a mean-load screen (ASM-025): it says the centre is not overloaded on average, not that each case is handled in time. The screen is therefore supplemented by tests of bursts, common-cause alarms, breaks and travel (D27.4, OPS-073). Every open case needs an owner, deadline and backup (CAP-048), and field response is kept separate from remote assistance (CAP-049) because field work includes staff travel and queues and cannot be absorbed by a free remote seat. The values of qualified staffed seats and relief capacity are open (TBD-045, TBD-008).

27.D.8 Rules and invariants

R27.1
The service mode restricts admission of new commitments only; it never changes ADS mode, fleet eligibility or case state (CAP-033).
R27.2
Accepted journeys are protected in CONSTRAINED; in SUSPENDED, support and local fallback are maintained (CAP-029, CAP-030).
R27.3
No transition without trigger, persistence and owner approval; no exit without the recovery threshold with hysteresis (CAP-031, CAP-032).
R27.4
The impact assessment preserves accepted commitments and unknown physical effects (CAP-035).
R27.5
Every affected passenger party is contacted and its outcome tracked to resolution (CAP-038, CAP-039).
R27.6
Capacity returns only through the five-condition gate; connectivity restoration alone never releases capacity (CAP-044, CAP-045).
R27.7
Offers widen only after sustained recovery is observed (CAP-046).
R27.8
Every open case has an owner, deadline and backup; expired or unacknowledged ownership triggers reassignment, not silent abandonment (CAP-048, OPS-016).
R27.9
Closing a case never automatically clears an operational hold (P18 11.2).
R27.10
Each degraded period is recorded with trigger, affected scope, admission restriction, accountable owner, next review and recovery evidence (CAP-037).

27.D.9 Data and state

The degraded-period record holds the six items of R27.10 together with the unmet demand and passenger exposure of the period (CAP-036). The document does not assign the record or the current service mode to a D-store; this is an open point. All other state is carried by existing models:

  • Case lifecycle OPEN → ASSIGNED → ACK → ACTIVE → RESOLVED → CLOSED in D5 / D7, with owner lease and dueAt.
  • Fleet eligibility AVAILABLE / RESTRICTED / HELD and remote knowledge CURRENT / DEGRADED / UNKNOWN (P18 11.2).
  • Booking states in D1, including RECONCILING after a timeout or lost acknowledgement (P09 2.3; shown as UNKNOWN in the P04 booking lifecycle), and the dispatch permit.
  • ResourceBundle and ResourceInterval in D2 for held, replacement and relief capacity.
  • Fault and command history in D3 (CommandAuditEvent).

Events on C09: MissionObserved, EnergyUpdated, CaseChanged, AllocationCommitted and BookingChanged. Each carries correlationId so that a passenger outcome can be traced to the originating case.

27.D.10 Interfaces used

  • I04: fault, communication state, secure-state evidence; the vehicle keeps local fallback regardless of link state.
  • I07: case assignment, lease, escalation, release decision; permissions differ by case type.
  • I03: hold of affected capacity, replacement journeys, binding reason when no replacement is feasible.
  • I02 and I06: amended bookings and activity holds for affected passengers.
  • I05: site outage, energy shortfall and revised feasible slots.
  • C09: event propagation with idempotent consumers; a replayed CaseChanged must not reopen admission.

27.D.11 Security, privacy and audit

  • Transition approval, release authority and compensation decisions are recorded with the acting owner and the evidence used; an approval without a current case revision is rejected.
  • Passenger contact uses accessible channels and gives status and alternatives only; passenger support cannot override door interlocks or authorise motion and gives no unsafe exit instruction (OPS-024).
  • Passenger exposure is recorded for the degraded period at the level needed for review; individual contact records stay within the booking scope of the party concerned.
  • Retained fault and command history is the basis of reconciliation and review and is not deleted when the case closes.

27.D.12 Observability and operations

The operator workspace (P21 14.1) shows, per affected scope: the current mode, its trigger and next review; affected bookings and passengers not yet contacted; vehicles held and the gate condition each still fails; relief and field capacity reserved versus required; and open cases by owner, deadline and backup. Measures recorded per degraded period: detection, acknowledgement, resolution, overdue cases and failed recovery (OPS-073), unmet demand and passenger exposure.

27.D.13 Verification approach

  1. Drive each transition of D27.1 with a trigger that holds, one that clears within persistence, and one that oscillates around the recovery threshold; confirm no transition without approval and no repeated entry / exit.
  2. In CONSTRAINED, confirm accepted journeys keep their bundles while new offers in the affected zone / time are restricted; in SUSPENDED, confirm support and local fallback remain available.
  3. Evaluate the gate with each condition false in turn and confirm capacity stays held; include connectivity restored with stale evidence (CAP-045; fault pattern T-R06 of P24 17.1).
  4. Run the cross-products of P18 11.3 together with service-mode changes, so that the mode is shown not to alter ADS mode or case state.
  5. Run the response-capacity stress tests of D27.4, plus handover and centre loss (OPS-073).
  6. Combine faults with a recovery ramp in the scenarios of P28 21.2 and confirm that recovery competes correctly with service demand for the same fleet, site and staff.

27.D.14 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Admission control, not vehicle control
A service mode that also changed vehicle behaviour would couple a centre decision to local safety. Restricting only new commitments keeps the ADS authority boundary intact and lets the mode change without vehicle coordination.
Three modes
A binary on / off model forces a choice between over-promising and stopping service. CONSTRAINED lets the service continue for unaffected zones and times while protecting accepted journeys.
Persistence, approval and hysteresis
Automatic transitions on a single signal could oscillate and confuse passengers with repeated offer changes. Persistence filters transients, approval assigns accountability, and hysteresis prevents re-entry immediately after exit.
Parallel outcomes
Treating passenger recovery as a consequence of vehicle recovery delays support. Running the three outcomes in parallel, each with its own owner, keeps the passenger outcome moving while the vehicle is inspected.
Gate with five conditions
Each condition protects against a different false release: a cleared symptom, old evidence, missing authority, an infeasible next mission, or a passenger left unresolved.

27.D.15 Open points

  • Service-mode triggers, persistence and recovery thresholds with hysteresis, and permitted transitions (TBD-028).
  • Operations parameters: response class, seat / field coverage and escalation (TBD-008); qualified staffed seats and relief capacity (TBD-045); hours / staffing / recovery limits (TBD-013).
  • Owning store of the degraded-period record and the current service mode (not stated).
  • Compensation / refund policy content (owner required by CAP-040; policy not stated).

Operating feasibility and verification evidence

A configuration qualifies only within its tested demand, geography and operating conditions. Service quality, resource limits, recovery and economics require separate evidence.

21.1Measurement chain and explicit denominators

  1. RequestsUnique service intents
  2. DispatchVerified assignment
  3. PickupPhysical arrival
  4. CompletionVerified trip outcome

Service quality

  • Dispatch success = assigned / eligible dispatch requests.
  • Keep capacity and admission rejects in the denominator.
  • Demand fulfillment = completed / eligible requests.
  • Report customer cancellations separately by reason.

Pickup and utilization

Wait starts at request time for immediate demand, or agreed pickup time for a reservation. Report p50 / p95 with the observed-arrival count and missing outcomes. Show on-time pickups / pickups due, including failures. Separate available hours from scheduled fleet hours.

At cut-off, classify every passenger booking and shipment separately: completed, cancelled, rejected, expired, unresolved or active. A pooled mission is not one passenger request. Retain people counts separately from booking counts. Show exclusions, censoring and missing evidence.

D28.1Data flowMeasurement chain from intent to verified outcome

Each stage of 21.1 takes its count from the component that owns the evidence. Rejections and cancellations leave the chain as classified outcomes; they are never dropped from the denominator.

Source: P28 21.1; P10 3.1; P08 1.1; P02 02

D28.2InterfaceMeasure definitions: numerator, denominator and treatment

Each measure of 21.1 with only the numerator, denominator and treatment rules the chapter states. Cells left as “not stated” are not defined in the document.

Counting unit

21.2Reproducible scenario design and pass conditions

  1. Freeze inputs
    • Passenger / cargo OD and windows
    • Lead time and sharing acceptance
    • Party, mass, volume and handling time
    • Fleet, hubs and response limits
    • Input / policy / route revisions
  2. Exercise conditions
    • Single-party / pooling / cargo / both
    • Peak and directional concentration
    • Vehicle / hub / energy capacity loss
    • No-show / failed cargo handover
    • Combined faults and recovery ramp
  3. Evaluate each case
    • Passenger and freight service gates
    • Seats, payload, volume and energy
    • Detour, dwell and recovery workload
    • Unserved / unresolved outcomes

PASS RECORD

State target, denominator, time window and acceptance rule before running. Use repeatable demand traces or recorded seeds, then independent trials. Preserve every run and failure. Finite synthetic tests establish a tested envelope only. Pilot evidence determines field readiness.

21.3Capacity decision and business consequence

Feasible alternatives

Compare fleet, hub placement and service policy only after all required operating conditions pass. Rank cost within the feasible tested set. If none qualifies, report the binding constraint and re-plan.

Economic reconciliation

  • Reconcile passenger fares and freight revenue.
  • Count shared route / infrastructure costs once.
  • Include dwell, displaced trips, handling and returns.
  • Separate operating contribution, CAPEX and cash flow.

Release evidence: input revision, scenario / seed, execution trace, metric definitions, pass / fail by condition, residual restriction and accountable decision. Operational feasibility does not by itself establish project profitability or safety certification.

D28.3State machineScenario and pass-record lifecycle

28.DDetailed specification

This section specifies how operating feasibility is measured and how a configuration of fleet, hubs and service policy is qualified. It defines the counting units and denominators of each service measure, the cut-off classification of bookings and shipments, the reproducible scenario and pass-record discipline, the evaluation of each case against its binding constraint, the capacity decision within the feasible tested set and the economic reconciliation that follows. It is the evidence side of P25–P27 and of the shared-capacity chapters P29–P30, and it implements the measurement contract of P05 and the experiment design of P06.

28.D.1 Purpose and scope

A configuration that works on average can still fail individual passengers, shipments or hubs. The purpose of this specification is to make each claim of feasibility traceable to a stated measure, an explicit denominator, a frozen input set and a preserved run, so that a reviewer can reproduce the result and see what was excluded. A configuration qualifies only within its tested demand, geography and operating conditions; service quality, resource limits, recovery and economics are separate evidence and none substitutes for another.

In scope: the measurement chain request → dispatch → pickup → completion; measure definitions; cut-off classification; scenario construction, execution and evaluation; the pass record and release evidence; the capacity decision and economic reconciliation. Out of scope: KPI target values (TBD-031), field-test design parameters (TBD-030), safety certification and project profitability (ASM-032).

28.D.2 Actors and responsibilities

ActorResponsibility
PMOwns measure selection, targets once baseline evidence exists, and the KPI decision (P07 product decision ownership).
EngineeringOwns metric definitions as contracts, trace quality, scenario reproducibility and the execution trace.
Operations / partnersOwn the service capacity and recovery assumptions used in scenarios; confirm response limits.
FinanceVerifies revenue scope, cost allocation and the separation of operating contribution, CAPEX and cash flow.
Accountable decision ownerSigns the pass / fail by condition, the residual restriction and the capacity decision.
C02, C03, C04, C07Supply the evidence for each stage: C02 requests and booking outcomes, C03 assignments and binding reasons, C04 physical arrival and mission evidence, C07 verified usage and ledger (D28.1).

28.D.3 Measurement chain and counting units

Each stage takes its count from the component that owns the evidence, never from a downstream summary:

  1. Requests are unique service intents in C02 / D1 (intentId, bookingRev). A repeated submission with the same idempotent request is one intent; an amendment is a new revision of the same intent, not a new request.
  2. Dispatch is a verified assignment: an AllocationCommitted outcome from C03 / D2 (bundleId, bundleRev). A hold or a quote is not an assignment, and an assignment is not completed service (SVC-056).
  3. Pickup is physical arrival observed by C04 (MissionObserved with missionRev and observedAt). A planned ETA is not a pickup.
  4. Completion is a verified trip outcome: UsageVerified from C07 where mission evidence, service actual and user outcome reconcile (SVC-046).

Counting units are kept apart: passenger bookings, shipments, people and vehicle missions (SVC-047). A pooled mission is not one passenger request, and people counts are retained separately from booking counts (CAP-056). The traceability key chain intentId + passenger / shipmentId + bookingRev + routeRev + missionId (SVC-016) links each counted item across stages.

28.D.4 Measure definitions

The definitions extend D28.2 with the treatment of edge cases. Eligibility for each denominator is stated in the pass record before running (CAP-058).

Dispatch success
Assigned / eligible dispatch requests. Capacity and admission rejects stay in the denominator (CAP-050); removing them would make a configuration that rejects demand look more reliable. Rejects are reported by binding reason.
Demand fulfillment
Completed / eligible requests. Customer cancellations are reported separately by reason (CAP-051) so that a cancellation caused by a revised ETA is distinguishable from a change of plan.
Pickup wait
Starts at request time for immediate demand, or at the agreed pickup time for a reservation; it ends at observed physical arrival. Reported as p50 / p95 with the observed-arrival count and missing outcomes (CAP-052). Consistent with P05, an arrival before the reference time does not produce a negative wait (SVC-054).
On-time pickup
On-time pickups / pickups due, including failures (CAP-053). A missed pickup is in the denominator as a failure, not excluded as missing.
Fleet hours
Available hours are reported separately from scheduled fleet hours (CAP-054), so that time lost to replenishment, faults and inspection (P25 18.2) is visible rather than absorbed into utilisation.

Censoring: an item whose outcome is not yet observed at cut-off is censored, not dropped. Exclusions, censoring and missing evidence are shown with every reported measure (CAP-057). A percentile computed only over observed arrivals is always shown with the number of arrivals that were not observed.

28.D.5 Cut-off classification

At cut-off, every passenger booking and every shipment is classified separately into exactly one of six classes (CAP-055). The class is derived from the D1 booking state and the verified evidence, not from the plan.

ClassDerived fromRule
completedCOMPLETED with reconciled mission evidence and service actualCounted only when evidence reconciles; an unreconciled completion is unresolved
cancelledCANCELLED (reason + release)Reason retained; customer and operator causes reported separately
rejectedI03 REJECTED with binding reasonKept in dispatch and fulfillment denominators
expiredQuote or hold that reached expiresAt without acceptanceRetained as an offer outcome
unresolvedUNKNOWN or RECONCILING; missing or conflicting evidenceNever counted as completed; shown with its owner
activeCONFIRMED or IN_SERVICE at cut-offReported as censored for completion measures

The sum of the six classes equals the number of bookings (or shipments) in scope; a reconciliation check that the sum matches the request count is part of every report.

28.D.6 Scenario design and execution

Main flow (D28.3):

  1. State the pass record. Target, denominator, time window and acceptance rule are written before running (CAP-058). A target is set only with baseline evidence (SVC-048).
  2. Freeze inputs. Passenger / cargo OD and windows; lead time and sharing acceptance; party, mass, volume and handling time; fleet, hubs and response limits; input, policy and route revisions. The evidence record holds engine / scenario version, input units and sources, demand trace, information receipt times, initial fleet / hub state, seed and effect switches (SVC-060).
  3. Exercise conditions. Single-party, pooling, cargo and both; peak and directional concentration; vehicle, hub and energy capacity loss; no-show and failed cargo handover; combined faults and recovery ramp.
  4. Run. Use repeatable demand traces or recorded seeds, then independent trials (CAP-059). Decisions in the run use only information already received at decision time (SVC-003).
  5. Preserve. Every run and failure is preserved, including runs that crashed, timed out or produced an unexpected result (CAP-060).
  6. Evaluate each case. Passenger and freight service gates; seats, payload, volume and energy; detour, dwell and recovery workload; unserved and unresolved outcomes; binding constraint and owner.

Alternative and exception flows.

  1. Run not reproducible. If a recorded seed or trace does not reproduce its result, the run is marked failed and the cause (non-determinism, undeclared input) is fixed before the scenario is used as evidence.
  2. Pass record changed after running. A changed target, denominator, window or acceptance rule creates a new pass record; earlier runs are evaluated against the record that was stated before they ran.
  3. Missing evidence in a run. Items with missing evidence are classified unresolved and shown; the run is not repaired by imputation.
  4. Paired comparisons. When effects are compared, paired runs use the same initial conditions and random seeds against a baseline with all effects off (SVC-057); each effect is reported as ΔK = K_effect − K_baseline with repeated-run differences and uncertainty (SVC-053).

28.D.7 Capacity decision and economic reconciliation

  1. Fleet, hub placement and service policy alternatives are compared only after all required operating conditions pass; cost is ranked only within the feasible tested set (CAP-062). An alternative that fails any required condition is not ranked, however cheap.
  2. If no alternative qualifies, the binding constraint is reported with its owner and the plan is revised (CAP-063). The minimum tested fleet meeting all service gates is the required-fleet measure of P05 (TBD-046).
  3. Economic reconciliation reconciles passenger fares and freight revenue, counts shared route / infrastructure costs once, includes dwell, displaced trips, handling and returns, and keeps operating contribution, CAPEX and cash flow separate (CAP-065, SVC-052). Revenue and cost come from the C07 contract and ledger.
  4. The release evidence comprises input revision, scenario / seed, execution trace, metric definitions, pass / fail by condition, residual restriction and accountable decision (CAP-064).

28.D.8 Rules and invariants

R28.1
Every measure has a stated numerator, denominator and time window; rejects stay in the denominator (CAP-050).
R28.2
Each stage count comes from the component owning its evidence; a plan, ACK or quote is never counted as an outcome.
R28.3
Every booking and shipment has exactly one cut-off class; unresolved items are never counted as completed (CAP-055).
R28.4
Bookings, shipments, people and vehicle missions are counted separately (CAP-056).
R28.5
The pass record is fixed before running (CAP-058).
R28.6
Every run and failure is preserved (CAP-060).
R28.7
Finite synthetic tests establish a tested envelope only; pilot evidence determines field readiness (CAP-061, ASM-031).
R28.8
Cost is ranked only within the feasible tested set (CAP-062); service feasibility remains binding even when aggregate contribution improves (SVC-075).
R28.9
Shared costs are counted once; operating contribution, CAPEX and cash flow are separate (CAP-065).

28.D.9 Data and lineage

The evidence of a run is a set of linked records, all referencing the frozen input revision:

  • Intent and booking records from D1 (intentId, bookingRev, state, termsRev) and offer outcomes.
  • Bundles and intervals from D2 (bundleId, bundleRev, policyVersion, inputSnapshotRef) and binding reasons for rejects.
  • Mission and status journal from D3 (missionRev, observedAt) for physical arrival and completion.
  • Energy plans and observed delivery from D4 where replenishment is in scope (P26).
  • Cases from D5 / D7 for recovery workload (P27).
  • Usage and ledger entries from D6 (UsageVerified, contractRev, billRev) for completion and economics.

Simulated acceptance is labelled as simulated and kept distinct from measured behaviour (SVC-061). Corrections to actuals are correction entries, so a report can be regenerated for any earlier revision.

28.D.10 Failure handling

Evidence failureHandling
Missing outcome at cut-offClassify unresolved or active; report as censored; show count with each measure
Conflicting evidence between stagesClassify unresolved; owner reconciles by original IDs; no stage overrides another silently
Duplicate intent or eventDeduplicate by intent and event identity; a duplicate never counts twice
Future-information leakage detectedRun rejected as evidence (SVC-003)
No alternative qualifiesReport binding constraint and owner; re-plan (CAP-063)
Unreconciled costGate holds (SVC-064)

28.D.11 Security, privacy and audit

  • Pilot evidence contains passenger and shipment records; reports use the counts and outcomes needed for the measure, within the consent scope recorded at intake (SVC-019).
  • The pass record, run artefacts and decision are retained together so that the decision can be audited against the evidence it relied on.
  • Each gate records owner, residual risk / restriction and signed decision (P24 17.3).

28.D.12 Verification approach

The measurement system is itself verified before it is used as evidence:

  1. Seed a known demand trace with a known set of outcomes (completions, cancellations, rejects, expiries, unknowns) and confirm every measure and every cut-off class reproduces the known values.
  2. Confirm the class sum equals the in-scope count for bookings and for shipments.
  3. Replay a run from its recorded seed and confirm identical results; repeat with independent trials and report the spread.
  4. Inject duplicate events on C09 and confirm no double count.
  5. Check a pooled mission with several bookings and confirm one vehicle mission, several bookings and the correct people count.
  6. Use the acceptance extension of P24 17.2: peak demand, spatial imbalance, finite hub capacity, replenishment queues and combined failures.

28.D.13 Decision process

The pass record feeds the gate process of P07. At G3 the evidence is the scenario / ODD slice, initial state, revisions, injected fault, trace and oracle result; G4 uses observed outcomes (P24 17.3). A failed required condition returns to the earliest gate whose assumption is invalidated (SVC-066); a REVISE names owner, required evidence, deadline and temporary scope restriction (SVC-065). Operational feasibility does not by itself establish project profitability or safety certification.

28.D.14 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Explicit denominators
Ratios over “served” requests reward rejection. Keeping capacity and admission rejects in the denominator makes the measure move in the same direction as the passenger’s experience.
Feasibility before cost
Ranking all alternatives by cost and then checking service would favour configurations that are cheap because they fail demand. Filtering to the feasible tested set first keeps service limits binding.
Pre-stated pass record
Choosing the acceptance rule after seeing results invites selection of the favourable window or denominator. Fixing it before running makes the outcome falsifiable.
Tested envelope
A finite set of synthetic scenarios cannot cover the field. Stating the envelope explicitly prevents a simulation pass from being read as field readiness.

28.D.15 Open points

  • KPI targets, which require baseline evidence (TBD-031).
  • Required fleet from the fleet sweep (TBD-046).
  • Field design: assignment unit, observation window and thresholds (TBD-030).
  • Finance record contents for the GO / HOLD decision (TBD-051).
  • Implementation, performance and safety validation (TBD-052).

Capacity along the route

For each segment s: Σ_i onboard(i,s) × partySize_i ≤ seats_usable(s)

D29.2Decision logicInsertion feasibility check with binding reasons

The constraints of 22.2 evaluated for one candidate insertion. Each check either passes to the next or returns its own binding reason; a hard constraint is never relaxed to make an insertion fit.

Higher occupancy can coexist with fewer completed journeys. Agree thresholds and operating authority before pilot release.

29.DDetailed specification

This section specifies shared rides (value mechanism 04) as a guarded route insertion. It defines when a request is eligible to share, how C03 evaluates a candidate insertion against every onboard and committed passenger, how consent and commitment are obtained from the new party, how the shared route is observed and reconciled after no-shows, delays and cancellations, and how the outcome is measured against single-party operation on the same demand. It uses the reservation saga of P11 4.1 unchanged and adds the per-segment and per-passenger constraints of 22.2.

29.D.1 Purpose and scope

Sharing can raise passenger output per vehicle-hour, but only when compatible journeys fit the same route without breaking any accepted promise. The purpose of this specification is to make every insertion a checked, consented and revisioned change to one vehicle mission, and to measure sharing by completed journeys and contribution rather than by occupancy.

In scope: request eligibility; candidate insertion and the feasibility check; offer, consent and commit; execution and observation per party; reconciliation after no-show, delay and cancellation; stress cases; measures and the comparison basis. Out of scope: the ranking weights among feasible insertions (TBD-032), fare levels (TBD-015) and freight on the same route, which P30 specifies.

29.D.2 Actors and responsibilities

ActorResponsibility
New party (rider)States pickup / arrival windows, party size and accessible-space needs; gives sharing consent; accepts the sharing price and allowed detour.
Onboard and committed partiesHold accepted windows, access requirements and detour allowances that every insertion must protect; receive revised ETAs.
C02 Booking / activitiesKeeps each party’s intent and booking; offers sharing price and allowed detour explicitly (CAP-072); persists COMMIT_PENDING and commits; notifies each party.
C03 Joint reservation authorityGenerates candidate insertions; checks segment capacity, accessible positions, luggage and every passenger’s time constraints; holds seats and the route revision; returns a binding reason when infeasible; stops adding riders when a limit would fail.
C04 Fleet / vehicle adapterRecords one vehicle mission with several bookings (SVC-012); receives the mission revision with routeRef and ordered stops; observes boarding and alighting per party.
C06 OperationsOwns exceptions on a shared route, including vehicle loss with several parties needing recovery.
C07 Usage / settlementSettles recognized fares after discounts per booking and counts route cost once.

29.D.3 Preconditions and inputs

  • The request is eligible: pickup / arrival windows, party size and accessible space, sharing consent and fare terms, and maximum accepted ride time are known (22.1).
  • The vehicle’s current route revision, ordered stops and segment occupancy are current in D2; the vehicle configuration defines seats_usable(s), accessible positions and luggage space.
  • Every onboard and committed party has earliestPickup_i, latestPickup_i, latestArrival_i and detourAllowance_i recorded with its accepted terms.
  • Direct time and ride time are computed on the same traffic / time basis (CAP-070).
  • The response-capacity constraint for the operating area is known, so that the stop rule can be evaluated (CAP-076).

29.D.4 Behaviour

Main flow: insertion into an existing mission (D29.1).

  1. The new party submits a request with windows, party size and sharing consent. C02 normalises the intent and sends Plan(terms, windows) to C03.
  2. C03 generates candidate insertions. For each, the pickup is placed before the drop-off and every downstream ETA is recomputed (CAP-066), including boarding, alighting and intermediate dwell.
  3. C03 evaluates the feasibility check of D29.2 in order: seats on every segment (CAP-067); accessible positions and luggage space under the vehicle configuration (CAP-068); windows for every passenger; arrival and detour (CAP-069). The check covers every onboard and committed passenger, not only the new party (CAP-071).
  4. Feasible candidates are ranked; ranking never relaxes a hard constraint (BKG-010, Appendix B C03).
  5. The D2 transaction creates an expiring HELD bundle for the seats and the route revision (BKG-020).
  6. C02 offers the sharing price, allowed detour and hold expiry to the new party (CAP-072).
  7. The party accepts (Accept(termsRev)). Expired or changed input is rejected; otherwise D1 persists COMMIT_PENDING, intent and outbox (BKG-024).
  8. C03 re-checks every onboard and committed passenger against the current route before the commit is applied, then commits; AllocationCommitted is published. Each intent is linked to the route revision (BKG-032).
  9. C04 receives the mission revision with routeRef and ordered stops. C02 publishes BookingChanged with the revised ETA for each affected party.
  10. C04 observes boarding and alighting per party (MissionObserved). Each intent keeps its own booking-level outcome.

Alternative flows.

  1. Infeasible. No promise is made; C03 returns REJECTED with the binding reason and, where available, an alternative (CAP-073), for example a single-party journey or a different window. The binding reason names the failed check (seat, accessible position, luggage, window, arrival or detour).
  2. Party declines or hold expires. The HELD bundle expires and releases its unused hold; the existing route revision is unchanged.
  3. Route changed between hold and accept. The accept is rejected as changed input; a new candidate is evaluated against the current revision.
  4. Stop rule. If adding the party would make an accepted passenger limit or the response-capacity constraint fail, C03 stops adding riders to that mission (CAP-076).

Exception flows (stress cases of 22.4, D29.3).

  1. No-show after insertion. Reconciliation is triggered (CAP-074): the no-show is recorded as that party’s booking outcome; its stops are removed in a new route revision; downstream ETAs are recomputed; the seats on later segments are released only after reconciliation (BKG-030).
  2. Delayed boarding or traffic delay. Every downstream ETA is recomputed and each remaining party’s window, arrival and detour constraint is rechecked. Where a constraint can no longer hold, the affected party is notified with alternatives and the case is owned.
  3. Cancellation while onboard. Reconciliation is triggered; the party’s seat stays occupied until alighting is observed, because a started allocation retains occupancy until physical clearance (BKG-038); a new route revision reorders the stops.
  4. Full accessible space. An insertion requiring an accessible position fails with that binding reason; accepted access requirements of onboard parties are protected.
  5. Mismatched OD / low overlap. The detour constraint fails; the request is offered a non-shared alternative.
  6. Vehicle loss with several parties. Degraded-operation recovery of P27 20.2 applies per party: each party is contacted, a feasible replacement journey is reserved and each handover is tracked.

29.D.5 Rules and invariants

R29.1
Pickup precedes drop-off for every party in every route revision (CAP-066).
R29.2
For each segment s, Σ_i onboard(i,s) × partySize_i ≤ seats_usable(s); party size counts people, not bookings (CAP-067, BKG-018).
R29.3
Accessible positions and luggage space are checked separately; seats do not substitute for them (CAP-068).
R29.4
For each passenger i, the pickup window, arrival limit and detour allowance hold, with ride time including boarding, alighting and intermediate dwell and direct time on the same basis (CAP-069, CAP-070).
R29.5
An insertion never breaks an accepted window or access requirement of an onboard or committed passenger (CAP-071, BKG-005).
R29.6
Sharing price and allowed detour are offered explicitly; no party is added to a shared route without accepted terms (CAP-072, SVC-005).
R29.7
An infeasible insertion returns a binding reason (CAP-073).
R29.8
A pooled route is one vehicle mission with several passenger bookings; its distance is counted once (CAP-075).
R29.9
Each party keeps its own intent, booking and outcome through the shared route (SVC-011).
R29.10
Stop adding riders when an accepted passenger limit or response-capacity constraint would fail (CAP-076).

29.D.6 Data and state

A shared route is represented by existing entities: one Mission / Command with routeRef and missionRev in D3; one bundle per booking in D2 whose ResourceInterval entries hold seats on the segments the party occupies (pooled capacityType, summed per segment); one Booking per party in D1 with its own bookingRev and termsRev. Segment occupancy is the per-segment sum over the bundles; it is derived, not stored separately as a second source of truth.

ItemHeld inChanged by
Route revision, ordered stopsD2 (route / segment capacity), mission revision in D3Commit of an insertion; reconciliation after no-show / cancellation
onboard(i,s), partySize_iSeat intervals of party i’s bundleInsertion, observed boarding / alighting
earliestPickup_i, latestPickup_i, latestArrival_i, detourAllowance_iAccepted terms of booking i (termsRev)Only by an accepted amendment of that party
Accepted detour / fareD1 booking termsAccept(termsRev)
Actual passenger timesMissionObserved in D3Observation only
Booking-level outcomeD1Completion, no-show, cancellation, reconciliation

Booking states follow D04.2 (as seen by the user) and D11.3 (D1 finalisation), and reservation transitions follow D09.3; sharing adds no state.

29.D.7 Interfaces used

  • I02: request, offer with hold expiry, Accept(termsRev), cancel.
  • I03: Plan, Hold, CommitBundle with expectedResourceRevs covering the seat intervals of all affected segments; REJECTED with binding reason.
  • I04: mission revision with routeRef and ordered stops; boarding / alighting observation.
  • C09: AllocationCommitted, BookingChanged per party, MissionObserved.
  • I08: verified usage per booking for fare settlement.

29.D.8 Measures and comparison basis

Sharing is evaluated on three groups of measures (22.3), always side by side:

Passenger output
Passenger journeys / vehicle-hour; passenger-km / vehicle-km; seat-km used / available seat-km; wait, detour and missed pickups. Journeys are completed journeys under P28 21.1, not boardings.
Net contribution
Recognized fares after discounts, less route, energy and support cost, including added dwell and recovery, with route cost allocated only once.
Comparable alternatives
Single-party versus shared operation on the same underlying passenger intents and the same fleet, hubs and faults, with rejected and displaced trips visible (CAP-092).

Total contribution and passenger fulfillment are shown together (CAP-077). Higher occupancy can coexist with fewer completed journeys, for example when detours push other parties outside their windows; a comparison that reports occupancy alone is incomplete.

29.D.9 Security, privacy and audit

  • Each party receives its own ETA and booking status; one party’s booking details are not part of another party’s notification.
  • Sharing consent is recorded with the accepted terms and is not inferred from a previous booking (SVC-005).
  • Accessibility needs are used for the feasibility check and recorded with the booking terms; they are not shown to other parties.
  • Shared-ride evidence records route revision, ordered stops, segment occupancy, accepted detour / fare, actual passenger times and booking-level outcomes (CAP-077).

29.D.10 Verification approach

  1. For each check of D29.2, construct an insertion that fails only that check and confirm the binding reason names it.
  2. Construct an insertion that satisfies the new party but breaks an onboard party’s window; confirm rejection (R29.5).
  3. Change the route between hold and accept; confirm the accept is rejected as changed input.
  4. Run each stress case of D29.3 and confirm reconciliation, booking-level outcomes and route revisions.
  5. Run single-party and shared operation on the same intents, fleet, hubs and faults and report passenger output, net contribution and rejected / displaced trips together (CAP-092).
  6. At G3, verify seat limits per segment and route revisions on normal and fault paths (SVC-068).

29.D.11 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Re-check everyone
Checking only the new party is cheaper but lets each insertion erode earlier promises. Rechecking every onboard and committed passenger, and again before commit, keeps every accepted promise binding.
Per-segment capacity
A vehicle-level seat count allows a route in which two parties overlap on one segment beyond capacity. Checking each segment matches how seats are actually used.
Explicit consent and price
An implicit sharing default would change the party’s journey without acceptance; stating price and allowed detour makes the trade-off the party’s decision.
Occupancy is not success
Occupancy rises when vehicles carry more people, but also when detours lengthen rides. Completed journeys per vehicle-hour and contribution, against a single-party baseline, measure the actual gain.

29.D.12 Open points

  • Shared-ride thresholds and operating authority, agreed before pilot release (TBD-029, CAP-078).
  • Ranking weights for empty km / wait / cost / risk (TBD-032).
  • Fare, demand and transit-overlap limits (TBD-015).
  • KPI targets for the shared-capacity measures (TBD-031).

23.2Capacity is a vector at each route segment

Independent constraints

Passenger seats and accessible positions remain within their configured limits.

Σ_j cargoVolume_j,s ≤ usableCargoVolume_s   and   Σ_j onboardMass_j,s ≤ payloadLimit_s
  • Onboard mass includes people, luggage and cargo under the same payload boundary.
  • Check segregation, securement, door access and passenger comfort before accepting a job.

Time and recovery constraint

  • Route time = travel + passenger dwell + cargo handling + required turnaround.
  • Recompute every pickup, arrival and delivery ETA.
  • Cargo waiting / failed handover consumes capacity.
  • Protect passenger recovery and energy reserve.

Service policy and authority

  • Use an approved vehicle / goods combination.
  • Confirm transport, insurance and partner eligibility.
  • Assign loading, custody and exception owners.
  • Decline cargo that breaks passenger commitments.
  • Apply return / storage rules after failed delivery.
D30.2Data modelCapacity vector at one route segment

Each route segment carries independent capacity dimensions. A job is accepted only when every dimension holds on every segment it occupies; no dimension compensates for another.

Time is checked separately: route time = travel + passenger dwell + cargo handling + required turnaround, and every pickup, arrival and delivery ETA is recomputed.

Source: P30 23.2; P29 22.2

  • Passenger revenue reflects discounts and displaced / unserved trips. Do not subtract that loss twice.
  • Include handling, detours, energy, cleaning, support, returns / claims and app cost. Count route cost once.

Report passenger fulfillment / delay and freight delivery / lateness separately, plus vehicle-hours, payload / volume limits, dwell and total contribution. Hold effects 01–03 constant across the four conditions, then test interactions.

30.DDetailed specification

This section specifies passenger–freight sharing (value mechanism 05): carrying shipments on spare route and vehicle capacity without weakening any passenger commitment. It defines shipment eligibility and service authority, the joint feasibility check over a capacity vector at each route segment, the custody chain from pickup to verified delivery or return, the handling of failed handovers and exceptions, and the four-condition economic comparison that decides whether freight adds net contribution. It reuses the reservation saga of P11 4.1 and the insertion discipline of P29.

30.D.1 Purpose and scope

Freight can use capacity that a passenger route leaves idle, but each shipment adds dwell, handling, custody obligations and failure modes that passengers do not. The purpose of this specification is to admit cargo only where it fits every capacity dimension on every segment, keeps passenger windows binding and protects recovery and energy reserve, and to account for freight so that incremental revenue is compared with all the costs it causes.

In scope: shipment request and eligibility; joint feasibility with passengers; capacity per segment; route time; custody handovers, delivery proof, failed attempts, returns, loss and damage; the four operating conditions and the contribution comparison; outcome and failure evidence. Out of scope: goods classification policy, insurance terms and partner contracts, which are recorded as eligibility inputs (TBD-047).

30.D.2 Actors and responsibilities

ActorResponsibility
Shipment party / handover contactStates origin / destination and windows, mass, volume and compartment needs, handling time and the handover contact; hands over and receives cargo.
C02 Booking / activitiesKeeps the shipment intent separate from passenger intents (SVC-011); checks permitted goods / service policy with Org (CAP-085); offers, persists and commits.
C03 Joint reservation authorityInserts loading / unloading dwell; checks payload, cargo volume, access and every passenger window per segment; reserves staff and loading space; declines cargo that breaks passenger commitments (CAP-084).
C04 Fleet / vehicle adapterLinks the shipment to the route revision; records pickup / custody handovers and delivery or failed-attempt proof (CAP-087).
C06 OperationsOwns loading, custody and exception assignments and return, loss and damage cases (CAP-086, CAP-088).
C07 Usage / settlementReconciles freight revenue with passenger fares; counts route cost once (SVC-014).
Hub staffLoad, secure and unload cargo within reserved staff and loading-space intervals.
Org / partnersApprove the vehicle / goods combination; confirm transport, insurance and partner eligibility (CAP-085).

30.D.3 Preconditions and inputs

  • The goods are permitted under the service policy and the vehicle / goods combination is approved; transport, insurance and partner eligibility are confirmed (CAP-085, TBD-047).
  • Consent, capacity and custody ownership have been agreed at G2 (SVC-067, TBD-050).
  • The vehicle configuration defines, per segment, seats, accessible positions, usableCargoVolume_s and payloadLimit_s.
  • The current route revision, its passenger bookings and their windows are current in D1 / D2.
  • Staff and loading space at origin and destination are available as resource intervals (CAP-016).

30.D.4 Behaviour

Main flow: shipment lifecycle (D30.1).

  1. The shipment party submits a request with OD, windows, mass, volume, compartment needs, handling time and handover contact. C02 checks permitted goods and service policy and normalises the shipment intent.
  2. C02 sends Plan(terms, windows) to C03. C03 inserts loading and unloading dwell into candidate routes and recomputes every pickup, arrival and delivery ETA; route time = travel + passenger dwell + cargo handling + required turnaround (CAP-082).
  3. C03 checks, on every segment the shipment occupies, each dimension of the capacity vector (D30.2): seats and accessible positions within limits (CAP-080); Σ_j cargoVolume_j,s ≤ usableCargoVolume_s and Σ_j onboardMass_j,s ≤ payloadLimit_s, with onboard mass including people, luggage and cargo (CAP-079). It checks segregation, securement, door access and passenger comfort (CAP-081). Passenger windows remain binding.
  4. If any check fails, or the shipment would break a passenger commitment, C03 declines with a binding reason and alternative (CAP-084). Otherwise it holds seats / cargo / loading slot, staff and loading space in one bundle (HELD with expiry, BKG-020).
  5. C02 offers terms; the party accepts (Accept(termsRev)); D1 persists COMMIT_PENDING and C03 commits. The shipment is linked to the route revision (BKG-032).
  6. C04 receives the mission revision. C06 assigns loading, custody and exception owners (CAP-086).
  7. At pickup, the handover is recorded with custody evidence and published as MissionObserved.
  8. At delivery, the handover or a failed attempt is recorded with proof (CAP-087).
  9. C07 records UsageVerified: freight revenue is reconciled and route cost is counted once (SVC-014).

Alternative flows.

  1. Incompatible goods. The request is declined at step 1 or 3 (policy, segregation or vehicle / goods combination) with the binding reason.
  2. Hold expiry or decline by the party. The HELD bundle expires and releases seats / cargo / loading slot and staff intervals.
  3. Cargo on a single-party route. The same checks apply with one passenger party; the passenger’s accepted terms remain binding.

Exception flows.

  1. Absent recipient / failed delivery. Failed-attempt proof is recorded; return / storage rules apply (CAP-088). Cargo waiting or a failed handover consumes capacity: the volume and mass remain on the remaining segments, and any storage or return trip is a new reserved interval (CAP-083).
  2. Long unloading. Actual dwell exceeds the reserved handling time; downstream ETAs are recomputed; passengers whose windows can no longer hold are notified with alternatives and the case is owned.
  3. Full payload. A later insertion (passenger or cargo) that would exceed payloadLimit_s on any segment is declined; passengers already committed are not displaced by cargo.
  4. Cancellation. A cancelled shipment not yet picked up releases its intervals after reconciliation (BKG-030); a cancelled shipment already onboard keeps its capacity until it is unloaded and its custody resolved.
  5. Vehicle loss. Passenger recovery and energy reserve are protected first (CAP-083); cargo custody, storage and returns follow P27 20.2 under the assigned exception owner.
  6. Loss or damage. A case is opened under C06 with owner and deadline; custody evidence identifies the last confirmed handover.

30.D.5 Rules and invariants

R30.1
Capacity is a vector at each route segment; each dimension holds independently and none compensates for another (CAP-079, CAP-080).
R30.2
Onboard mass includes people, luggage and cargo under the same payload boundary (CAP-079).
R30.3
Passenger windows remain binding; cargo that breaks passenger commitments is declined (CAP-084).
R30.4
Route time includes cargo handling, and every pickup, arrival and delivery ETA is recomputed after each change (CAP-082).
R30.5
Cargo waiting and failed handover consume capacity; passenger recovery and energy reserve stay protected (CAP-083).
R30.6
Only an approved vehicle / goods combination with confirmed eligibility carries cargo (CAP-085).
R30.7
Every shipment has loading, custody and exception owners (CAP-086).
R30.8
Each shipment is linked to the route revision; each custody handover and the delivery or failed attempt is recorded with proof (CAP-087).
R30.9
Passenger and shipment identities are kept within one shared mission (CAP-089); completion uses passenger and cargo evidence separately (SVC-018).
R30.10
Route cost is counted once; displaced / unserved trip loss is not subtracted twice (CAP-091).

30.D.6 Data and state

A shipment is an intent in D1 with its own shipmentId in the traceability chain intentId + passenger / shipmentId + bookingRev + routeRev + missionId (SVC-016). Its bundle in D2 holds cargo intervals on the segments it occupies, together with staff and loading-space intervals at origin and destination. The mission in D3 carries both passenger and shipment stops in one ordered list.

Shipments use the same booking and bundle states as passenger bookings; cut-off classification is applied to shipments separately (CAP-055).

30.D.7 Interfaces used

  • I02: shipment request, offer, accept, cancel.
  • I03: plan, hold and commit of seats / cargo / loading slot, staff and loading space as one bundle.
  • I04: mission revision with shipment stops; custody handover and delivery observation.
  • I07: exception cases for return, loss and damage.
  • I08 and C09: verified usage, UsageVerified and freight revenue reconciliation.

30.D.8 Economic comparison

Freight is evaluated in four operating conditions on the same demand basis (D30.3): single-party, shared rides, passenger + cargo, and combined. Effects 01–03 are held constant across the four, and interactions are tested only afterwards (CAP-090, SVC-050).

Δ contribution = Δ passenger revenue + freight revenue − Δ total attributable operating cost
  1. Δ passenger revenue is measured from net passenger fares, which already reflect discounts and displaced / unserved trips; that loss is therefore not subtracted again as a cost (CAP-091).
  2. Freight revenue is recognized freight revenue from the C07 ledger.
  3. Δ total attributable operating cost includes handling, detours, energy, cleaning, support, returns / claims and app cost; route cost is counted once across passengers and cargo.
  4. The result is shown with passenger fulfillment / delay and freight delivery / lateness reported separately, plus vehicle-hours, payload / volume limits, dwell and total contribution (CAP-093).

A positive Δ contribution does not qualify freight if a passenger service gate fails; service feasibility remains binding (SVC-075).

30.D.9 Security, privacy and audit

  • Handover contact details are used for the shipment’s handovers and exceptions and are kept within the shipment’s booking scope.
  • Passengers sharing the vehicle are not given shipment details beyond what passenger comfort and safety information requires.
  • Custody evidence is retained as the basis for loss and damage cases and is not overwritten; corrections to revenue or cost are correction entries (ENE-040).
  • Approval of the vehicle / goods combination and eligibility confirmations are recorded with the approving owner.

30.D.10 Verification approach

  1. For each dimension of the capacity vector, construct a shipment that fails only that dimension on one segment and confirm decline with that binding reason.
  2. Construct a shipment that fits all cargo dimensions but makes a passenger miss a window; confirm decline (R30.3).
  3. Run the stress tests of 23.4: full payload, long unloading, absent recipient, incompatible goods, cancellation and vehicle loss (D30.3).
  4. Confirm one shared mission retains passenger and shipment identities and separate outcomes (CAP-089).
  5. Run the four conditions with effects 01–03 held constant and check that route cost appears once and displaced-trip loss is not double counted.
  6. At G3, rehearse failed delivery and rollback and verify payload limits per segment (SVC-068).

30.D.11 Design rationale and alternatives considered

Capacity vector
A single “space” number would let spare seats hide a full cargo area, or cargo volume hide a payload overrun. Independent dimensions per segment keep each physical limit visible.
Shared payload boundary
Passengers, luggage and cargo load the same vehicle; a separate cargo mass limit that ignored people could exceed the vehicle’s payload.
Passenger priority
Freight is incremental by definition; allowing cargo to displace committed passengers would turn a shared-capacity gain into a service loss.
Custody chain
Freight failures can be discovered after the fact. Recording every handover with evidence lets a loss or damage case identify where custody last held.
Four conditions
Comparing only combined operation against single-party would mix the effects of pooling and cargo; four conditions separate each effect before interactions are tested.

30.D.12 Open points

  • Approved vehicle / goods combinations; transport, insurance and partner eligibility (TBD-047).
  • Consent, capacity and custody ownership; passenger and freight gates; cost boundaries (TBD-050, G2).
  • Fare, demand and transit-overlap limits (TBD-015) and KPI targets (TBD-031).
  • Return / storage rule content after failed delivery (rule required; content not stated).

B.VTZFunctional blocksVehicle trust zone

The vehicle trust zone (device identity, boot epoch and capability revision) holds the ADS local safety authority, the edge adapter / durable journal and the media / passenger interface. Level 4 ADS retains DDT and fallback authority; remote monitoring, contextual assistance and passenger support use separate permissions and evidence paths.

BlockFunction (as stated)Inputs → outputsStore / interfaceDetail views
ADS / local safety authorityOEDR: detect and respond to road events. DDT: tactical / operational driving. Perception, localisation, motion control. DDT fallback initiates local response. MRM seeks MRC with achieved-state evidence; zero speed alone is not MRC. RA advice: the ADS can reject it after re-evaluating the scene and ODD.Guarded advice / request → accept / reject + reason; mode / ODD / motion; executing + seqOnboard; vehicle-reported operating stateD18.1, D19.2, D19.3
Edge adapter / durable journalVehicle state, ODD and diagnostic feed. Command identity, expiry and dedup. Receipt / acceptance / execution split. Safety checks remain onboard. Prioritised uplink + event buffer. No cloud override of ADS constraints.Mission / action → Receipt, accept / reject, observed result; ADS state → telemetryTelemetry / alarm and command / result channels; durable journalD14.1, D13.1
Durable journal (fence)Vehicle durably stores its accepted authority epoch and validates signed grants, expiry and command identity. Old-epoch packets reject after fence install. Reboot without recoverable authority/journal evidence blocks new action until resynchronised.InstallFence(epoch, signed grant) → PersistedFenceACK(epoch)Onboard durable journalD20.3, D14.2, D20.1

RM-01 / RM-02. Real-time remote DDT is outside this baseline. An advice response cannot widen ODD, disable collision avoidance or create a direct actuator path (RM-06).

Active authority: vehicle fence ACK gates new actions. Standby promotion: acquire higher authority epoch; require vehicle fence ACK; reconcile prior effects before action. Unsupported fence/dedup capability excludes automated centre handover for that vehicle.

B.C09Functional blocksC09 Event backbone

C09 is the event backbone: at-least-once delivery + transactional outbox + idempotent inbox + replay isolation. It distributes BookingChanged, AllocationCommitted, MissionObserved, EnergyUpdated, UsageVerified and CaseChanged from each owner's outbox to scoped subscribers.

Replay isolationReplay must use separate projections and idempotent effect handlers; RECONCILE rebuilds projections and verifies external effects by original IDs.Historical events → rebuilt projections without effectSeparate projectionsD08.2 · D24.2
QuarantineEvents that cannot be applied are quarantined; lag + poison-event alerts.Unappliable event → quarantine + alertBroker / consumersD10.3

Frame / coverageFrame / calibration / coverage checks. I09 adds coverageRef, frame/map/calibrationRev, clock bound and source lineage.frameId, mapRev, calibrationRev, coverageRef → frame / coverage verdictI09c; CoverageHealthD15.2
EligibilityAccepted / quarantine / diagnostic. Unknown ≠ clear road. Thresholds for age, association, coverage and queue size are agreed per use case.Checked envelope → accepted observation (I09) or quarantine / diagnosticI09 → C06D15.3, D16.3
Quarantine / degradeInvalid / stale / overloaded: quarantine observations, publish coverage degradation. Reject / diagnostic receipt. Coverage degraded + owner. Heartbeat expiry → coverage UNKNOWN; retain source time.Invalid, stale, unknown clock bound, bad calibration or lost coverage → diagnostic receipt; coverage degraded + ownerC06D16.1, D16.3
Overload protectionReserve queue capacity for health / critical events. Drop policy is explicit; historical replay cannot act live. Overload reports queue age and dropped observations.Queue age → explicit drop, quarantine—D16.2
Owns
No D store is stated for C10. Raw clips by purpose + access + retention contract; regional workers scale independently of ADS control.
Invariants
Vehicle I04 / roadside I09 remain separate source envelopes. No global identity assumed from local track IDs. No observation-to-command bypass; operator action follows P22 guards. Proposed monitoring path does not claim collision avoidance or perception completeness.
Downstream
C06 associates by time/space gate, preserves uncertainty and conflicting evidence, and attaches quality and provenance (VALIDATE → ASSOCIATE → PRESENT / ESCALATE).
Open
CPM mapping and radio profile require a separately verified adapter.

OPS-054A shall hold only with the current case revision, valid release authority and no blocking incident or unresolved command; F shall hold only when the passenger outcome is known, the D1 permit is current and route, energy and resource bundle are reconciled.C06, C02, C03, C05P18 11.3 RM-05T · TC-509 · D18.2
