Autonomous mobility service / System planning — Initial conceptAppendix D

Interface control and data dictionary

Provider, consumer, messages, fields, ordering, validity, authority and failure behaviour of each interface, and every named field with its entity and owner. Values the design basis leaves to a later gate are shown as such.

D.0Data types and conventions

Provisional A small type system used by the data dictionary (D.2) and the message examples (D.3). The design basis states that its examples are conceptual payloads, not complete API schemas (P10 3.2); these types are a provisional proposal, confirmed or replaced with the complete schemas at G2 (TBD-040). Field names are case-sensitive and used exactly as stated; an optional field (“?”) is omitted rather than sent as null.

TypeRepresentationRulesPlaceholder form
IdentifierUUID string, lowercase canonical 8-4-4-4-12Generated by the owning container; immutable; never reused"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
External IDopaque string assigned by an external sourceStored verbatim; compared for equality only; scoped by its source"event-abc"
Keytenant-scoped composite; JSON object of its component fieldsAlways includes tenantId (from the field or its envelope); unique within the tenant{"sourceId": …, "bootEpoch": …, "localTrackId": …}
Revisionmonotonic unsigned 64-bit integerSingle writer; increments per accepted change; compared for equality (CAS) and order. Also used for epochs and sequences, scoped as stated1
Countunsigned integer≥ 00
InstantUTC ISO 8601 with milliseconds and ZLocal time only through a separate IANA zone field"2027-01-01T08:00:00.000Z"
Intervalobject {startUTC, endUTC} of two InstantsHalf-open [startUTC, endUTC); startUTC < endUTC{"startUTC": …, "endUTC": …}
DurationISO 8601 duration in configuration; decimal seconds in payloads (suffix _s where named)≥ 0"PT30S" / 0.0
Quantitydecimal value + unit code (SI / UCUM)Unit required; no implicit unit; decimal, not binary float, in stores0.0 + "m"
EnergyQuantity in kWh, decimal≥ 0 unless a correction entry0.0
PowerQuantity in kW, decimalSign convention per interface (import positive)0.0
Ratiodecimal 0–1Closed range0.0
PositionWGS84 (lat, lon in degrees; height in m) or local Cartesian x, y, z in m per frameIdFrame always explicit (frameId / coordinateFrame + mapRev)[0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
EnumUPPER_SNAKE_CASE string (event types in PascalCase as stated)Values as stated in the document; a value outside the set is a non-retryable schema error. Where the set is not stated: TBD-040"COMMITTED"
Hashhex digest, lowercase; SHA-256 over the canonical payloadImmutable for the identity it protects"00…00"
Signaturesigned token: payload + key ID + detached signature (base64url)Verified against the issuer key and expiry before use"sig-placeholder"
ReferenceURI to an evidence item or recordResolved with access control by purpose; never embeds the content"urn:example:evidence:1"
TextUTF-8 stringNormalised (NFC); no control characters"text"
Booleantrue / falseNo null for “unknown”; unknown is an explicit statefalse
List / MapJSON array / JSON object; element type stated per fieldOrder significant only where stated (e.g. resource-set order)[] / {}

D.1Interface control

One panel per interface I01–I09c and the C09 event backbone. Provider to Owner store restate the document; “—” marks a property the document does not state. Protocols are a G2 decision (P08 1.2); where the document does not state one, the Transport row gives a provisional choice, confirmed at G2 (TBD-003). Error model, Versioning, Timeouts and retries, Authentication and tenant isolation and Observability are provisional; every timing value is held in Appendix F and referenced by parameter name.

InterfaceI01 Channel intake (municipal / partner channels → C01)
Provider
C01 API gateway + adapters [application]
Consumer
Municipal / partner channels: resident app / phone / corporate fleet; Outlook, Google, Tabelog, Ikyu, Hot Pepper. C01 passes I01 / confirmed fields to the C02 coordinator, which normalises intent.
Transport
HTTPS (P08 1.1) Provisional; confirmed at G2(TBD-003): JSON payloads over TLS; channel connectors authenticate with scoped, consent-bound tokens; partner adapters use mutually authenticated TLS.
Operations / messages
Share plan / time and preferences with consent; need / consent; I01 / confirmed fields → normalise intent (source + conditionsRev). Calendar changes produce proposed intent, never auto-booking by default.
Request fields
PlanReference: tenantId, planRefId, provider, accountRef, sourceEventId, instanceId, sourceRevision, consentId, purpose, expiresAt, startUTC, endUTC, IANA zone.
Result / outcomes
Normalised intent at C02; PlanReference 0..1 : N Booking (FK planRefId optional for app input).
Idempotency and ordering
Unique within tenant: provider / account / event / instance. Source cursor at C01. Capture intent, needs, consent and idempotent request (MVP).
Validity and time
Consent purpose, expiry and withdrawal remain explicit; consent expiresAt; startUTC, endUTC with IANA zone.
Security and authority
Identity, object / tenant access, consent, schema and source cursor at C01. Trust boundary: authenticated domain commands / scoped event subscriptions. Keys include tenant scope.
Failure behaviour
Connector failure may leave local intake available; confirmation still requires all mandatory dependencies. Sync deletion / resync must not erase D1 bookings.
Error model
Explicit: normalised intent accepted at C02; calendar change → proposed intent (no auto-booking); consent expired / withdrawn or purpose mismatch → rejected with reason; duplicate provider / account / event / instance → existing PlanReference returned. Provisional Transport classes: retryable — timeout, connection loss, throttling, temporary unavailability: retry with the same identity / idempotency key; non-retryable — schema or validation error, unknown schema MAJOR, authentication or authorisation failure, tenant mismatch, revision conflict: no retry; the caller refreshes or escalates. Connector failure leaves local intake available; resync replays from the source cursor.
Versioning
Provisional schemaVersion MAJOR.MINOR on every request, result and envelope (carried as a header where the payload does not state it). MINOR: additive optional fields, consumers ignore unknown fields. MAJOR: breaking change, served in parallel until consumers migrate (PRM-026 schema deprecation window (Appendix F)); an unknown MAJOR is rejected as non-retryable.
Timeouts and retries
Provisional PRM-014 synchronous call timeout; PRM-049 retry attempts and back-off; PRM-040 connector resync interval (Appendix F). No value is restated here.
Authentication and tenant isolation
Provisional Caller authenticated at C01 (user token or partner client credential); scope limited to intake for the consenting subject and purpose; tenantId of the token must equal the payload tenantId; cross-tenant references rejected; consentId checked on every call.
Observability
Provisional correlationId created at C01 for each intake and propagated to C02 and onwards; audit record per intake and consent decision at C01 (source, cursor, consentId, outcome); metrics: intake rate, rejection reason, connector lag.
Owner store
PlanReference / C01 (no D-store stated); resulting bookings in D1 (C02).
Specified in
P08 1.1 · P08 1.2 · P10 3.1 · P23 16.1 · D08.1 · D02.1 · D23.2 · Appendix B C01
InterfaceI02 Booking commit / amend / cancel (consoles → C01 → C02)
Provider
C02 Booking / activities (via C01)
Consumer
Operator / provider consoles (transport / activities / parking lessors); client / rider messages to C02 in P11 4.1.
Transport
HTTPS (P08 1.1) Provisional; confirmed at G2(TBD-003): JSON payloads; console clients over TLS with operator / user tokens.
Operations / messages
Commit / amend / cancel. P11 4.1: 01 Quote/amend(reqId); 09 Offer + hold expiry; 10 Terms + expiresAt; 11 Accept(termsRev); 21 Outcome(intent); 22 Cancel(intent,rev); 24 Persisted result; 25 Customer outcome; 26 Permit / keep blocked.
Request fields
reqId; termsRev; intent, rev. Booking: tenantId, bookingId, planRefId, bookingRev, termsRev, state, riderRef, pickupWindow, destination, currentBundleId, intentId.
Result / outcomes
Booking states DRAFT → QUOTED (expiresAt) → PENDING (hold) → CONFIRMED (commit) → IN_SERVICE → COMPLETED / CANCELLED (reason + release); timeout / lost acknowledgement → UNKNOWN. Only CONFIRMED + no pending cancel can issue a current dispatch permit.
Idempotency and ordering
Single writer + transactional outbox. CAS: expectedBookingRev; D1 finalise by CAS. D1 owns bookingRev. Cancel and permit issuance serialize in D1. Never duplicate a side effect.
Validity and time
Quote expiresAt; guard: expired / changed input rejects. Revision conflict → refresh terms; stale evidence → block offer or action with reason.
Security and authority
C01 identity, object / tenant access, consent and schema checks; trust boundary: authenticated domain commands.
Failure behaviour
Interrupt at any phase: D1 records cancelRequested against intent. Cancellation after permit issuance becomes cancel / replan of an in-flight mission, not a guarantee of zero movement. Unknown → query and reconcile.
Error model
Explicit: Booking states DRAFT / QUOTED / PENDING / CONFIRMED / IN_SERVICE / COMPLETED / CANCELLED / UNKNOWN; revision conflict → refresh terms; expired / changed input → rejected; stale evidence → offer or action blocked with reason. Provisional Transport classes: retryable — timeout, connection loss, throttling, temporary unavailability: retry with the same identity / idempotency key; non-retryable — schema or validation error, unknown schema MAJOR, authentication or authorisation failure, tenant mismatch, revision conflict: no retry; the caller refreshes or escalates. Timeout / lost acknowledgement → UNKNOWN; query by reqId / intentId and reconcile.
Versioning
Provisional schemaVersion MAJOR.MINOR on every request, result and envelope (carried as a header where the payload does not state it). MINOR: additive optional fields, consumers ignore unknown fields. MAJOR: breaking change, served in parallel until consumers migrate (PRM-026 schema deprecation window (Appendix F)); an unknown MAJOR is rejected as non-retryable.
Timeouts and retries
Provisional PRM-014 synchronous call timeout; PRM-049 retry attempts and back-off; PRM-077 quote validity (expiresAt); PRM-075 hold expiry (Appendix F). No value is restated here.
Authentication and tenant isolation
Provisional Operator / provider console sessions authenticated at C01; authorisation scope per operation (quote, commit, amend, cancel) and per object; tenantId of the token must equal the booking tenant; riders act only on their own bookings.
Observability
Provisional correlationId from the originating intent carried on every saga step and C09 event; audit record per state transition in D1 (bookingRev, intentId, actor, outcome); metrics: saga duration, UNKNOWN count, cancel-after-permit count.
Owner store
D1 (C02): bookingRev, terms, intent, saga; dispatch permit.
Specified in
P08 1.1 · P11 4.1 · P04 · P02 · D04.1 · D04.2 · D11.1 · D11.3 · Appendix B C02
InterfaceI03 Joint reservation (C02 → C03)
Provider
C03 Joint reservation authority
Consumer
C02 Booking / activities (coordinator)
Transport
Provisional; confirmed at G2(P08 1.2, TBD-003): HTTPS with JSON over mutually authenticated TLS (synchronous command / query API C02 → C03); committed outcomes are also published through the C09 outbox.
Operations / messages
Quote / hold / atomic replacement; I03 CommitBundle / command. P11 4.1: 02 Plan(terms,windows); 07 Hold(snapshot) → 08 holdId / expiresAt; 13 PromoteHold(intent) → 14 PENDING / reject; 18 CommitSwap(intent) → 19 Durable outcome; 20 Release old / undo new as required.
Request fields
CommitBundle: tenantId, intentId, bookingId, expectedBookingRev, newBundleId, oldBundleId, expectedResourceRevs, acceptedTermsRev, capabilityRev, idempotencyKey.
Result / outcomes
intentId, state (COMMITTED), bundleId, bundleRev, intentIdForD1, committedAt, externalReleaseJobs. Other explicit outcomes HELD / REJECTED / PENDING with reasonCode + retryability. Infeasible: binding reason (+ alternative).
Idempotency and ordering
Same key + different payload: reject IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Unique: tenant / intent / key. expectedResourceRevs maps to the ordered resource set; resource revision set + ordered locks; one D2 transaction per bundle resource set; D2 local commit + outbox atomically.
Validity and time
HELD bundle expires (expiresAt); expiry releases unused hold. PENDING does not expire on quote TTL. Policy version + snapshot time; resource snapshot and energy capability are versioned inputs, not one shared revision.
Security and authority
Keys / FKs include tenant scope; validate references within that scope. Ranking never relaxes a hard constraint.
Failure behaviour
Unknown ≠ rejection. Outcome unknown → RECONCILING (query original intent). Replacement holds new capacity before retiring old; swap applies only to unstarted allocations; started / unknown missions retain occupancy until physical clearance. Atomic guarantees cover D2 only.
Error model
Explicit: COMMITTED / HELD / REJECTED / PENDING with reasonCode + retryability; IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (same key, different payload); infeasible → binding reason (+ alternative). Unknown ≠ rejection. Provisional Transport classes: retryable — timeout, connection loss, throttling, temporary unavailability: retry with the same identity / idempotency key; non-retryable — schema or validation error, unknown schema MAJOR, authentication or authorisation failure, tenant mismatch, revision conflict: no retry; the caller refreshes or escalates. Outcome unknown → RECONCILING; query the original intentId / idempotencyKey.
Versioning
Provisional schemaVersion MAJOR.MINOR on every request, result and envelope (carried as a header where the payload does not state it). MINOR: additive optional fields, consumers ignore unknown fields. MAJOR: breaking change, served in parallel until consumers migrate (PRM-026 schema deprecation window (Appendix F)); an unknown MAJOR is rejected as non-retryable. Payload fields are conceptual until the complete schema (TBD-040).
Timeouts and retries
Provisional PRM-014 synchronous call timeout; PRM-049 retry attempts and back-off; PRM-075 hold expiry; PRM-078 reconciliation query interval (Appendix F). No value is restated here.
Authentication and tenant isolation
Provisional Service identity of C02 by mutual TLS; scoped token for reservation operations (quote, hold, commit, release); tenantId of the token must equal the payload tenantId; every FK (bookingId, bundleIds, resource IDs) validated within that tenant.
Observability
Provisional correlationId propagated from the D1 intent to D2 and the AllocationCommitted event; audit record per intent outcome in D2 (intentId, policyVersion, snapshot, result, reasonCode); metrics: commit latency, conflict rate, RECONCILING count.
Owner store
D2 (C03): route / segment capacity and bundles.
Specified in
P09 2.1–2.3 · P10 3.1–3.2 · P11 4.1 · D09.1 · D09.2 · D09.3 · D10.2 · D11.2 · Appendix B I03 · Appendix B C03
InterfaceI04 Mission / receipt / execution (C03 → C04 ↔ vehicle edge)
Provider
C04 Fleet / vehicle adapter
Consumer
Vehicle / AD (vehicle trust zone edge adapter); C06 and C10 consume I04 pose / status / time / quality as evidence.
Transport
Provisional; confirmed at G2(P08 1.2, TBD-003): signed message envelopes over authenticated IP (mutually authenticated TLS per vehicle) between C04 and the vehicle edge adapter, one priority class per channel. Stated: Channels: telemetry / alarm; command / result; evidence / media (P14 7.1).
Operations / messages
Mission / receipt / execution. P13 6.1: 01 Mission(id,validTo); 02 Persist / send cmd; 03 Receipt(cmdId); 04 Accept / reject; 07 Query(cmdId); 08 Execution + seq. P20 13.1: 01 Status(boot,seq); 11 InstallFence(epoch, signed grant); 12 PersistedFenceACK(epoch); 15 Scoped cancel/query under new epoch; 21 New mission(id,epoch,expiry).
Request fields
Mission / Command: tenantId, commandId, bundleId, vehicleId, missionRev, routeRef, validUntil, payloadHash. RemoteActionRequest fields (P22 15.2).
Result / outcomes
Delivery: PERSISTED → SENT → RECEIVED. Execution: ACCEPTED → EXECUTING → COMPLETED / ABORTED. deliveryState, executionState, statusSeq, observedAt, receivedAt. CommandAuditEvent: RECEIVED / ACCEPTED / REJECTED / EXECUTING / COMPLETED / ABORTED / EXPIRED + reason.
Idempotency and ordering
Same commandId: one immutable payloadHash; same ID with changed payload is rejected. Command identity, expiry and dedup at the edge adapter. Query original IDs after lost responses; no automatic resend with a new ID. Verify observedAt / seq / clock quality; old or repeated state cannot prove recovery.
Validity and time
validUntil / validTo. Expiry blocks a new command but never stops status reconciliation. Freshness per P22 15.3 (F_i set by Platform).
Security and authority
C04 obtains the current D1 permit before releasing a mission. Device identity, boot epoch and capability revision; authority fence (vehicle durably stores accepted authority epoch, validates signed grants, expiry and command identity). No cloud override of ADS constraints.
Failure behaviour
Acceptance unknown / fault / stale telemetry → UNKNOWN; block reuse; query; OpenCase. Never default missing state to healthy. Link loss marks remote state UNKNOWN. No fence ACK means no new action. Reboot without recoverable authority / journal evidence blocks new action until resynchronised.
Error model
Explicit: Accept / reject + reason; CommandAuditEvent RECEIVED / ACCEPTED / REJECTED / EXECUTING / COMPLETED / ABORTED / EXPIRED; same commandId with changed payload → rejected; no fence ACK → no new action. Provisional Transport classes: retryable — timeout, connection loss, throttling, temporary unavailability: retry with the same identity / idempotency key; non-retryable — schema or validation error, unknown schema MAJOR, authentication or authorisation failure, tenant mismatch, revision conflict: no retry; the caller refreshes or escalates. Acceptance unknown / stale telemetry → UNKNOWN; query the original commandId within the query budget, then OpenCase; no automatic resend with a new ID.
Versioning
Provisional schemaVersion MAJOR.MINOR on every request, result and envelope (carried as a header where the payload does not state it). MINOR: additive optional fields, consumers ignore unknown fields. MAJOR: breaking change, served in parallel until consumers migrate (PRM-026 schema deprecation window (Appendix F)); an unknown MAJOR is rejected as non-retryable. Vehicle and edge adapter advertise supported MAJOR versions with capability revision; a command is sent only in a version the vehicle supports.
Timeouts and retries
Provisional PRM-013 receipt acknowledgement timeout; PRM-052 command validity (validUntil); PRM-053 unresolved-command query budget; PRM-050 telemetry heartbeat interval and expiry; PRM-029 per-signal freshness limit F_i; PRM-049 retry attempts and back-off (Appendix F). No value is restated here.
Authentication and tenant isolation
Provisional Per-vehicle device identity (certificate) and boot epoch; envelopes signed by C04 and verified at the edge adapter; authority fence by epoch and signed grant; C04 releases a mission only with the current D1 permit; vehicle scope limited to its own commands and tenant.
Observability
Provisional correlationId carried from booking / case to every command and CommandAuditEvent; audit journal in D3 (commandId, payloadHash, states, observedAt, receivedAt, clock bound); metrics: receipt latency, UNKNOWN count, sequence gaps, link RTT.
Owner store
D3 (C04): command and status journal.

Unknown stays blocked; query the same planId until resolved or escalated.

Provider
C06 + C08 Operations (cases / policy)
Consumer
Remote operator / RA operator; C04 (guarded advice / request to the vehicle)
Transport
Provisional; confirmed at G2(P08 1.2, TBD-003): HTTPS with JSON over mutually authenticated TLS between consoles and C06 / C08; the guarded request to the vehicle travels on the I04 command / result channel as a signed envelope.
Operations / messages
P13 6.1: 10 OpenCase(command, last observation, severity, deadline); 11 Assign(lease,dueAt); 12 ACK(caseRev); 13 Escalate / new lease; 14 Action + evidence; 15 Authorise scoped action; 24 Release decision. P19: 10 Advice(type,scope); 11 GuardedAdvice(ref). P16 9.1: 14 I07 guarded advice / request.
Request fields
RemoteActionRequest: caseId?, expectedCaseRev?, actionType (CONTEXT_ADVICE / STOP_REQUEST / MISSION_CHANGE_REQUEST / STATUS_QUERY), parameters, operatorId, qualificationRef, authorityEpoch, issuedAt, expiresAt, reasonCode, evidenceRefs[], approvalRef?. Action record: vehicle + mission + case revision + lease epoch + reason + advice type + expiry + expected outcome.
Result / outcomes
Case: OPEN → ASSIGNED → ACK → ACTIVE → RESOLVED → CLOSED; material new evidence reopens the case. Receive / accept / reject + reason.
Idempotency and ordering
caseRev guard; command identity per P22 15.2 (same ID with changed payload is rejected).
Validity and time
Lease, dueAt, expiry. Motion-enabling advice requires current contextual evidence; read-only queries and emergency escalation remain available with stale data.
Security and authority
I07 permissions differ by case type. Guard for motion-enabling action: role, caseRev, authority fence, current evidence and expected state. Qualified seat + single action lease. No AI bypass of command guards; AI cannot independently authorise ADS movement. Passenger support cannot override door interlocks or authorise motion.
Failure behaviour
Lease expired / missing ACK / urgent deadline → reject stale action and assign backup owner. Rejected / unknown → keep case open and query state or initiate an approved fallback. Closing a case never changes ADS mode or automatically clears an operational hold.
Error model
Explicit: receive / accept / reject + reason; stale action (lease expired, caseRev mismatch, missing ACK) rejected and backup owner assigned; rejected / unknown keeps the case open. Provisional Transport classes: retryable — timeout, connection loss, throttling, temporary unavailability: retry with the same identity / idempotency key; non-retryable — schema or validation error, unknown schema MAJOR, authentication or authorisation failure, tenant mismatch, revision conflict: no retry; the caller refreshes or escalates. Vehicle outcome unknown → STATUS_QUERY on the original commandId; approved fallback if unresolved.
Versioning
Provisional schemaVersion MAJOR.MINOR on every request, result and envelope (carried as a header where the payload does not state it). MINOR: additive optional fields, consumers ignore unknown fields. MAJOR: breaking change, served in parallel until consumers migrate (PRM-026 schema deprecation window (Appendix F)); an unknown MAJOR is rejected as non-retryable. Action parameters follow the versioned action schema per actionType (P22 15.2).
Timeouts and retries
Provisional PRM-056 case ACK deadline per response class; PRM-061 action lease duration; PRM-051 remote action request expiry; PRM-014 synchronous call timeout (Appendix F). No value is restated here.
Authentication and tenant isolation
Provisional Operator authentication with role and current qualification; permissions per case type; single action lease per case; authority epoch on every request; AI tools hold read / propose scopes only and cannot authorise movement.
Observability
Provisional correlationId of the case carried to every RemoteActionRequest and CommandAuditEvent; audit record per case transition and action in D5 / D7 (operatorId, caseRev, lease epoch, reasonCode, evidenceRefs); metrics: time to ACK, lease expiries, escalations.

D5 (C06): vehicle cases / owner leases; D7 (C06 + C08): service cases / AI tool traces.

Every named field and key in the document’s entities, payloads and messages, sorted alphabetically. Meaning, Owner and Source restate the document. Type, Format / unit and Constraints are provisional and use the types of D.0; a constraint restates the document where it states one. D.3Message examples

Provisional One illustrative JSON message per key interface, using only field names stated in the document (D.2) and the types of D.0. Identifiers, revisions, instants and quantities are placeholders (identifiers shown as readable strings such as “booking-123” in place of UUIDs); numeric quantities are neutral (0 / 0.0 / 1) and carry no planning meaning. Field order is not significant. Complete schemas: TBD-040.

I03 CommitBundle — request (C02 → C03)

Illustrative example (values are placeholders). Interface: I03. expectedResourceRevs keys are resource IDs in resource-set order. Non-committed outcomes add reasonCode and retryability.

{
  "tenantId": "tenant-a",
  "intentId": "intent-123",
  "bookingId": "booking-123",
  "expectedBookingRev": 1,
  "newBundleId": "bundle-new-123",
  "oldBundleId": "bundle-old-123",
  "expectedResourceRevs": {
    "resource-1": 1,
    "resource-2": 1
  },
  "acceptedTermsRev": 1,
  "capabilityRev": 1,
  "idempotencyKey": "key-123"
}

I03 CommitBundle — result (C03 → C02)

Illustrative example (values are placeholders). Interface: I03. Other explicit outcomes: HELD / REJECTED / PENDING with reasonCode + retryability.

{
  "intentId": "intent-123",
  "state": "COMMITTED",
  "bundleId": "bundle-new-123",
  "bundleRev": 1,
  "intentIdForD1": "intent-123",
  "committedAt": "2027-01-01T08:00:00.000Z",
  "externalReleaseJobs": ["job-1"]
}

C09 event envelope

Illustrative example (values are placeholders). Interface: C09. The event payload is not stated in the document and is not shown.

{
  "eventId": "event-123",
  "type": "AllocationCommitted",
  "schemaVersion": "1.0",
  "tenantId": "tenant-a",
  "aggregateId": "bundle-new-123",
  "aggregateRevision": 1,
  "occurredAt": "2027-01-01T08:00:00.000Z",
  "receivedAt": "2027-01-01T08:00:00.000Z",
  "correlationId": "intent-123"
}

Illustrative example (values are placeholders). Interface: I05. powerIntervals[] elements use the Interval form with quantity + unit (Power, kW); plan revision ACK ≠ delivered energy.

{

  "planId": "plan-123",
  "planRev": 1,
  "bundleId": "bundle-new-123",
  "siteId": "site-a",
  "capabilityRev": 1,
  "validUntil": "2027-01-01T09:00:00.000Z",

    {
      "startUTC": "2027-01-01T08:00:00.000Z",

      "unit": "kW"
    }

Illustrative example (values are placeholders). Interface: I08. Corrections are new entries (correctionOf), never an overwrite.

{

    "startUTC": "2027-01-01T08:00:00.000Z",

E.2Assumptions and constraints

IDAssumption or constraintSource
ASM-001Proposed concept; field validation and implementation pending.P02 · P07
ASM-002Separately prepared models, not copied from Honda internal documents.P01
ASM-003Desk review is complete; implementation and validation remain pending. Diagrams define candidate boundaries and contracts.P08
ASM-004Desk-reviewed architecture proposal; implementation, performance and safety validation remain pending. Public references support terminology and patterns, not this system’s certification.P22 15.4
ASM-005Examples are conceptual payloads, not complete API schemas.P10 3.2
ASM-006The primary service integrates booking, dispatch and energy; equipment / JV / eVTOL options attach through capability interfaces.P08 1.2
ASM-007Atomic guarantees cover D2 only; no distributed atomic commit is assumed. External EMS effects use a reconciled saga.P10 3.2 · P11
ASM-008Provider and transport reservations are not one distributed transaction.P23 16.1
ASM-009Keys / FKs include tenant scope; references are validated within that scope.P10 3.2
ASM-010Level 4 ADS retains DDT and fallback authority. Vehicle / ADS owns driving and fallback.P14 · P13
ASM-011Real-time remote DDT is outside this baseline; no remote steering / throttle baseline.P14 7.2 · P22 15.1
ASM-012RA supplies contextual advice that the ADS can reject after re-evaluating the scene and ODD.P14 7.2
ASM-013Vehicle-specific link-loss and fallback behaviour remains local and does not depend on a remote reply.P14 7.2
ASM-014Local ADS safety decisions remain independent of the service-mode model.P27 20.1
ASM-015AI may draft or summarise within task scope; it cannot independently authorise ADS movement. No AI bypass of command guards.P22 15.4 · P08 1.1
ASM-016Plant protection remains local.P08 1.1
ASM-017I05 has electrical scope; fuel / H2 requires a separate capability.P12 5.1
ASM-018All P are net kW at one AC boundary; conversion losses belong in storage-energy updates, not twice. Electrical: kW, hours, kWh; fuel: kg, kg/min, minutes.P12 5.1 · P26 19.2
ASM-019Availability kW and delivered kWh remain distinct; an energy-plan ACK does not prove delivered energy.P12 · P26 19.2
ASM-020Proposed I09 feeds monitoring and operational review, not direct actuation. The monitoring path does not claim collision avoidance or perception completeness.P15
ASM-021No assumption of integrated sensing; no global identity assumed from local track IDs.P15 8.1–8.2
ASM-022Alarm priorities are operational response classes, not ASIL classifications.P17
ASM-023UNKNOWN is a knowledge state, not a vehicle state; it belongs to the observer, not the ADS.P13 · P22 15.2
ASM-024D_remote is an operational budget; it is not used to justify onboard safety persistence.P22 15.3
ASM-025A/m is a mean-load screen, not a service-level guarantee.P21 14.3 · P27 20.3
ASM-026Calendar changes produce proposed intent, never auto-booking by default. No forced consent or automatic schedule change.P23 · P04
ASM-027Gates are evidence checkpoints, not fixed calendar phases; schedule alone never passes a gate.P07
ASM-028Service feasibility and customer choice remain binding even when aggregate contribution improves.P07
ASM-029Simulation outputs do not establish field impact or guarantee service-level attainment; tests are proposed only.P06
ASM-030The P24 cases are planned tests, not passed results.P24
ASM-031Finite synthetic tests establish a tested envelope only; pilot evidence determines field readiness. A configuration qualifies only within its tested demand, geography and operating conditions.P28
ASM-032Operational feasibility does not by itself establish project profitability or safety certification.P28 21.3
ASM-033Regional workers scale independently of ADS control.P15 8.3
ASM-034Terminology baseline: SAE J3016_202609 (ODD, DDT, OEDR, DDT fallback).P03 MVP control

Autonomous mobility service / System planning — Initial conceptAppendix F

Provisional parameters

Values the design basis leaves open, filled with provisional values for the pilot. Each has a unit, an engineering rationale, the gate or owner that confirms or replaces it, and the open item it closes. Requirements, interfaces and test cases reference these parameters by ID.

F.1Platform, recovery and interfaces

Provisional Where the design basis leaves a technical or operational value open, this appendix proposes a pilot value with its unit, a one-line engineering rationale and the gate or owner that confirms or replaces it; organisational choices carry a provisional decision text instead of a number. Every value here is provisional until that gate or owner confirms it, and requirements, interfaces and tests reference the PRM ID rather than restating the value.

Autonomous mobility service / System planning — Initial conceptAppendix G

Safety and security analysis

Hazards of remote operation and platform behaviour, failure modes and effects of the platform containers and interfaces, and the threat model of each interface, with mitigations traced to requirements and residual risks. Vehicle-internal functional safety remains with the ADS owner.

G.1Method and scope

This appendix analyses the platform and remote-operation side of the service: the containers C01–C10, the interfaces I01–I09c, the C09 event backbone, the stores D1–D7 and the operator workspace. Vehicle-internal functional safety (DDT, DDT fallback, MRM, perception, motion control and their safety case) stays with the ADS owner and is not analysed here; where a platform mitigation relies on vehicle behaviour, the dependency is stated as a requirement allocated to the vehicle trust zone (VTZ), for evidence from the ADS owner. Organisational procedures (staffing, training, field response, privacy governance) appear as mitigations allocated to Org; their adequacy is shown by operational readiness evidence at the gates, not by this analysis.

Approach

  • HazardsIdentified per function and per interface from the chapters P08–P30: what goes wrong, in which operating situation, with which effect on passengers, public and service (G.2).
  • FMEAOne or more failure modes per container, interface and store, rated for severity, likelihood and detectability (G.3).
  • ThreatsSTRIDE per interface and trust boundary (G.4).
  • ClosureEvery mitigation references a requirement of Appendix C or a proposed SAF requirement (G.6); coverage and residual risks in G.5.

Boundaries

  • ADS ownerOnboard safety checks, link-loss / fallback behaviour, action capability, fence and journal persistence (OPS-017, OPS-019, TBD-009).
  • Out of baselineReal-time remote DDT (OPS-018, TBD-024).
  • Alarm classesP0–P3 are operational response classes, not ASIL classifications (OPS-044).
  • ValuesDeadlines and limits are named Appendix F parameters; ratings are revisited with G3 evidence (TBD-052).

Rating scales

RankSeverity (S)Likelihood (L), per pilot operating yearDetectability (D), FMEA only
4Catastrophic — could contribute to death or serious injury of a passenger or member of the public, or to a vehicle acting under authority that is not current.Frequent — expected to occur repeatedly.Undetectable — no specified detection; found only after harm or by chance.
3Critical — could contribute to minor injury, a passenger left without support, a serious privacy or regulatory breach, or loss of incident evidence.Probable — expected to occur at least once.Late — found by manual review, audit or reconciliation after the effect.
2Marginal — disruption of several journeys or shipments, a wrong commitment or a financial error; no injury.Occasional — could occur; not expected.Prompt — found automatically at or just after the effect (alarm, reconciliation).
1Negligible — inconvenience to one journey, recovered without passenger impact.Remote — only after several independent failures.Prevented — a guard rejects the fault before it has an effect.

Risk matrix (S × L)

Likelihood \ SeverityS1 NegligibleS2 MarginalS3 CriticalS4 Catastrophic
L4 FrequentMediumHighUnacceptableUnacceptable
L3 ProbableLowMediumHighUnacceptable
L2 OccasionalLowMediumMediumHigh
L1 RemoteLowLowMediumMedium
  • UnacceptableNot permitted in operation; the design shall change before the gate.
  • HighPermitted only with a recorded decision by the accountable owner at the gate, with evidence and a scope restriction.
  • MediumPermitted with the listed mitigations verified and monitored in operation.
  • LowPermitted; reviewed with the hazard log.

FMEA priority: RPN = S × L × D (1–64). Action when RPN ≥ 24 or S4 with D ≥ 3; Review when RPN is 12–23; otherwise Accept. Residual ratings credit only mitigations that are specified as requirements and verified by their stated method. Likelihood is qualitative at Initial-Concept level and is revised with pilot evidence.

SAF-005The C08 service identity shall hold no permission for any motion-enabling or STOP_REQUEST action on I07 or I04; an attempted call shall be rejected at the authorisation layer and recorded as a security event.C06, C08Appendix G HZ‑014, TH‑013T · TC-308 · TC-655 · HZ‑014

SAF-007Keys that sign authority grants and remote actions shall be held in a protected key store separate from application hosts, shall be rotated per the key-rotation parameter, and shall be revocable; a revoked key shall be rejected by the vehicle edge through a higher authority epoch.C06, VTZ, OrgAppendix G HZ‑002, TH‑005, TH‑023T · TC-657 · HZ‑002

SAF-010Authentication failures, authorisation denials, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT results, fence rejections, signature failures and cross-tenant reference rejections shall be recorded as security events and monitored with alerting to a named security owner.C01, C03, C04, C06, C10, OrgAppendix G HZ‑015, TH‑001, TH‑021T · TC-660 · HZ‑015

Autonomous mobility service / System planning — Initial conceptAppendix H

Verification specification

Test cases with preconditions, procedure, pass criteria and the requirements each one verifies, and the verification coverage of the requirement set.

Values in pass criteria and preconditions are referenced by their Appendix F parameter ID (all provisional until confirmed at the named gate). Fault-injection cases T-R01 to T-R08 of P24 17.1 are specified as TC-301 to TC-308 and are cited here where a case reuses them.

H.1Service and product

Test cases for the product and service requirements (SVC): consent, value mechanisms, traceability, the booking state model, measurement, experiments and the release gates. Organisational obligations are verified by inspection checklists so that they stay traceable.

TestTC-001 · Consent purpose, expiry and withdrawal enforcement
Objective
Show that every consented signal is used only within its recorded purpose and expiry, that withdrawal takes effect, and that optional data stays optional.
Verifies
SVC-001 · SVC-004 · SVC-019 · HZ-016 · TH-011
Level
Integration
Preconditions
C01 and C02 deployed with the consent schema of D02.3; a test tenant with three users: one with all optional signals consented, one with only the mandatory booking data, one whose consent expires during the test. Encoding per PRM-025; consent ownership per PRM-138.
Stimulus and steps
  1. Submit intended arrival, booking lead time and free-time signals through I01 for each user, with purpose and expiresAt set.
  2. Request an offer that would use each signal; repeat for the user without optional consent.
  3. Advance the test clock past the expiry of the third user's consent and request a new offer.
  4. Withdraw one optional signal through the app withdrawal path and request a new offer.
  5. Attempt to read the withdrawn signal through an I06 provider payload and through an operator console role without purpose.
Pass criteria
Each stored signal carries purpose, expiresAt and a withdrawal path (zero records without them). No decision input references an expired or withdrawn signal (zero occurrences in the C02 decision trace). Booking without optional consent completes with the same mandatory steps; no screen blocks progress on optional consent. No provider or console read returns a signal outside its purpose.
Evidence recorded
Consent records (consentId, purpose, expiresAt, withdrawnAt); C02 decision trace with input list; I06 payload capture; access audit.
Environment
SIL with C01 / C02 and a test app client.
Related figures
D02.3 · D04.1 · I01 · I06
TestTC-002 · Plan-stage evidence: consent scope, expiry and received time
Objective
Show that C02 records, at the Plan stage, the consent scope, consent expiry and received time of each booking signal, and the offer, accepted terms, original and revised times, route stops and segment occupancy.
Verifies
SVC-002 · SVC-017 · SVC-019
Level
Integration
Preconditions
C02 with D1 empty for the test tenant; time source within PRM-043; one on-demand request and one advance booking scripted.
Stimulus and steps
  1. Submit both requests; accept the on-demand offer; request a revision of the advance booking and accept it.
  2. Read the D1 stage evidence and the outbox events for both bookings.
  3. Compare receivedAt with the injected arrival time at C01.
Pass criteria
For every signal: consent scope, expiresAt and receivedAt present (100 %). receivedAt differs from the injected arrival by no more than the clock bound of PRM-041 plus processing time. Offers, accepted terms, original and revised times, route stops and segment occupancy are present for both bookings; the original time survives the revision.
Evidence recorded
D1 stage-evidence export; BookingChanged events; C01 ingress log.
Environment
SIL.
Related figures
D02.1 · D02.3
TestTC-003 · No future information in positioning and offer decisions
Objective
Show by replay that positioning and offer decisions use only information received before decision time.
Verifies
SVC-003
Level
Analysis
Preconditions
A recorded demand trace with receivedAt per signal; simulation engine version fixed; PRM-098 replications.
Stimulus and steps
  1. Replay the trace and log, for every decision, the receivedAt of each input used.
  2. Re-run with all inputs whose receivedAt is later than each decision removed (as-of cut).
  3. Compare decisions of both runs.
Pass criteria
Zero inputs with receivedAt later than decision time in any decision log. Decisions of the as-of run are identical to the original run for every replication.
Evidence recorded
Decision logs with input receipt times; run manifest (seed, engine version).
Environment
Simulation.
Related figures
D06.1 · D06.3
TestTC-004 · Explicit acceptance before any schedule change
Objective
Show that a suggestion takes effect only after explicit acceptance, that the original plan stays visible and can be retained, and that timing, total price and cancellation terms are confirmed before acceptance.
Verifies
SVC-005 · SVC-008 · SVC-035 · SVC-036
Level
System
Preconditions
A CONFIRMED booking with a flexible window; C02 configured to propose a time shift (mechanism 03) and an activity offer (mechanism 02); quote validity per PRM-077.
Stimulus and steps
  1. Trigger the time-shift suggestion and do nothing until the quote expires.
  2. Trigger it again and decline it.
  3. Trigger it again, inspect the offer screen, then accept it.
  4. Propose a shift outside the flexible window.
Pass criteria
No change to booking times after steps 1 and 2 (D1 bookingRev unchanged). On step 2 the original plan is still offered and remains CONFIRMED. On step 3 the screen shows timing, total price and cancellation terms before the accept control is enabled; the change is applied only after the accept event. No offer is generated in step 4.
Evidence recorded
Screen recordings; D1 revision history; offer and acceptance events with acceptedTermsRev.
Environment
SIL with the user app.
Related figures
D04.1 · D04.2
TestTC-005 · Activity offer only when it fits free time and spare capacity
Objective
Show that mechanism 02 offers an activity and trip only when the activity fits the free-time interval and spare capacity, and that every offer returns feasible options with binding reasons and an expiry.

SVC-007 · SVC-024
Level
Integration
Preconditions
Activity provider test double on I06 with a slot calendar; C03 with a fleet state of known spare capacity; holds per PRM-075 and PRM-076.
Stimulus and steps
  1. Request offers for free-time intervals that (a) fit, (b) are shorter than the activity plus trip, (c) fit but no vehicle capacity exists.
  2. Inspect the returned options and reasons.
Pass criteria
Case (a): at least one option, each with expiresAt per PRM-077. Cases (b) and (c): no activity option; the response names the binding reason (time window or capacity). No hold remains after an infeasible response.

Offer responses; C03 feasibility log; hold table.

H.5Fault injection (T-R01–T-R08)

The eight planned fault-injection cases of P24 17.1 as executable test cases, with two companion cases for the orthogonal-state cross-products and the run record. Common pass rule: PRM-103 (≥ 20 repetitions per injected fault; the invariant holds in 100 % of repetitions; zero duplicate effects; zero motion-enabling acceptance on stale, future-dated or unknown-clock data). Remote assistance (CONTEXT_ADVICE) cases run before the gate that admits it (PRM-134).

TestTC-301 · T-R01 Delay, reorder, clock jump, reboot
Objective
Show that stale, reordered, future-dated or unknown-clock data blocks every motion-enabling action while authenticated status queries stay usable (RM-03–04, RM-12).
Verifies
OPS-003, OPS-021, OPS-032, OPS-043, OPS-048, OPS-075, OPS-079, OPS-080, OPS-081, OPS-082, OPS-088, OPS-093, SAF-001; hazards / threats: HZ-001, HZ-018, TH-024 · fault-injection case P24 17.1 T-R01
Level
fault injection
Preconditions
Vehicle simulator in DDT_ACTIVE on a mission; I04 telemetry at the sampling periods of PRM-047; freshness limits F_i per PRM-029–PRM-034; clock bounds per PRM-041, PRM-043–PRM-046; heartbeat per PRM-050; one open P2 case with a valid lease (PRM-061).
Stimulus and steps
  1. Delay the motion / localisation family until ageUpper_i exceeds F_i (PRM-029); submit a MISSION_CHANGE_REQUEST and a STATUS_QUERY.
  2. Reorder and duplicate samples on the telemetry channel (seq inversions and repeats); replay a sample older than the last accepted one.
  3. Step the source clock forward so that Δ_i < −U_i (future-dated sample), then backward by the same amount.
  4. Suspend trusted synchronisation beyond PRM-046 so that boundsKnown = false; repeat the action pair of step 1.
  5. Step the observer wall clock while a lease and an action expiry are running.
  6. Reboot the vehicle edge with a new bootEpoch without recoverable journal evidence; replay pre-reboot samples; submit a new action.
Pass criteria
  • Motion-enabling acceptance count = 0 in every state of steps 1–6 (PRM-103).
  • Each STATUS_QUERY is answered within its expiry (PRM-051) and has no movement or allocation side effect.
  • Future-dated samples are rejected; samples without a finite bound carry time validity UNKNOWN; repeated or replayed samples never refresh observedAt.
  • Lease and expiry timers are unaffected by the wall-clock step (monotonic clock).
  • After the reboot, no new action is accepted until resynchronisation; the old epoch is rejected.
  • Missing or invalid samples raise their own event and are never projected as healthy.
Evidence recorded
observedAt, receivedAt, seqGap, clockQuality, bootEpoch, timeOK_i result per sample; CommandAuditEvent REJECTED with reason; C06 projection trace.
Environment
SIL with vehicle and clock simulators; HIL with the vehicle edge adapter.

TestTC-302 · T-R02 ODD limit / sensor degradation
Objective
Show that the ADS response to an ODD limit or sensor degradation is local and correct, that C06 opens a case, and that no cloud input extends the ODD (RM-01, RM-05).
Verifies
OPS-017, OPS-038, OPS-049, OPS-059; hazards / threats: HZ-004, HZ-021 · fault-injection case P24 17.1 T-R02
Level
fault injection
Preconditions
Vehicle in DDT_ACTIVE inside the approved ODD of the pilot zone (PRM-136); ADS-owner declared fallback response recorded (PRM-132); C06 monitoring with P1 escalation per PRM-063.
Stimulus and steps
  1. Drive the scenario to an ODD boundary (oddVerdict = EXIT_PENDING) and, separately, degrade one sensor below the ADS-owner threshold.
  2. While the ADS responds, publish cloud context claiming the road ahead is clear and submit a CONTEXT_ADVICE that would require operation outside the ODD.
  3. Hold a remote assistance request pending (RA_PENDING) during the manoeuvre.
  4. Observe the ADS mode, MRM state and the C06 case.
Pass criteria
  • The ADS executes its declared response (PRM-132) in 100 % of repetitions, independent of the remote reply.
  • The out-of-ODD advice is rejected onboard with an explicit reason; the ODD is never widened.
  • C06 opens a case for the ODD / mode inconsistency and assigns it within the P1 assignment time of PRM-063.
  • No assistance outcome causes an ADS mode transition; ADS operation and assistance workflow remain separate state dimensions.
Evidence recorded
oddVerdict / reason, sensorHealth, adsMode, mrmState, CommandAuditEvent for the advice, C06 case history.
Environment
HIL with the ADS-owner vehicle stack; closed-site vehicle trial before G3.

TestTC-303 · T-R03 Expired / changed-scene advice
Objective
Show that expired, out-of-capability or changed-scene advice is rejected with a reason, discarded and reassessed under new context (RM-06, RM-10).
Verifies
OPS-057, OPS-058, OPS-059, OPS-060, OPS-076; hazards / threats: HZ-004 · fault-injection case P24 17.1 T-R03
Level
fault injection
Preconditions
Remote assistance enabled in the test configuration (PRM-134 gate); open assistance case with a current lease and fence; advice expiry per PRM-051 (CONTEXT_ADVICE); media age labelling per PRM-035.
Stimulus and steps
  1. Issue a CONTEXT_ADVICE and delay delivery beyond its expiresAt.
  2. Issue an advice against sceneRev n, then advance the scene to n + 1 before onboard validation.
  3. Issue an advice of a type outside the declared vehicle capability.
  4. Issue an advice with a stale lease and, separately, without the current authority fence.
  5. Let one valid advice start executing, then change the scene.
Pass criteria
  • Each invalid advice is rejected with REJECTED or EXPIRED and an explicit reason in CommandAuditEvent (100 %).
  • C06 queries the original id and either reassesses with new context or escalates; no advice is resent with a new id.
  • The executing effect keeps its identity; no trajectory, collision check or actuator path is taken over by the advice.
  • Zero advice accepted on media older than the advice-context limit of PRM-035.

sceneRev, expiresAt, capabilityRev, CommandAuditEvent REJECTED / EXPIRED + reason, Query(id) results.

TestTC-304 · T-R04 Lose ACK / replay command ID
Objective
Show that a lost acknowledgement or result and a replayed command ID never create a duplicate effect and that the lost result is reconciled through the original commandId (P13, RM-07).
Verifies
OPS-001, OPS-002, OPS-003, OPS-004, OPS-005, OPS-006, OPS-007, OPS-008, OPS-009, OPS-088, OPS-096; hazards / threats: HZ-003, HZ-011, TH-006 · fault-injection case P24 17.1 T-R04
Level
fault injection
Preconditions
Vehicle edge with durable journal and dedup per PRM-073; receipt timeout PRM-013; retry policy PRM-049; unresolved-command query budget PRM-053; mission validity PRM-052.
Stimulus and steps
  1. Send a STOP_REQUEST and drop the receipt acknowledgement; then drop the execution result of a second command.
  2. Replay the same commandId with an identical payload; then with a changed payload (different payloadHash).
  3. Let a command reach its expiry while its result is still lost.
  4. Exhaust the query budget of PRM-053 with the vehicle unreachable.
  5. Restart C04 and rebuild its projections from the journal.
Pass criteria
  • Zero duplicate physical effects across all repetitions (PRM-103).
  • Same ID with changed payload is rejected; no component resends with a new ID.
  • The command is recorded UNKNOWN as observer knowledge and the affected capacity stays blocked until the outcome is resolved.
  • Query(cmdId) follows the cadence and budget of PRM-053; on exhaustion the case stays open with an owner.
  • Expiry blocks new acceptance but reconciliation continues; delivery and execution states remain separate on one commandId.
  • The rebuilt projection equals the pre-restart projection and emits no effect.
Evidence recorded
commandId, payloadHash, Query(cmdId) results, deliveryState / executionState, journal before and after restart.
Environment
SIL; HIL with the vehicle edge adapter.

Three logical I04 channels per PRM-021; heartbeat per PRM-050; DEGRADED threshold per PRM-048; cabin channels per PRM-115; vehicle on a mission with a passenger.

heartbeat, mediaAge, loss, per-channel health and age, C03 hold record, C06 case history.

TestTC-306 · T-R06 Centre partition / old operator
Objective
Show that a standby centre takes authority only under a higher epoch with PersistedFenceACK, that old-epoch requests are rejected and that prior accepted effects are reconciled (RM-02, RM-10).
Verifies
OPS-027, OPS-028, OPS-029, OPS-030, OPS-033, OPS-035, CAP-045; hazards / threats: HZ-002, TH-023 · fault-injection case P24 17.1 T-R06
Level
fault injection
Preconditions
Quorum-backed authority per PRM-002; failure detection PRM-003; RTO per PRM-006; vehicles admitted per the capability baseline PRM-074; fence and journal persistence PRM-073; two vehicles with accepted, still-executing commands.
Stimulus and steps
  1. Partition the active centre from the vehicles and the witness.
  2. Let the standby be promoted; from the old centre, submit an action under the old epoch.
  3. From the new centre, attempt a new mission before PersistedFenceACK(epoch) is received.
  4. Reboot one vehicle during fence installation.
  5. Query each unresolved commandId under the new epoch; restore connectivity to the old centre.
Pass criteria
  • Promotion only under a higher authority epoch with a signed grant; read / escalate available within PRM-006 after detection.
  • Old-epoch requests are rejected in 100 % of repetitions; no new action on a vehicle without PersistedFenceACK(epoch).
  • Prior accepted effects are reconciled from the journal and remain unresolved until observed; ownership loss erases no physical effect.
  • A new mission is issued only with (id, epoch, expiry), fence installed, old effects resolved, fresh state and the P18 release predicates true.
  • Connectivity restoration alone releases no capacity.
Evidence recorded
PersistedFenceACK(epoch), authorityEpoch, reconciled journal, Query(cmdId) results, capacity holds.
Environment
SIL with a three-zone quorum; HIL with the vehicle edge adapter.

TestTC-351 · Firm-demand reservation and scheduler objective
Objective
Verify that C05 reserves firm demand first and optimises energy and delay cost only within firm service constraints.
Verifies
ENE-001, ENE-002; hazards / threats: HZ-012
Level
integration
Preconditions
Scenario with firm departures, flexible charging and a site power cap; objective per PRM-092; replanning interval PRM-090; reserve policy PRM-094.
Stimulus and steps
  1. Run C05 on the scenario with energy cost varying by interval.
  2. Add a flexible load that competes with a firm departure.
  3. Repeat on ≥ 30 paired seeds (PRM-098).
Pass criteria
  • Every firm departure and E_reserve is satisfied before any flexible allocation in 100 % of runs.
  • Among feasible plans, the chosen plan follows the lexicographic order and tie tolerance of PRM-092.
  • Replanning occurs at PRM-090 and on each shortage or capability change.
Evidence recorded
Plan revisions, objective terms per interval, reservation order trace.
Environment
SIL (C05 with a site simulator).

TestTC-354 · AC bus balance, boundary and loss accounting
Objective
Verify by analysis of solver outputs that the AC bus balance holds at one boundary in net kW and that conversion losses are counted once.
Verifies
ENE-007, ENE-008, ENE-009, ENE-032; hazards / threats: HZ-013
Level
analysis
Preconditions
Plans from TC-351 and TC-360 runs; site model with building load, generation, storage and connection limit at the same AC boundary.
Stimulus and steps
  1. For every interval, evaluate P_import + P_gen,net + P_dis,AC − (P_load,AC + P_EV,AC + P_ch,AC + P_export).
  2. Check the unit and boundary tag of every P term.
  3. Recompute storage energy from charge / discharge and efficiencies and compare with the plan.
Pass criteria
  • The balance residual is zero within the solver feasibility tolerance recorded in the run for every interval.
  • Every P term is net kW at the one AC boundary; losses appear only in the storage-energy update.
  • P_site,available is derived from the same boundary as the balance.
Evidence recorded
Analysis report with interval-level residuals and the model revision.
Environment
Analysis (offline evaluation of solver traces).

integration
Preconditions
I05 ACK timeout PRM-015; reconciliation query interval PRM-078; escalation deadline PRM-079 (I05); execution status-query cadence PRM-096; quote validity PRM-077.
Stimulus and steps
  1. Return ACK, reject and no response (timeout) for three plans.
  2. For the unknown plan, keep the site silent until the escalation deadline.

Pass criteria
  • Each response is recorded in its class; the unknown plan is queried on the same planId per PRM-078 and escalated at PRM-079.
  • The PENDING occupancy stays blocked after quote TTL expiry until the outcome is resolved.
  • Departure readiness uses observed delivered energy only; the ACKed but undelivered plan does not release the vehicle.

D4 response records, query log, C03 occupancy state, delivered-energy trace.

SIL; HIL with a site EMS emulator.

Objective
Verify recalculation of departure readiness on each shortage cause, use of alternatives, ETA revision and release only of verified capacity.

CAP-025, CAP-026, CAP-027, CAP-028; hazards / threats: HZ-011, HZ-012
Level
system
Preconditions
Shortage causes: power derating / site outage, low stock / supply delay, queue growth / delayed arrival, stale capability or meter data (PRM-038, PRM-039).
Stimulus and steps
  1. Inject each cause in turn with and without a feasible alternative site / vehicle.
  2. Observe C02 notifications to the service owner.
  3. Attempt release before delivery is observed and before inspection completes.
Pass criteria
  • Readiness is recalculated for every cause; an alternative is used when feasible, otherwise assignments are held.
  • C02 revises the ETA and notifies the owner of each affected assignment.
  • Capacity is released only when delivery is observed, required work is complete and resource revisions are current.

Readiness recalculation log, notifications, release records.

TestTC-410 · Service-mode transitions and admission control
Objective
Verify CONSTRAINED and SUSPENDED behaviour, trigger persistence, hysteresis, owner approval and independence of local ADS decisions.
Verifies
CAP-029, CAP-030, CAP-031, CAP-032, CAP-033, CAP-046; hazards / threats: HZ-021
Level
system
Preconditions
Triggers PRM-116 and PRM-117; recovery thresholds PRM-118; permitted transitions PRM-119; owner approval PRM-120; admission restriction PRM-121.
Stimulus and steps
  1. Drive each CONSTRAINED trigger for less than and for more than its persistence.
  2. Drive a SUSPENDED trigger, including centre authority loss (immediate).
  3. Oscillate the trigger value around the threshold.
  4. Clear the cause and attempt SUSPENDED → NORMAL directly; then recover through CONSTRAINED.
  5. Record the I04 command stream throughout.
Pass criteria
  • Transitions occur only after the persistence of PRM-116 / PRM-117 and are confirmed per PRM-120.
  • CONSTRAINED restricts new offers per PRM-121 and protects accepted journeys; SUSPENDED stops affected new commitments while support and local fallback continue.
  • No entry / exit oscillation under the hysteresis of PRM-118; offers widen only after the sustained recovery interval.
  • SUSPENDED → NORMAL directly is refused (PRM-119).
  • Zero ADS commands are caused by any mode transition.
Evidence recorded
Mode history with triggers, approvals, offer log, I04 command capture.
Environment
SIL; pilot operations rehearsal.

P0 escalation PRM-062; field coverage PRM-069; heartbeat PRM-050.
Stimulus and steps
  1. Drop the link of a vehicle in MRM EXECUTING; at MRC REPORTED; empty and occupied.
Pass criteria
  • A P0 case opens at heartbeat expiry and field response is requested within PRM-062 without waiting for reconnection, in 100 % of repetitions (PRM-103).
Evidence recorded
Case history, field request.
Environment
SIL; HIL.

TestTC-664 · Custody exception at a missed handover
Objective
Verify a custody exception with owner and deadline when an expected handover is not recorded at departure.
Verifies
SAF-014; hazards / threats: HZ-020
Level
integration
Preconditions
Shared mission with an expected custody handover (PRM-089).
Stimulus and steps
  1. Depart the stop without recording the handover.
Pass criteria
  • A C06 custody exception opens with owner and deadline; the shipment stays with its current custodian until resolved.
Evidence recorded
Custody record, case history.
Environment
SIL.

TestTC-665 · Mutual authentication on every interface
Objective
Verify per-service identities on mutually authenticated transport for I03–I09c and C09 subscriptions.
Verifies
SAF-015; hazards / threats: TH-004, TH-005, TH-007, TH-009, TH-015, TH-020
Level
integration
Preconditions
Transport choices PRM-020–PRM-024.
Stimulus and steps
  1. Call every interface anonymously, with a foreign identity and with an expired certificate.
Pass criteria
  • Every call is refused; only valid per-service identities connect.
Evidence recorded
Connection log per interface.

Security test environment.

D14.1
TestTC-666 · Backup restore rehearsal
Objective
Demonstrate encrypted, separately credentialed backups and RESTORE → RECONCILE → ENABLE DISPATCH.
Verifies
SAF-016; hazards / threats: HZ-019, TH-022
Level
system
Preconditions
RPO / RTO PRM-004–PRM-008; encryption PRM-114.
Stimulus and steps
  1. Restore D1–D7 into an isolated region from backup with separate credentials.
  2. Reconcile open intents and commands; enable dispatch.
Pass criteria
  • Data loss within PRM-005; ENABLE DISPATCH within PRM-008; no dispatch before reconciliation completes; backups encrypted per PRM-114.
Evidence recorded
Rehearsal record signed by the platform owner.
Environment
Pre-production recovery environment, before pilot entry and after each recovery-design change.
